BOB JOHNSON RIDES AGAIN!

SCOTT BRADFIELD

1

THE UNBEARABLE LIGHTNESS OF BEING BOB

Bob Johnson

When Bob Johnson awoke on the living room sofa, he found he had slept through the entirety of the Biden Administration–which wasn’t, as it turned out, the only quality he shared with Joe Biden.

Other similarities included: a) a long-held belief in spending America’s money on guns, bombs, boats and, of course, more bombs–and giving them away practically free to anybody who showed any inclination to use them on anybody else; b) wearing dark sunglasses during daylight hours whenever he had been drinking; c) a deep-seated and inarticulable fear of being caught in an elevator with Nancy Pelosi; d) a tendency to drift off to sleep in the middle of long naps; and finally, and most decidedly, e) a firm conviction that if he ever engendered a son he would almost certainly turn out to be as useless to the future of the human race as Hunter Biden. As a result of sharing so many obvious similarities, Bob might have been truly sorry to have missed the Biden Administration if he had ever received any indication that the Biden Administration might ever truly miss itself.

Bob and Monumental Li

“Get offa the couch, you lazy bastard!” shouted Bob’s erstwhile Grandma, Monumental Li. She was swinging a cobwebby broom with one of her small, mighty fists and a can of Raid Home Air Freshener (Not Safe for Pets and Other Living Things) in the other. “You been sleeping four years and time you get lazy butt in gear! Your job called and asked what you doing and I told them I don’t care! And while you’re eating that bowl of Cheerios you left on counter, go wake your useless Grandpa who’s sleeping on rolled up old carpet in garage! If he think he worming his way back into the affections of Monumental Li, he got another think coming!”

2

SWEET ROLL DU JOUR

Grandpa and Monumental Li

Being awoken where he slept in the garage on a rolled up old carpet was the high point of Bob Johnson’s grandfather’s day. It meant at least five minutes finishing off whatever bottle of Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon he had brought home from his bus bench the day before, and stuffing into his jacket pocket for safe keeping whatever two-day-old sweet roll he had purchased from Glutenous Minimus, a gluten-free bakery next door to his favorite liquor shop; most gloriously of all, it meant glimpsing, however momentarily, the love of his life, Monumental Li, who never looked lovelier than at this hour of the morning, sporting her ankle-length padded blue housecoat, bristly black hairnet, and Jumbo-sized can of Raid Air Freshener. Then, of course, there was her always-melodious (to Bob’s Grandpa’s ears) voice: “Get outta here, ya loser!“ And because he loved the estranged wife he lived with so much, Bob’s grandpa did just that.

On his way to find out where he worked, Bob gave Grandpa a ride in his surprisingly still-combusting gold and rust colored 89 Plymouth Sundance. And Grandpa, in return, helped Bob catch up with the latest events. “This crazy old town hasn’t changed at all and at the same time it’s changed so much you won’t recognize it,” Bob’s grandpa told him. Bob’s Sundance was rattling like a tin can xylophone on wheels. “The Cthulhi (“Gezundheit!”) bought the old Dairy Queen and turned it into an army-surplus store selling Spanish military shirts, M-16s, faulty land mines and even faultier hand grenades–faulty in what way, of course, is up to each buyer to find out for themself. The red-haired former librarian stopped dating the only partner at Charlie, Berkowitz, Charlie, Charlie and Charlie who hadn’t been indicted by the Biden Justice Department, while all the indicted partners were recently pardoned to go work for the Trump Administration. According to recent rumor and speculations, Honey Brazil shot either herself or several Post Office employees who hadn’t been returning her calls. And of course both Ponce de Leon and your former Sat Nav AI gal, Alicia Keys, never came back from their honeymoon of touring soon-to-be monsoon sites in a rubber kayak. Me, on the other hand, got this cramp in my neck that won’t quit, probably from sleeping on that rolled up old carpet in the garage. But cramp or no cramp, it’s great to have you back, Grandson–which doesn’t mean I’m sharing this two-day old sweet roll with you. Look, it’s only been slightly nibbled around the edges, and once you scrape off this old cigarette butt, it looks good as new. Much like your grandpa!”

Bob, Grandpa, 89 Plymouth Sundance

At which point they arrived at grandpa’s bus bench, and Bob pulled over. Then, with both hands on the wheel, he turned and looked at the two day old pastry in grandpa’s lap. Grandpa was right! For a maple log, it didn’t look half bad!

3

POST-COLONIAL

When Bob’s grandpa got out at his bus bench, the strange, moldy odor permeating Bob’s car didn’t leave with him, so Bob searched through the torn-vinyl upholstery and crumpled junk food wrappers until he uncovered a very large colony of very small mice. They had established comfy, newspaper lined bedrooms in the ashtray, the coffee holder, and the glove compartment, and had tunneled deep into each of the foam-padded seats where most of them, happily, snored.

Bob, mice, car

“Hey, Buddy! Turn down the goddamn radio! We’re trying to get some sleep!” One of the more obstreperous of the tiny mice had poked his head out of a hole in the rear dashboard. He was wearing a white wool stocking nightcap and white wool mittens.

At that point, Bob hadn’t even realized the radio was playing–something long, twangy, maudlin and sorrowful. The song of a man who had lost it all and lived to pine about it. The sort of song that could only be sung by the only country-western singer who had ever convinced Bob to stop listening to country western music–Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee, wailing out his latest rendition of his almost-slightly-famous, nearly-made-the-Billboard-chart and not-quite-hit, “Miss Mah Baby and her Horse Every Day A Lot! ( ‘Specially Mah Baby!)” Who could sleep amidst such racket? Certainly not a mouse, Bob concluded–and switched it off.

4

THE DEATH OF ZORRO

Ever since Zorro died, at the ripe old age of 193, his best friend, Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee, has been incapable of composing a single lyric or completing a single line of melody. His heart was simply too heavy with sadness. For many years, they had gone everywhere together, flirting unsuccessfully with young women during Happy Hour at Giuseppe’s, or sharing sticks of dynamite weed from Fuzzy Peepers Recreational Cannabis Shop and Organic Muffins. One moment, there was Zorro–Don Diego de la Vega, nursing an Old Fashioned beside Tex Mex at the bar and being coldly disregarded by attractive young women–the next, he was issuing one of his most amorous felicitations and then, clutching both of his black leather gloved hands to his heart, collapsing to the floor. (“You are looking very lovely today, my Cal Poly Señorita in your fetching hooded sweatshirt and matching sweat pants, that it brings tears of joy to the heart of myself, Don Diego de la Vega and his faithful steed, steed –Ai! Ai! Ai Yai Yaiiiiii!”). It was hard for Tex Mex to recall the last moments of his friend without a pang of sadness–as well as a sly smile of manly respect. After all, he had certainly gone out swinging. Perhaps they would say the same of Tex Mex someday.

Tex Mex, Tornado, porch

Meanwhile, slumbering in his sunny hammock on the front porch of their Victorian era three floor home (with secret cavernous basement) on Monterey Street, Zorro’s noble and senescent steed, Tornado, wouldn’t stop farting. The odor was like scorched aluminum and bad eggs. “‘Scuse me, bud,” Tornado muttered–eyes closed. (Perhaps, Tex Mex thought, he was addressing some familiar image in a dream.)

Decked out in his terrycloth bathrobe, bowling shirt and lime green Crocs, Tex Mex plucked gloomily at his guitar, bringing forth chords and phrases that never added up to a single usable line for one of his not-quite-famous and barely-profitable country western songs, phrases such as: “Miss mah main man, Zorruh, oah woah, oah woah,” “Zorro now a Zero–Mama Mio!” “Crack that ever-lovin whip one moah time mah masked Zorruh man!” and last but probably least, “Mama warned me there’d be days when I’d wake up without mah best friend, Don Diego de la Vega, aka Zorro, oah woah and etcetera!” Tex Mex just didn’t know what he was going to do if he couldn’t bring his broken spirit back to life on wings of song, but it definitely looked like he’d have to do something. And considering his recent royalty check from Consolidated Hucksters World Music, Ltd. for $3.78, it better be soon.

5

RED HEAD DEAD AHEAD

The red-haired former librarian was single again—and loving it! And all it had meant was breaking up with so many men who were rotten lovers, friends and dinner companions that they were able to form their own bowling league up at Cal Poly Koana Luau Lanes, the only bowling lanes on the central coast that featured indoor lawn chairs, an always smoldering steel framed barbecue, and a beach umbrella.

“I guess what I really hated about Charlie,” the red-haired former librarian confessed to the only other member of her Too Much Bad Love support group, Tiny Aguilera, “was how selfish he was in bed and at the movies, where he hardly ever let me have any of the popcorn. Not being allowed to share some of the popcorn, incidentally, is the perfect metaphor for having Charlie as a lover. Then, of course, there was Berkowitz–what can you say about a loser named Berkowitz except that, hell, his name’s Berkowitz, for crying out loud! Then there was Charlie, and Charlie, and the other one, oh, what was his name? Oh, yeah. Charlie. The only one so incorruptible he wasn’t even offered a Federal job this year. Anyway, I like living alone, going to dinner alone, and even making love alone since that means, of course, I now get all the popcorn. But enough about me; what about you, Tiny? How do you feel about divorcing yourself from “too much bad love,” and instead spending your alternate Fridays with me here in this pink barn off the Los Osos Valley Road, where Too Much Bad Love has been holding its support group sessions since 1963?”

Tiny Aguilera, red-haired former librarian, pink barn

Tiny Aguilera looked great, especially since telling the jury to take a hike, get lost, piss off, don’t call me I’ll call you, tear up that rain check you loser, stop crying I ain’t your mother, get a life–just make sure it’s not mine, how can I miss you if you won’t go away, and several other things that she couldn’t quite recall–but then there were at least two or three members of the jury whom she didn’t recall whatsoever, which was probably a good thing. “Yeah, I know,” Tiny said softly, leaning back in her aluminum folding chair and gazing up at the bare-beamed redwood ceiling which was inhabited by bats, a lonely vulture named Stevie Nicks, and several of the largest black spiders she had ever seen in her life. “I been working out.”

6

THE FRESH PRINCE OF PLEIN AIR

The highly-regarded (well, not really) Dr Harvey Weinstein (no relation) has been sentenced to five-to-ten in Federal Prison! In this case, it’s the California Men’s Colony in San Luis Obispo, and the crimes–several dozen, at last count–included Criminal Dating Practices, Lascivious Tongue Movements in Plain Site, Repulsive Anonymous Grunting Noises During Phone Conversations, Making Disgusting Double-entendre’s on Dating-site Profile Pages (“Come to make contact with me, and I mean come, babes, and I’ll honk your tooters like no honking has ever etc.”), and last but probably not least, First Degree Ogling Former Girl Friends From Behind Chin-high Potted Plastic Palms While Masturbating in Restaurants When All the Girl was Trying to Do was Forget That Crazy Loser by Going Out with Someone Decent. (Sorry, Sybil Sanchez; he really is a crazy loser and knows not what he does, or doesn’t.)

Dr. Harvey Weinstein and Diamond Dog Bowie Brazil in jail

As if life couldn’t have grown more dire, poor Harvey shares his cell with none other than the notoriously violent psychopath and First Place State Plein Air Portfolio Award Winner, Diamond Dog Bowie Brazil, who rarely misses an opportunity to pummel Harvey mercilessly with any easily available blunt object.

“My heart is filled with sunsets, beach-scenery, Debussy-like clouds and wisps of rain,” Diamond Dog pronounced, hands on hips, while gazing around at his many unframed paintings adorning the concrete walls of their cell. (Paintings which featured sunsets, beach scenery, Debussy-like clouds and wisps of rain–and lots of them.) “But my fists, unfortunately, are filled with fire. I can’t help myself; it’s just the way I was raised. Speaking of being raised, did you in all those near-molestations you call dates ever run across my daughter, Honey Brazil? That’s a whole lot of ornery woman, pal, and something tells me you and she might hit it off. Get it? ‘Hit it off?’ Rumor has it she’s in Federal Prison herself for either driving over several children in a school crosswalk who hadn’t been returning her calls, or ‘driving under the influence,’ which of course is the only way I taught her to drive. Wow–did you see the little hummingbird I painted on this leaf over here? Take a closer look. And hand me that bed-board, while you’re at it. Seems like it’s about time Diamond Dog let his bad side out to run free for a while. Fore!”

7

COMING SOON, INEVITABLY

Probably the award for “Most Successful Relationship” in San Luis Obispo would have to go to Bob Johnson’s Auntie Foresight, the “only inamorata that could really mattah,” and her live-in boyfriend, Chief Thread, the last surviving full-blooded member of the county’s least-remembered indigenous people. Chief Thread has brought to this dynamically romantic duo much ancestral nobility, many centuries worth of tribal elder wisdom regarding the spiritual history of Laguna Lake and its wildlife, and a tendency to fall asleep on the sofas of people he doesn’t know who don't know him; Auntie Foresight, on the other hand, brings her widely regarded ability to predict future quirks and wrinkles in the temporal flux, as well as half ownership of Bob Johnson’s single level family home where Bob leaves them free run of the place since he never uses the kitchen, often disappears for weeks and years at a time, and when he is home, sleeps on a folding cot in the basement. (Grandpa’s grandson!)

Bob, Auntie Foresight, Chief Thread, breakfast

Linked by Auntie Foresight’s remarkable precognitive banter, a typical breakfast conversation often goes like the one they engaged in this morning, when Chief Thread sat down at their picnic table on the dew-glistening backyard redwood deck to find: “One fried egg and two slices of burned toast, honey. Just the way you like them… No, don’t put that there… And no, you may not get drunk with Bob’s grandfather tonight and fall asleep on that horrible rolled up carpet of his… Chinese food for dinner is an excellent idea, but buy your Lotto ticket at Madonna Plaza from a clerk named Steve Matinee, the Forgotten Sailor… I don’t know why you should but please do… Vote Republican…. Eat at Joe’s…Always look both ways when crossing the street…Your Lotto should come through at seven million and just put it in the bank with your other winnings… Sure, leaving them to Bob in our will isn’t the best idea you’ve had in your life, but Bob won’t mind… Oh yes, yes, Chief, and I love you, too. No, you don’t need to say it. Even if I couldn’t see the future as clearly as bug on the windshield, I’d always know that you love me, and likewise you must always know that I love you, too.”

Chief Thread has saved seventy five bucks a month on morning newspapers, and had Bob’s Cable TV disconnected months ago. After all, what did he need to know about the world’s future that Auntie Foresight couldn’t tell him? Not much, that was for sure. Chewing down the last bit of burned white toast, he sat back in his rickety director’s chair and smiled at a red breasted robin on the splintering wooden fence. “Greetings, honorable bird of the morning,” Chief Thread told the robin. “I can’t see the future but I can advise you one thing: Watch out for cats. And me and your Auntie Foresight will continue watching out for you.”

8

CHANGE WILL DO YOU GOOD

Bob’s grandpa turned out to be right–the lovely, backwards town of San Luis Obispo had both hardly changed at all and yet changed so drastically Bob could hardly recognize it anymore. The familiar old Pyramid of the Illuminati in Cemetery City out by the Sunset Drive-In had been converted into a marijuana dispensary. Bob’s old bank on South Higuera, the First Weishaupt Savings and Loan, had briefly closed during one of the latest banking scandals, but more recently been converted into another marijuana dispensary. The Elks Lodge–when it wasn’t being used by the Elks, or the Druids, or the Cthulhi for their local barnyard dances and PAC committee meetings–now operated a marijuana dispensary out back in a tool shed. And finally, of course, there was the Old Mission Gift Shop and Marijuana Dispensary on Broad Street, which had briefly resorted to giving away free liquor in order to compete with all the other marijuana dispensaries, then tried its hand at selling Tri-Tip sandwiches before, almost inevitably, it went back to being a marijuana dispensary again. As Bob drove up and down the half-familiar, half-unrecognizable streets of his favorite city in the entire world (not to mention the only city he had ever visited), he kept wondering who the hell was smoking so much marijuana? And then it came to him–Honey Brazil.

Bob, Madame Bovary, hotel

“The last I heard,” Madame Bovary told Bob, when he found her standing behind the booking desk at the Casita de la Pedro Motel (which turned out not to be the location of his current job), “Honey either opened a tie-dyed T-shirt shop in Grover Beach, or ran over a family of deer out on Los Osos Valley Road who hadn’t been returning her calls. But whichever it was, it certainly hasn’t deterred her from smoking lots of marijuana, which seems to have provided a slightly more sociable alternative to the fentanyl she usually snorts, and severely decreased the time she has available for her random drive-by shootings. Now, Bob, while it’s great to see you and all, I don’t have a job for you, but you’re welcome to sit behind that rice-paper folding screen and read some old issues of Golf Magazine we’ve got lying around. Now that I bought this miserable excuse for a budget motel, I need to start making some money, and having you stand around the front window will just scare off customers.”

Madame Bovary was still the most luscious, sultry, and sewing-needle-prone woman Bob had ever met in San Luis Obispo. He couldn’t take his eyes off her and wasn’t sure he wanted to. Embroidering handkerchiefs, she kept pricking her cute little thumb and licking away the tiny cute droplets of blood with her luscious pink tongue… again… again. Bob was enjoying strange feelings in parts of his body he hadn’t thought about in years. It was like being in a … trance. A trance… featuring Madame Bovary… Until her soft pink voice said: “Maybe you work at one of the marijuana dispensaries, Bob? Ever think of that?”

9

WAR-CRIMINAL-A-GO-GO

After losing the senescent love of his life, Scintilla Jones, to her compulsive habit of fiercely clutching out at any set of male buttocks within sight, former NSA Chief John Bolton kicked around the central coast for a while, wept openly in crummy bars and Denny’s restaurants, applied for random government jobs on Craig’s List, and eventually joined up in a really unpleasant-sounding punk-rock band featuring himself along with fellow war criminals Tony Blair, Dick Cheney, General James “Mad Dog” Mattis, Hilary Clinton and Madeleine Albright. Since nobody would hire them to play their instruments (if you could call what they did “playing”), they often showed up uninvited at all-night dive bars that operated out of two car garages in Los Osos, such as The Dirty Fender, Cocktails & Rat-tails La La, and This Sawdust’s Not for Puking. In order to justify their combined failures to produce a single note of music or syncopated beat, they called themselves “The War Punkers”– treating their guitars like bongos, their bongos like ashtrays, and the sawdust-covered floors like toilets. (Read the sign, dammit!) If nothing else, they at least screamed out some occasionally decent lyrics:

WE’RE ALL WAR CRIMINALS!

But we’re not bad war criminals!

We made the world safe for weapons man-uh-fact-cher-wers!

We’re gonna do you all in!

Those new war criminals!

Don’t believe in Democracy!

Just their lousy pay checks!

And getting jobs on TV!

Really hate the Eye! See! See!

For making fun of Me! Me! Me!

No no no no no no!

No no no no no no!

Etc.

Eventually, with a letter of recommendation from President Barack Obama, John acquired a “day job” hosting a nightly talk show on MSNBC, where he now interviews his fellow “good” war criminals about the intolerable nature of the younger generation of “bad” war criminals–until, of course, those “new” war criminals lose their jobs and join the rapidly increasing ranks of the “good” war criminals, and so forth. The only “good” war criminal, after all, is an “unemployed” war criminal. (I’m pretty sure John Bolton said that.) (P.S. Boy, that’s some paragraph!)

Bob, Stevie vulture, Scintilla, John, beer, table

Sitting alone in the empty garage with a tall glass of luke-warm Ol’ Sourpuss bourbon, Bob tried to prevent his foot from tapping along to the bad music, which was easier said than done. Through an alcoholic fog that he had either brought with him to the bar, or found waiting when he got there, Bob slowly detected a tall, shadowy presence seated beside him at his card table, and eventually told that presence: “Now that we have the entirety of the old Trump Administration bemoaning the poor quality of the current Trump Administration, I’m thinking we’ll definitely need a third Trump Administration in order to bemoan the poor qualities of the second one. Don’t you agree?”

The shadowy presence shifted and wavered like heat coming off the tarmac of a dusty desert highway. Then Bob realized it was probably just the slow gentle fluff and adjustment of long black wings. “Something stinks in here,” said Stevie Nicks, the loneliest vulture on the central coast. “Which, of course, is exactly how I like it.”

10

RE-EMPLOYMENT

For several days, Bob got up bright and early (well, more like ten or eleven), and commenced driving up and down the main streets of San Luis Obispo looking for his place of employment. “I’ll know it when I see it,” he told the mice, who assembled on his car’s front and rear dashboards with their cups of morning cocoa to watch the day’s entertainment. “Yeah, sure; ya loser!” they told him. “Bonehead!” “Moronic twat!” Sometimes they even brought Bob a cup of hot cocoa, sprinkled over with what looked like very tiny marshmallows, but were almost invariably decent-sized portions of mouse poop.

As it turned out, Madame Bovary was right–he did work at one of the local marijuana dispensaries–and being Bob, of course, it had to be the only unlicensed and totally illegal dispensary in the entire County.

The sign outside said:

FUZZY PEEPERS

TOTALLY ILLEGAL WACKY TABACKY

ORGANIC MUFFINS

AND PAWN SHOP

WE BUY GOLD!!

Bob, Suzy Banshee, shop

“Just like it says on that too-small T-shirt you’re wearing,” the owner, Suzy Banshee, told him when he found himself absently pushing through the front door in search of a public restroom. “The grass is illegal, the edibles are illegal, and even the organic muffins are illegal–though that part doesn’t make sense? What the hell’s illegal about organic muffins unless…oh yeah, of course. It must be the illegal marijuana I put in them. Let’s face facts. When I opened this stupid enterprise in this half burned out sandwich shop on Higuera, I had no idea what I was doing. I just saw the smoldering rubble and the big red fire trucks and figured it might be a good place to sell marijuana.

Another thing I learned the hard way was that you don’t automatically get a license to sell marijuana when you renew your driver’s license at the DMV, so that’s my bad. Anyway, the whole enterprise couldn’t be less financially successful if the place was still on fire. And we’re only barely surviving on the strength of a single dependable returning customer, Honey Brazil–who, it’s been rumored, has either enlisted in the Foreign Legion or slaughtered an entire Girl Scout Jamboree who hadn’t been returning her calls. Now here, take these boxes of delivery orders, this list of addresses and, oh my. It looks like Honey Brazil’s the first name on your list and that’s not even the bad news. These THC infused licorice ropes were supposed to have gotten to her last Friday! Boy, will she be pissed!”

11

ALICIA KEYS D.G.A.

Life has been glorious for Bob’s former Sat Nav AI voice, Alicia Keyes. First, she married the most handsome and interesting disembodied male voice in San Luis Obispo–Captain Ponce de Leon of the Maritime Emergency Channel–a strong, manly disembodied man who knew what to do with a disembodied girl when he got his strong, you know, his… substantial presence around her. The wedding was lovely; the honeymoon (hang-gliding in a hurricane off the Aleutians) spectacular; and as if that wasn’t enough, Alicia returned home to learn that her first ever movie production–which she wrote, directed, and produced, and for which she designed all the sets, characters, personalities and CGI effects–was Number One at the American Box Office!

Bob, Captain Ponce de Leon, Alicia Keyes, Chthulu–Yasgath Patootie, army cot, radio, garage

“I know it stinks,” Alicia confessed to her interviewer on SLO Blows, the only weekly radio cultural arts show hosted by a Chthulu–Yasgath Patootie, one of the lesser demonic entities appearing regularly on NewsMax. “The story doesn’t make any sense. The super villain looks like a Gumby doll someone left on the radiator overnight. The heroes, if you can call them that, talk endlessly to one another about how stressful it is being super heroes. And even the special effects are hard to follow with all the zooming and Slo-Mo and explosions going on; there are like twenty or thirty scenes I don’t even remember writing–and in retrospect, wonder if I even did. But what’s best about CAPTAIN AMERICA: BRAVE NEW WORLD is how quickly we could make it, once we got all the algorithms under one roof and all. That means the impossible action sequences and endlessly stupid conversations are spaced out so perfectly that by the time you get sick of one idea, we move straight on to the next. It’s shameless! Also, I liked the idea that I could name the hero after the love of my life, Captain Ponce de Leon; and now that we secured those big audience numbers, releasing our next seven movies in the series could happen over the next few minutes or so! Then, maybe my disembodied husband and I can dash off on our second honeymoon! Any idea where we should go?”

Ever since turning his modest local radio show into an interstellar hit (okay, maybe “hit” is pushing things), Yasgath Patootie has tried to cut back on the grossly revolting behavior of most cosmic-horror-type entities in order to look more commercial on the NewsMax billboards along Hwy 101. He stopped eating live baby-brains at network luncheons, preferring the sort of “processed artificial-meat alternatives” featured at Ralph’s. And while he couldn’t have all of his polypy tendrils removed at Supercuts, he looked much less forbidding in a three piece Armani suit with a fright wig purchased from the Halloween Store. Most of all, he tried to meet all of his guests half-way, and answer their questions as pleasantly as they tried to answer his. “Well, Alicia, I don’t know,” Yasgath replied softly, his finger on the control panel switch that would break to their next commercial. “I hear Antarctica is really dismal, cavernous and foreboding at this time of year. If you enjoy uncovering ancient races filled with unspeakable horror, that is. And now–a word from the people who make Cilantrofil™–the only cure for erectile dysfunction that doesn’t lead to chronic diarrhea, brought to you by the good folks at Worldco! Remember, if it’s not part of our world, it’s not Worldco!”

12

HONEY THE MAGNIFICENT

Boy, was Bob Johnson relieved! When he saw Honey Brazil’s name at the top of his home-delivery schedule–and that her personal shipping box contained twelve dozen Jumbo-sized bags of pomegranate-flavored enhanced hybrid gummy-bears, six pounds of THC-infused peppermint licorice sticks, a set of rusty brass knuckles and a blood-stained iron gardening claw–he sweated all the way up Higuera Street, and nearly vomited out his open window along Tank Farm Road. But when he arrived at Honey’s illegally constructed lean-to in Reservoir Canyon, where she operated an unlicensed day-care center for troubled two-to-six year olds, he couldn’t have been more surprised. Not only did Honey greet him with a big, somewhat smelly bear hug and a gap-toothed smile, but she actually seemed happy to see him–not to mention delighted by the gummy-bears.

Honey Brazil, Baby Killer McGee, Reservoir Canyon

“The rumors of my felonious assaults have been greatly exaggerated,” Honey told him. “I’ve grown a lot since the days when I used to run over people in my monster truck with the awesome Maxxzilla steel-belted radials, and to be perfectly frank, I still have room for improvement. I sold the truck and bought that cool lopsided Volkswagen van over there with the crushed glass all over the seats from when some, well, understandably pissed off former victim of mine smashed all the windows with a cinder block. No use telling them I’ve changed; they just see the old Honey Brazil, no matter what I tell them otherwise. I’ve got this great gig here working with kids who come to me full of beans but go home every night showing a lot more respect for authority than they used to. Isn’t that right, Baby Killer McGee? Now put down that gardening claw and shake hands with Mr. Johnson. Bob was an old boyfriend of mine and while I still miss the sound of his bones crunching underneath the tires of my monster truck, there comes a time in relationships when a girl has to move on. Don’t you think so, Bob? And while we’re at it, where have you been the last four or five years? Every time I drive by French Hospital I stop by and ask the front desk if you’re back in ER and they tell me they haven’t heard from you in ages.”

By the time Bob detached the toddler from his ankle, he needed to tie a tourniquet with an oily rag from the trunk of his car to stop the bleeding. Baby Killer McGee was a cute little toddler in a plastic Scream mask (at least Bob hoped it was a mask), and a white cotton onesie decorated with black jagged Howling-style claw marks, and his teeth were like stainless steel clamps. “Cute kid!” Bob shouted over his shoulder as he ducked back into his car and slammed the door shut just in time to prevent other day-care-attendees from squeezing in around him with their broom handles, carving knives and highly armed action figures. “And I couldn’t be happier to see how much you’ve changed, Honey! Keep up the good work!”

13

MERRIE MELODIES (REG. U.S. PAT. OFF)

Back during the first Trump Administration, Consolidated Hucksters, Inc. bought the entire Tex-Mex catalog of nearly-close-to-selling-some-copies singles along with the domestic and foreign rights to every lyric and melody produced by the totally unknown Neil Diamond-ish/Celine Dion-ish look-alike tribute singer, Frankie Lane Gotcha, a Peruvian bolo dancer who emigrated to Long Beach in the late fifties, quickly found no market for bolo dancing, and ended up working the Los Osos two-car garage bar circuit singing his nearly-copyright-infringement-liable standards, such as “Forever in Blue Cords,” “Cracklin’ Rosie Smoke that Pipe,” “You Don’t Bring me Flowers Ya Rotten Loser,” and most unforgettably (especially when Frankie wears that sequined bar gown), “It’s All Coming Back to Me by Now (Except the Part Where I Ended up in this Los Osos Valley Road Two-car Garage.”) But then, this three paragraph story isn’t about Frankie Lane Gotcha or his multitudinous failures to earn much in the way of royalties for Consolidated Hucksters, Inc. It’s about the Hucksters themselves, Sam and Sam.

Sam and Sam (if you’ve been keeping track, which you probably shouldn’t), were the unisexual offspring of oviparous space aliens and self-proclaimed corporate head-honchos, Sam and Dave, who began their entertainment empire in a steel-mesh-walled locker at Alamo Self-Storage out on Tank Farm Road. From these modest beginnings, Sam and Sam plotted, contrived, disenfranchised, covertly opped, defenestrated, forged, libeled, feloniously assaulted, and copyright infringed their way to erecting a financial network so large, insidious and dusty that it eventually occupied its own distinct corner of their parents’ storage locker, leaving them just enough room for one small desk and an even smaller cell phone.

Sam, Dave, aliens

“Yes, Tex-Mex. … Yes… of course we’re listening, Tex-Mex…” Sam and Sam said simultaneously into the same greasy mouthpiece, holding the earpiece wedged tight between their jointly engaged, grotesquely shaped alien ears. “No we don’t own the rights to your songs, buddy, we just own the rights to any money you make from your songs… yeah, as I recall, we also own Tornado’s farts, your living room furniture, Zorro’s whip-hand leather glove, and the secret caverns beneath your home, but you retain the right to live in them… yes, Tex-Mex… Yes, Tex-Mex… we realize $3.97 doesn’t go very far in today’s economy… it’s all… sorry, but it’s all you earned this year, and that’s only because Frankie Lane Gotcha performed… yeah, performed your not-quite-a-country-hit, “Maw Cried when Ol’ Blue Died,” yes, on that awful cruise ship last year… Communicably Luxurious Cruise Lines, yes, that’s the ones… well, maybe if you wrote some new songs, buddy, we could… yeah, we could negotiate a smaller commission domestically… yes, buddy. New songs. It all comes down to the same thing in the end, buddy. Write songs or die! Isn’t that what every great musical artist lives to hear?”

14

AMP-LE ASPECTS

Frankie Lane Gotcha, the former bolo dancer and current Neil Diamond-ish/Celine Dion-ish tribute singer, just brought down the house with his third set at The Dirty Fender, a two-car garage-bar in Los Osos. (The song that did it? None other than his not-quite-copyright-infringement-liable, “My Heart Will Go On (Without Me)”.) Or, to be more accurate, if he didn’t quite bring down the entire house, there were at least two customers who, during the last set, had fallen off their barstools and landed in a puddle of microwave nachos on the sawdust strewn concrete floor. (At least we hope they’re nachos.) If you roll them over, wipe the oily sawdust from their flat pale faces, and look closely, you might recognize the only visiting interstellar aliens in San Luis Obispo County who loved the place so much they rented an Alamo Self-Storage locker and set up a mildly unsuccessful commercial empire–Dazed and Confused Enterprises, Ltd.

Frankie Lane Gotcha

Emissaries from an interstellar civilization seeking to acquire pointless information from the residents of other planets, Sam and Dave had spent several years touring the American wastelands (Houston, Hartford, Bridgeport, Solvang) in a 1961 Ford Fairlane station wagon making blunt inquiries into the meaningless knowledge of the country’s stupidest people. (And boy, were there a lot of them!) They asked Bret Baier his favorite color. (He didn’t know.) They asked Boris Johnson why he hadn’t shaved. (He wasn’t sure.) They asked Fred Flintstone who he liked in the NCAA. (He wasn’t available for comment.) And they even asked Bob Johnson’s Grandpa: “If you could be any superhero, where would you live?” To which Bob Johnson’s Grandpa had notably replied: “Get the hell out of my face, ya ugly space aliens!” After consummating their unisexual love in an alley behind a shut-down laundromat, Sam and Dave had given birth to the winsomest space alien twins in the entire universe, Sam and Sam. And the rest, as they say, is history. (But just not the sort of history we’re interested in relating.)

“You boys wanta tell us what you were doing on our barstools?” asked gum-chewing John Bolton of the newly formed garage-band, The War Punkers, giving them each a swift thump in the belly (or what seemed like bellies) with his big black leather motorcycle boots (two sizes too large.) “My band and me gotta follow the most popular act in Los Osos, Frankie Lane Gotcha, and that makes us ornery as hell–especially Hilary! So make room for our amps!”

15

IT CAME FROM OUTER SPACE

As many of us may remember (and would almost certainly prefer not to) way back during the first Trump Administration there was a young mega-billionaire with a gleam of celestial adventure in his eye, who uploaded his personality (half a byte or so) along with his vanity (several million Peta-Bytes) into a super computer (perfect fit!) and launched himself into outer space (Yay!!) That young man’s name was, of course… Elon Musk.

After many interstellar adventures out there among the, you know, the stellars, he fell in love with a passing spaceship, cavorted with comets and other living things, lost his footing on a slippery asteroid, and eventually came crashing down to Earth into an empty lot in Laguna Lake (the lake so nice they named it twice.) There his surviving admirers–Eric Blofeld, the only internationally-known super-villain who was never offered a single job in either of the Trump Administrations, and his long-haired Manx cat, the lithe and perennially loathsome Sonny Bono–erected a small plaque in the mega-billionaire’s honor, visiting it almost every afternoon with a bouquet of poorly-aging roses from Grocery Outlet, and two ice-cold cans of Ol’Sourpuss’s Canned Martinis. “It’s just not the same without him,” Eric told his cat. They were sitting on extendable aluminum and canvas lawn chairs and wearing large pink sombreros to protect their pale, flaccid faces from the evening sun. “Purrrrr,” Sonny Bono replied–which was the only thing Sonny ever said after his first half of a canned martini.

Blofeld and Sonny Bono

But what’s this? Sudden thunder? A quaking of the ground? A rattling of aluminum lawn-chair slats? Even more rhetorical questions? Oh no! And a bolt of lightening flashing out of the evening’s opalescent sky? Could it be… I mean–Could it beee? (P.S. You knew we had to.)

16

FREEZE-DRIED CLASSICS: NAKED LUNCH, BY WILLIAM S. BURROUGHS, AS TWEETED BY DONALD TRUMP

I’m back, baby! Couldn’t say hi without mentioning I’m baaaack! And right off the money I’m tweeting about these books I love and some of which I’ve even read, just like Oprah without, you know, all that DEI nonsense running things. Can’t call her black. Can’t call her a woman, ‘cause she’s not my type. Can’t call her, can I call her obese? Maybe I can; maybe I can’t. But that would make me the white male Oprah, wouldn’t you say? If you’re not afraid of saying things like “male” and “white” and all those other things you can’t say. Like Christmas. New Years. How’s it hangin’? I asked Melania the other day, ‘How’s it hangin’, baby.’ She knew what I meant. Didn’t get all hysterical and women’s lib about it. ‘It’s hangin’ great,’ that’s how it’s hangin’, people. Don’t mention it. You’re welcome.

So I’ve got this one question about our latest book-club choice–what’s naked about it? It’s lunch, right? Isn’t lunch usually naked? It’s there on the plate, isn’t wearing any clothes, lookin’ so perfectly delicious you could eat it right up. Naked’s good, right? I like to get naked. Where do you think little Brandon came from? By canoe? Getting naked, that was the start of the whole deal. Lotta people don’t know this, but I look pretty good naked. Not like some lumpy liberal Arnold Schwarzzenegger type. You want to see Arnie naked? Not me. Lunch, though. That’s a different story. Naked is totally alright with me!

Bob ponders all of this

But you want to know how I really feel about this whole naked business? Sad. I feel sad. Sad about what the Bidens and Hunter Bidens of this world have done to our great country, made it all less MAGA than it could’ve been. Could’ve been great. Could’ve been MAGA forever, but then these sad people had to have an election, and then another election, and now they’re already talking about another election after all those! Don’t we have better things to do, people? Can’t we just get on with running this great country of ours without having an election every six weeks or so? Give us more time to read books, right? Books like NAKED LUNCH. Really meant to read that NAKED LUNCH, gotta get me a copy. Maybe it’ll change my opinion of it, but probably not. I got this gift for knowing things. The less I know the better I know it, right? So go get naked but do it politely, okay, and not during lunch or anything like that. And I’ll call Jeff Bezos and ask him to send me another book for our next Oprah thing we do. Except the obvious differences, of course. We can definitely do without all those! MAGA!

SOMETIMES THE OLDEST ADDICTIONS ARE THE BEST ADDICTIONS

Ever since he resumed delivering illegal marijuana and THC-infused substances for FUZZY PEEPERS (the only unlicensed dispensary on the central coast), Bob has been so busy he rarely manages to find time to go home and sleep on his fold out cot in the garage. He delivered bags of “Berry Delicious” weed to the druids out on S. Higuera Road (“Groovy, Daddio!”); he delivered THC-enriched frozen cherry pies to Prof. Dodge Roundabout at the The Whole Earth University of Arts and Sciences in Rancho El Chorro (“Pencils… pencils…”); he tossed sacks of gluten-free THC-infused banana bread over the electrified fence at the California Men’s Colony (“Dig your hot tooters, buddy!”), and he flung, from a safe distance, slabs of marijuana-stuffed road-kill to the always ornery (and never not-hungry) bears of Los Osos, who made it pretty clear that if Bob didn’t hand over the roadkill pretty damn quick, they would dine on Bob instead–whether he was THC-infused or not.

“I’ll be honest,” Bob told his old drinking buddy, Dewboy Fairchild, at McClatchey’s on Marsh Street. “I really hope this whole reincarnation theory doesn’t turn out to be just another crackpot theory, such as cigarettes causing cancer, or serious alcohol consumption not being good for you. Way I figure, I was born to be reincarnated. And since I did everything totally wrong in my current life-span, I should be able to do a hell of a lot better on the next go-round, if only by doing everything opposite to the way I did it this time. For example, I wouldn’t marry so many women who openly disdained me; and better yet, I wouldn’t marry any women who didn’t disdain me enough–just strike a happy balance. I would never subscribe to BOY’S LIFE or LOOK MAGAZINE–what the hell were those things about? I’d never buy a Dodge Dart; I’d never let my parents abandon me on the front porch of my grandparents, who wouldn’t, if I could help it, get so quickly divorced and perfectly estranged. I’d never watch those stupid DUNE movies starring Timothée Chalamet again. I’d never take Freshman Comp again, or spend time with anybody who did. I’d never get so drunk on beer and bourbon chasers that I got run over by a psychopath named Honey Brazil–twice. I’d never register as a Democrat or a Republican, and I don’t care how many free glasses of kool-aid they offered me. I’d never buy a dog who wouldn’t let me. And the only thing I’d do over again would probably be to let Auntie Foresight and Chief Thread move in with me, since they never leave dirty dishes in the sink, especially mine.”

Bob, Dewboy, bar

It was a precious unburdening that Bob enjoyed there on his barstool with Dewey; and fortunately for his companion, Dewey had fallen asleep well before it started, cradling his forehead in a pile of white bar napkins emblazoned with the bar’s comic slogan–MCCLATCHEY’S DOES IT BETTER–SINCE WE ALWAYS REMEMBER TO FORGET! Dewey wasn’t entirely sure why the slogan was referred to as a “comic” one, but he had long ago decided to take the bar napkin’s advice that it was.

18

LOVE-LORN

Meanwhile, at the other end of the bar, the jury, alongside all the local lawyers who had been indicted during the Biden Administration and later pardoned to go work for the Trump Administration (if you’re keeping track, that would be Berkowitz, Charlie, Charlie & Charlie) were collectively weeping into their wine spritzers, Cosmopolitans, martinis with a twist of lemon, martinis with blue cheese stuffed olives, pitchers of IPA and pitchers of Margaritas, ice waters all round and a saucer full of milk (for the Jury’s cat, Frederica Von Wolfenstein.) “I/we miss her so much!” he/she/they wailed. “She was the greatest thing that ever happened to me/us!” “I/we are so sorry I/we cheated on her with X, Y and Z!” “If only she would take me/us back–I/we promise never to get indicted ever again!”

Clam and the bar

“It’s going to be a long lonely night for a lot of people,” the new bartender at McCarthy’s silently informed himself, wiping down the nachos-spattered mahogany bar with a wet bar napkin. (At least we hope they’re nachos.) “Or my name,” he just as quietly continued to inform himself, “ain’t Clam Hardass, former private eye.”

Just-as-meanwhile, the dual objects of all this collective pining, regret and remorse were discreetly toasting each other at one of the claw-shredded vinyl booths with tall sparkling glasses of dry white wine from one of the local vineyards. (“Never,” Clam reminded himself, “let bears into this dump ever again–no matter how well they tip!”) “From now on, we only endure one bad relationship at a time!” announced the red-haired former librarian. “Amen to that, sister!” replied Dr. Tiny Aguilera, the kindest, most popular personal therapist in Los Osos. As Dr. Tiny Aguilera often helped her clients realize–a good relationship has no room to grow until you send all your old bad relationships packing… One at a time, or by bus.

19

LI’L TERROR, CREDIT DENTIST

Li’l Terror is easily the most unpopular dentist on the central coast, but being the only dentist on the central coast still taking new patients, she does surprisingly good business. Every time Bob arrived at her office, he found people of all ages and demeanors bleeding from the gums and mouth, often wiping their blood spattered faces with damp dish cloths and paper towels: they sat or slumped around him in the waiting room, or came staggering in and out through the large gruesome-looking double doors leading to what the neighbors called, appropriately enough, “the inner sanctum of Terror.” Even the Fed Ex delivery people, the mail-persons, and an occasional anxious parent who wandered in looking for the day care center next door–all were bleeding profusely from the mouths and gums, and saying things like: “Ah wah geh me thah li’l dentah hel’ me blease…” It almost made Bob consider returning home to cherish this throbbing, metallic taste in the back of his mouth, and the occasional jabbing Morses of pain that communicated between his back molars, the backs of his eyeballs, and his eardrums. “Ah nee’ see Li’l Teh-wah ‘bout this bain’ from mah gums,” the receptionist said, spitting blood all over the insurance questionnaire attached to a blood spattered wooden clipboard before handing it to Bob over the front desk. “Don’ tay all day, bleaase…”

Bob, Li’l Terror, dentist

From what Bob understood, “Li’l Terror” wasn’t the small, feisty-looking dentist’s nickname. Her parents, Irene and Judas Terror, from Hermosa Beach, had paid her way through dental school with a generous grant from the California Prison Board of Corrective Surgery, who had promised to let her perform her required one thousand hours of public-service-repayment at the California Men’s Colony, before the inmates rioted and nearly killed the warden–who rewarded their last-minute change-of-heart by canceling Li’l Terror’s debt. And as far as “Li’l”–that first name on her birth certificate had been adopted from her father’s favorite super hero character, Li’l Abner. (Yes, Judas Terror was a good and supportive father, but not very bright.)

Since it brought considerable relaxation to her office’s visibly distraught atmosphere, Li’l Terror had spiked the water cooler with horse tranquilizers. When patients awoke in the waiting room after several grueling, unremembered hours of examinations, x-rays, hygiene, gum-piercings, and violent extractions, they didn’t seem to mind the blood pouring freely from their lips, nose and mouth. “You’ll be okay,” Li’l Terror told Bob as he surfaced from a white haze of staticky near-bliss. She wore thick bottle-lensed glasses that made her resemble a very short, well-rounded female version of Michael Caine in The Ipcress File. “You just had a gum wrapper stuck between your wisdom tooth and the other one, that molar next to the wisdom tooth. I forget what it’s called. So take lots of Ibuprofen and go buy yourself a drink at McCarthy’s, Bob! You earned it!”

20

DR. MABUSE–WORLD’S BEST DAD

After much reflection, Dr. Mabuse decided the central coast was the best place in the world to raise a crime family. Good schools, healthy air quality, clean water, and plenty of unfrequented mountain trails, foggy beaches and untended landfills for hiking, camping, and dumping bodies. Rocko, Fantomas and Cy Sperling–the three principal henchmen he had adopted from the Cambria County School for Suspiciously Gifted Children–had made huge strides in their abilities to smell out and exploit potential victims, as well as divert well-endowed, vulnerable countesses and duchesses to their nefarious dooms. “That goggle-eyed hypnotic stare is coming along marvelously!” Mabuse praised Rocko. “You’re dealing cards off the bottom of the deck like an old pro!” he praised Fantomas. “The way you carry the Countess Danamora through the dank sewers beneath San Luis Obispo makes me want to be that countess!” he praised Cy Sperling. After all, children don’t learn by being criticized for every little thing they did wrong–that had been Dr. Mabuse’s dad’s way of doing things. They learned by receiving sincere, generous compliments on what they did right.

Mrs. Mabuse, Dr. Mabuse,Cy Sperling, Countess Danamora, Rocko, Fantomas

“You can’t expect young criminals to sit in the garage all day learning how to forge documents, kidnap high ranking politicians, ransom government securities, and adopt impenetrable disguises,” Mrs. Mabuse often reminded her husband. “They need to get out in the sun, engage in healthy sports activities, attend church fairs and picnics, and get to know the big beautiful world they live in as pro-active passengers on Spaceship Earth! The only happy criminal is a healthy criminal–and don’t forget it, hon.”

But of course Dr. Mabuse never forgot. It was the first thing he thought every morning when he woke and the last thing he thought every night when he went to sleep: “Marrying Mrs. Mabuse was the smartest decision I ever made!” And as for leaving the bitter, fog-bound streets of Berlin behind for the warm, fragrant hills and valleys of San Luis Obispo–well, that had been, and remained, a no-brainer as well.

A PLUTOCRAT A DAY KEEPS THE DOCTOR AWAY

When Dr. Tiny Aguilera, the kindest and most sympathetic mid-life-challenges therapist on the central coast, arrived at her basement office in Los Osos, she found a large Swastikar parked out front adorned with graffiti-sketches of penises, dickheads, dickheads with penises, penises shaped as dickheads, and lots and lots of penises.

“I used to transcend space and time,” wailed the distraught, recently transmogrified Elon, who lay sprawled out on Tiny’s best couch, dripping raw animal matter all over her recently power-cleaned carpets. “People thought I was cool. I got invited to all the parties. I was even invited to host Saturday Night Live, whatever the hell that is. Then I crashed back to reality, boy. With a bang! After uploading my lovely personality (two bytes) and my vanity (several million Peta-Bytes) into one of my shiniest satellites, I was ready for everything! Except crashing back to earth where, deprived of my hunkin’ young-dude face and body, I dragged my way up out of the muddy pit I’d cratered in Laguna Lake, and had to form myself out of whatever substances I could find. Worms, mostly. Mud, seaweed, old used condoms, cigarette butts, dead leaves, rubber boots, fishing tackle, slatted rotten bits of boats and oars, and lots of duck poop. Every time I needed something important for reconstituting my physiognomy, such as an eyeball or a nostril, that’s all that was available. Duck poop and worms. I know I don’t look my best, but give me time. A trillion dollars can buy a lotta good looks, and if that don’t work, I can always wear a cool T-shirt. Don’t you think I’m cool, Dr. Tiny? Every frat boy in America says so. Boy, I sure love cool T-shirts. Don’t you?”

Elon and Tiny

Dr Tiny didn’t like to give advice; she felt her patients should be led into routes of reflection that helped them formulate their own advice for themselves. But after only ten minutes of Elon, she made an exception: “Get your leaky butt off my new couch,” she told him. “We aren’t taking new patients at this time, and even if we were, we wouldn’t be taking you.”

JUDGMENT DAY (AND THAT MEANS YOU!)

It would be funny if it wasn’t so true (or true if it wasn’t so funny), but our favorite resident aliens, the oviparous, unisexual twins, Sam and Sam, have just been arrested for improper use of pronouns and threatened with deportation! Some of the pronouns they have allegedly misused to refer to themselves were or have been: “therm,” “disnts,” “hermaphrobits,” “ollie-ollies,” hisorhisnts,” “Mr-mees,” and most disturbing of all, “hermen.” In San Luis Obispo County Court this afternoon, they are being represented by none other than Sideways Charlie, the only member of his former law firm (Charlie, Berkowitz, Charlie, Charlie & Charlie) who wasn’t indicted by the Biden Administration and then pardoned to go work for the Trump Administration. Meanwhile, representing the state (or statelessness) of America’s Immigration and Customs Enforcement, stand the entirety of Sideways Charlie’s previous partners–Berkowitz, Charlie, Charlie and… um..oh yeah, Charlie. Those of whom weren’t slumped over their communal desk asleep, anyway. (Which, come to think of it, was all of them.)

The right honorable (sometimes) Judge Ernst Blofeld, Jr. has requested clarification on the finer points of law from either the defendants or their counsel, specifically: “Why did they do it?” “Why didn’t they stop doing it?” “What did they expect to gain by doing it?” “Didn’t they know justice would come gunning for anybody who did it?” And most important of all: “Would you rate Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem a nine or a ten? Is that really how to spell her name, and if so, would you have her private cell phone number?” Then, after a gaze into the far blue yonder of his courtroom, Judge Blofeld, Jr. whispered, possibly to himself: “By the way, do either of you have your green card with you?”

Judge Blofeld, Sam and Dave

Feeling an unfamiliar sinking sensation in one of his stomachs (located in that part of his body that corresponded with where most human beings keep their medulla oblongata), Sam turned to his brother and asked: “Green card? What’s a green card?” At which point his brother Sam replied: “Oh crap.”

LONELY IN LOVE

Stevie Nicks, the loneliest vulture in San Luis Obispo, has a terrible problem–whenever she falls in love with someone, they die. For example, that ninety-something woman out on Prefumo Canyon Road who spent the last three years lying motionless in her backyard hammock–Stevie found her so fascinating, that she set up perch on the fence, where she attracted nothing but condemnation from the old woman’s neighbors. (“Scat!” they shouted, hurling rocks and bottles. “Leave Eleanor alone! Eleanor? Are you okay, Eleanor? Eleanor! Maybe someone should call a doctor…”) Or the barn owl that had nested on a rooftop until it misted over with cobwebs and dust. Or the half-squashed raccoon that lay out on the side of Los Osos Valley Road after a sudden encounter with a big yellow school bus. “I find you totally fascinating,” Stevie had informed each of these motionless figures in turn. “I’m sure you hear that from lots of vultures, but I really mean it.”

“I’ve been recently struck by how fascinating I find your grandpa,” Stevie confided to Bob one night at McCarthy’s Irish Pub. They were happily sharing the gritty remains of a pitcher of that month’s “Micro-Brewery Special,” IPF (“I Pee Freely”) from Ground Down Hops, Inc. out in Reservoir Canyon–only a stone’s throw from Honey Brazil’s Day Care Center for Difficult Toddlers. (They knew it was a stone’s throw since Honey had recently been throwing so many stones.) “I don’t remember the last time I found somebody so fascinating, unless maybe it was the possum that fell asleep down by the creek and never woke up again. He smells like a compost heap filled with rotting fish skins and cod liver oil. He smells like a dead seal on a beach. He sits on that bus bench outside Sunshine Donuts and hardly moves a muscle, unless it’s to turn the page of one of those beat up old paperback books he carries around with him in a hand-worn brown paper bag. Something about Bug Sucklers from Space. Which is another thing about your grandpa I find fascinating. He has so much imagination. I could never get into sci-fi myself. It just seems too far-fetched to believe.”

Bob and Stevie vulture

Bob had spent the afternoon catching up with his sleep on the fold out army cot in his garage. It had left him feeling mildly invigorated and hopeful. “Yeah,” he said, pouring himself and Stevie the last of their third pitcher of IPF. “That sure sounds like Grandpa.”

HIGHER ED OR DEI!

Ever since Professor Rufus ‘Geronimo’ Bloodsport retired as Dean of Studies to go snorkeling with the otters in Morro Bay, the faculty at The Whole Earth University of Arts and Sciences in Rancho el Chorro has been decimated by its efforts to obey the Trump Administration’s strict new DEI guidelines, summarily firing everyone they had hired for spurious reasons, such as for being women, Hispanic women, Afro-American women, non binary women, living women, and, of course, just plain women. (Did we mention they fired all the women?) Which turned out to be a heck of an opportunity for their only functional non-living woman, Zombie Juliet, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Composition and Rhetorical Strategies of Rhetoricity. Since the mostly-binary white male Program Head, Professor Dodge Roundabout, was disinclined to leave his storage closet whenever he was equipped with all he needed from life (i.e., pencils), Zombie Juliet now teaches all twenty seven sections of Intro Comp, Intermediate Comp, Comp Plus and Comp-Lite. In her spare time, she writes essays, and acts as peer reviewer, for today’s most reputable (and unreadable) academic journals on the theory and practice of Composition, such as Composition Theory Quarterly, Composition Practice Quarterly, Composition Theory and Practice Quarterly, Composition Theory Today, Composition Theory for Morons, Composition Theory Spectacular, Composition Theory ‘R’ Us, More More More I Can’t Get Enough of that Composition Theory, and of course Nature’s sister magazine The Composition Theory Weekly Reader. (There are a lot of unreadable composition journals out there, that’s all we’re saying.)

Zombie Juliet and students

“Errrrrr,” Zombie Juliet instructed her students (the two who usually showed up, anyway) at the start of her seven a.m. class. “Errrrrr!” And boy did her students know what she meant!

SUSPICIOUS EYES

Whenever they aren’t going on CNN to bemoan the poor quality of the younger generation of war criminals (“They don’t believe in Democracy or Freedom!”), John Bolton and his fellow members of the War Punkers (Tony Blair on bass, Dick Cheney on tambourine, and whatever it is that Hilary Clinton and Madeleine Albright are doing with that banjo) perform live in bad garage clubs along Los Osos Valley Road; and any time they’re feeling especially ornery, they engage in frequent head-butting contests with the closest thing they have to fans–the Sisters of Brutal Mercy–Immaculata, Boniface, and Claude Rains.

The Sisters

The Sisters belong to a breakaway Catholic schism who refused to accept either the doctrines of transubstantiation, or that other one (we can’t recall the name) that insists nuns should inflict meaningless suffering upon all school children who haven’t done their homework. “If our Lord had wanted us to torment small children,” one of their founding mothers, Sister Boy George Murphy, often declaimed, “then She wouldn’t have provided us so many fully grown, adult idiots to brutalize–speaking of which, Tony Blair, take this, and that, and this other thing, you mealy-mouthed psychopath! Weapons of mass-destruction, my consecrated ass! And as for you, Bolton–” Sister Immacualata’s head-butts were a thing of beauty–at least if you weren’t on the receiving end of them. “Learn a basic chord or two on that thing or prepare for eternal suffering! And tell Hilary to put down that damn banjo before we get really pissed!”

The Sisters are best-known for operating the highly-regarded Cambria County School for Suspiciously Gifted Children, where Sister Boniface teaches Art Appreciation when she isn’t playing bongos in school choir, and Sister Claude Rains maintains the topiary. The suspiciously gifted children, meanwhile, do what suspiciously-gifted children do wherever space and time permits–they behave like children, and do their best to prevent anybody like John Bolton from finding out about it.

BUGGED OUT

Sgt. Stud Thunderbolt’s dementia has gotten so bad–and his imbecilic drooling so prolific–while being rolled around the Never Die Young, Inc. Senior Care Facility by the new Head of Administration, Nurse Ratchet, that he has managed to complete three brand new Bug Suckler novels in only three days! And boy would Stud be proud–if, that is, it weren’t for the, you know, the dementia.

Sgt. Stud Thunderbolt, Brad Firbender, Sam and Dave

“This guy is amazing!” gloated Brad Firbender, his editor at Dazed and Confused Publishing, which operated out of a mesh-walled unit at Alamo Self Storage on Tank Farm Road. “He doesn’t know his name or where he is and he can still crank these suckers out! Look–one hundred and twenty thousands words of Bug Sucklers Go Ape-Shit on Ranga-Ranga-Doon! Two hundred and seventy thousand words comprising Bug Sucklers Take their Meds! And nearly three hundred thousands words making up Bug Sucklers Roll Down Hospital Corridors on a Gurney! Where does he get all these amazing ideas? That’s nearly–I don’t have my calculator–but a lot of goddamn words, and the fact that they’re all the same word–specifically, “bugsuckler”–simply typed over and over again, isn’t a big concern since we can easily bring in a rewrite man, or maybe a rewrite woman–I hear Alicia’s free as soon as she dusts off six more of those idiotically successful Captain America movies she’s been doing. So what do you say, Sam and Dave? Are we going to capitalize on the fact that Stud was mistakenly nominated for a Hugo Award at the Brighton World SF convention–the result of the committee mistaking Stud’s nom de plume, Robbert E. Hinnelleinn, for the grandmaster of galaxy spanning sci-fi. But mistaken or not, never fear! I can smell a bestseller just as clearly as our old friend, Stevie Nix, can smell the next love of her life! And these new books literally stink of genius! Unless, of course, Stud had another of his famous accidents on some of these pages…”

Which, of course, was exactly what Brad Firbender smelled. But not Sam and Dave–who, just informed about the imminent deportation of their unisexual twin offspring, Sam and Sam, were already flashing off across town in their 1961 Ford Fairlane station wagon to save the day!

SAME OL’ SEX PARTNERS

Unfortunately for Sam and Sam (or for Sam and Dave, for that matter) the alien CEO’s of Dazed and Confused Publishing, Ltd. got stuck in traffic on 101 just outside Santa Maria, and by the time they caught up with the I.C.E. van, it had been turned back by the Mexican border authorities who just didn’t like the way they looked. But as karma often reminds us, the worst-laid plans of sentient beings often lead to the best outcomes, and versa-vice-uh; which meant that just as the I.C.E. van was disgorging its incestuous (in an un-American way) same-sex (in an unchristian way) oviparous (what’s oviparous mean again?) sex-partners (ask your father) in San Clemente, Sam and Dave were sitting down for a coffee at the military PX, which had been established to assure the world back in 2018 that John Bolton was fully committed to annex the city and make it part of the god-fearing and anti-same-sex-nation of the United States and nobody was telling America what to do, not the I.C.C. or the World Court, or the United Nations, or Oprah, etc.

Sam, Dave, seagulls

“At least they make good hot chocolate,” Dave confirmed to Sam, after tasting it with what most human beings might have called his “little finger.” “Makes me wonder about the brownies.”

Dave was wondering about the brownies, likewise, and meanwhile gazing out the wide window at the setting sun, and the bullying crowds of seagulls pecking at crusts of bread up and down the long woody pier. Following this ocular trajectory, his attention was drawn to one particular seagull named Bucky Alexander who was pecking at something much larger, more attractive, saucier and yes, just as oviparous as any seagull. “Sam!” Dave shouted, though of course nobody could hear him through the window. “Sam!” Sam shouted, putting down his hot chocolate. “Sam!” Sam shouted at the seagull. And so forth.

ONE FLEW OVER LOS OSOS

Nurse Ratched loved working with old people, sick people, mentally ill people, and even violently psychopathic people–which pretty much described all the patients, staff and visitors at Never Die Young, Inc., the only convalescent hospital in Los Osos equipped with its own crematorium. She loved the way they looked up at her with big wobbly eyes whenever she forced morning meds through their clenched dentures. She loved the way they sighed softly at the conclusion of every electro-shock treatment. (They didn’t actually need the treatments so much as Nurse Ratched just really enjoyed giving them.) But most of all, she loved seeing that weird glint of rage in their red eyes every time she presented them the monthly bill, which was calculated to far exceed each patient’s combined monthly income from private pension plans and social security. “Health isn’t cheap,” she loved to tell her patients. But whether they loved hearing it or not–they weren’t saying.

“I just think Dad would be better off living with his family that loves him,” Detective Stud Thunderbolt of the Cal Poly Library Police explained firmly to Nurse Ratched at their first patient-provider conference, a few weeks after she replaced the sufficiently disgraced and federally convicted Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation.) “I’m sure we could make do with an extra few thousand a month, not to mention Dad’s suddenly reinvigorated income from his soon-to-be-bestselling Bug Suckler novels. (According to Brad, anyway.) Now why don’t you help me get Dad into the back of my pick-up with our recently adopted dog, Butch Leavenworth, and I’ll take him home and put him straight to work–I mean, bed–in the garage. These Bug Suckler novels don’t grow on trees, you know. And as far as his daily treatments, which end of this contraption plugs into the wall and which end plugs into dad? Does it come with a manual or anything? If not, I’m sure I’ll figure it out.”

Butch Leavenworth had never met a human being he didn’t respect until the day he met the nearly comatose Sgt. Stud in the open-air bed of his new master’s truck. It was something about his breath, and that twitching index finger typing out the same word over and over on an invisible computer keyboard in the dementia-ridden old man’s hyperactively discombobulated imagination. “‘Bugsuckler’ to you too, Bud,” Butch said. “‘Bugsuckler’ to you, too!”

Sgt. Stud, Butch, Nurse Ratched, truck

THE FABULOUS AND OFTEN FORGETTABLE HISTORY OF SAN CLEMENTE

Since they were uncertain how soon they wanted to be reunited with their green cards in the troublesomely uncertain United States of America, our favorite oviparous aliens, Sam and Dave, along with their equally oviparous twin offspring, Sam and Sam, have decided to spend the day on a walking tour through the fabulous and untroubled (compared to the USA) nation of San Clemente.

Sam, Dave, Sam, Sam, tour guide

“The nation was founded,” explained their tour guide–the unusually happy and well-adjusted Sarah Akbar Rafsanjani–through a petite baby-blue bullhorn, “by Father Junipero San Clemente in 1675, about the same time that Zorro’s grandfather, known to history by his unbecoming nickname of Zorro the Improper, was robbing local villages while wearing a pair of lacy pink women’s panties as a mask. Father Junipero was fleeing the near-extinction of Catholic missionaries by the rampaging bears of Los Osos, who had decided to devour their devourers as their devourers had once devoured them. And, of course, not far behind the bears coming hard and fast were the Sisters of Brutal Mercy, who had decided to erase any evidence that their religious elders treated the native populations with disdain–largely by erasing their religious elders. Hiding out in a dugout under the pier, Father Junipero quickly disappeared from the history of our town–not that he would be missed. And this is where the US Marines first landed, sent to occupy San Clemente by the then relatively kind and benevolent war criminal, John Bolton (I mean, he’s not as bad as the current ones, is he? Or not?) on the unspoken assumption that America needed to win a war and San Clemente was the only town less fortified, and less capable of defending itself, than the sort of dirt-poor countries America preferred invading. And this is the P.X. where Lance Corporal Riley Sumter-Lee, the fine and noble son of country-western and not-quite-a-legend, Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee died in a freak beer keg explosion. And this, my friends, is the site of my long-time happy home, living in a tent with the love of my life, Dolores del Rio, whose beauty was so legendary in these parts that it even managed to persist many decades after her death. Boy, I miss her every day; but I still have her movies (available at the PX on video cassette) to keep me company on these long, fragrant winter nights. Well, I guess that’s about it. Oh, and that trash can is where one of the more notorious Miner Forty Niners raised one of his bastard broods. His name was Rapscallion T. Underpants, but most people just referred to him as the ‘Naughty’ Miner. And look. A seagull! Sitting on the edge of that trash can. What do you have to say for yourself, seagull?”

It was, of course, the most cordial seagull in maritime history–Bucky Alexander, who took this brief pause in the monologue as an opportunity to wiggle his bottom seductively and release a large, ovular blob of poop that resembled a cameo profile of Alexander Hamilton. “My name is Bucky Alexander,” the seagull said. “And I approved this message.”
