POWER SAVES

Here’s the good news first: Detective Stud Thunderbolt, having recently relocated his beloved (and mentally vacated) father home from an intensive-care facility to the warm (sometimes) comfort of his two car garage, has finally figured out which end of the electro-shock device plugs into the wall, and which end plugs into Dad.

Thunderbolt and electric outage

And now the bad news: his home energy is provided by the impossibly destructive, over-paid governing board of PG&E. And the moment he flipped the switch, the entire local grid–from Cambria down to Arroyo Grande–went dark.

Throughout the central coast, individual residents responded in individual ways to the end (however brief) of techno-civilization. In Laguna Lake, Chief Thread took it as an excellent opportunity to sneak into the homes of neighbors and try out their sofas. Way up at the end of Monterey Street, the not-at-all-legendary country-western never-to-be-an-icon singer-songwriter, Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee, picked up his twelve (or maybe thirteen) string geee-tar and strummed a few sudden, almost supernaturally-inspired lyrics: “Mah name is Zorro,” Tex Mex whispered. “And I am deceased. Vaya con dios! Death is such a beast…” In the garage-club circuit of Los Osos, the worst and most over-amped band in human history, The War Punkers (with Dick Cheney on tambourine–need we say more?) have gone remarkably, almost blessedly, silent. And in Bob Johnson’s ’89 Sundance, which Bob left parked outside some bar he couldn’t remember frequenting, the mice have decided to party, party, party like there’s no tomorrow. (There isn’t.) “Making love in the dark is such a treat!” they all exclaimed in warm quivering little tandems and trios in their messy little mouse beds throughout the glove compartment, ashtray, and several soiled cardboard fast food containers. “Not because I can’t see what you look like, honey! But because then you can’t see me!”

31

THOUGHT FOR THE DAY

The worst part about major power outages is that they don’t last forever. If they did, the terrible folks at PG&E would be unable to charge customers for the privilege of watching the company incinerate, in steady chronological flash-forged increments, the entire State of California, one dysfunctional power transformer at a time.

On the morning after, everyone woke slowly, crankily and inevitably; but none more so than Tex Mex, who reached out in the dazzling dawn sunlight for his devoted gee-tar, and grasped instead the disturbingly sweaty buttocks of Zorro’s horse, Tornado.

Tornado, Tex Mex, morning after

In their musky, orgy-battered apartments, the mice in Bob Johnson’s car rolled over, rubbed their eyes, and gazed into the eyes of other mice who gazed, just as unhappily, back at them. Bob Johnson, well… (It was Bob–what more can you say?) And Stevie Nicks, the loneliest vulture in SLO, found her arms and neck wrapped round an adorable (and very dead) badger, formerly known as Prince.

And still plugged into a charred and well-blown wall socket, Sgt. Stud Thunderbolt, former UFO investigator for the Truckee Police Department, illustrious former nominee for the prestigious Hugo award, and not-quite-ceased-drooling-yet alumni of Never Die Young, Inc., the only convalescent hospital in Los Osos with its own open graveyard, sat up in the cold metal bed of his son’s truck, brushed off what looked like a layer of roasted peanut shells, (“I like roasted peanuts–what can I say?” shrugged his newly-adopted dog, Butch Leavenworth) and reopened his mind to a universe filled with narrative possibilities more interesting than himself. Then, after another moment of deep reflection, he said the first words he had said in a long, long time. “Who in their right mind?” he asked, “would read, write, or even reflect upon a series of incredibly stupid sf novels featuring Bug Sucklers?” Then he lay back, rested his tired head against the soft haunches of the well-aging and somewhat threadbare Butch Leavenworth, and drifted softly back to sleep.

32

TRIXIE BELDEN MEETS HER MATCH

One of the only students who never misses Zombie Juliet’s 7 am class in Rhetorical Strategies of Composition and Intertextual-Rhetoricity every Monday-Thursday was Trixie Belden, the best looking girl’s cheerleader at Rancho el Chorro University of Arts and Sciences, as well as an occasional stunt double for the superstar international literary rights agent, Darlene “the Rock” Verhoeven-Johnson, who had been last seen hang-gliding into a monsoon with her close friends, Captain Ponce de Leon, and his newlywed wife, AI Sat Nav voice and hot shot movie director, Alicia Keys. “Frankly, just being able to tie up all those loose ends from the last Bob Johnson novel,” Trixie confided to Juliet at lunch in the school cafeteria, “already makes me a useful character in the very first paragraph of this stupid chapter.”

Trixie Belden and Zombie Juliet

Zombie Juliet had never considered enjoying an unprofessional, same-sex relationship with Trixie until that moment. There was something in the way the high flickering fluorescents caromed off Trixie’s magenta eye-shadow that sent the coagulated blood-quivering, jello-like, through Juliet’s moldy old zombie heart. And the way her perfect pink-gummed teeth glinted with sensual enjoyment as she bit into her meatless mushroom burger and sweet potato fries both captivated Juliet, and strengthened her resolve to never herself attempt eating a meatless mushroom burger and sweet potato fries. “Errrr,” she told Trixie, who didn’t seem confused by Juliet’s response so much as a bit, well, abashed that she had earned so much attention from her favorite Proff. I mean they were eating lunch together in the school cafeteria! How cool was that?

“Meeting guys has never been difficult for me,” Trixie said, winking at several young men from the Cold Turkey Softball team who, entering the huge military-sized cafeteria, were instinctively making a wide arc around their least favorite college Proff (Juliet) while still managing to catch the eye of their favorite cheerleader (Trixie.) “Ever since I can remember, I always got more valentines than any of the other girls in my class, and more dates with the most popular boys, and even my teachers liked me more than the other girls, perhaps because of my winsome nature. I was made number one cheerleader for our school team, the Cold Turkeys, without even a try-out; in fact, I never even knew there was an audition. But despite all my not-hard-won successes, the thing I always wanted most in life was to express myself linguistically in a rhetorically appropriate manner that would reflect the historicity of my grammatical-being right down to the, you know, the rhetoricity. Does that make sense, Miss Zombie Juliet? I know you’re dead and all, but you possess more rhetorical strategies in one of your bitten and bleeding fingernails than any other teacher I’ve ever met. And perhaps, if there was some sort of extra credit assignment that you and I could do together that might require us to share a candle-lit dinner at the Madonna Inn, or a couple of super hero movies at the Sunset Drive In, then it might be good for both of us? Get where I’m coming from? Oh darn! I ended that paragraph with a rhetorical question! What the hell was I thinking?”

33

VISITING HOURS AREN’T OVER UNTIL I SAY THEY’RE OVER

Visiting hours at the California Men’s Colony are whenever Honey Brazil says they are–that’s how terrified the bulky, over-weaponized guards are by the diminutive, compact and unpredictable Honey. “You can call me Sugar,” she told Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation) on their first date, after she clipped open a wrist-sized hole in the barbed wire fence dividing them in order to take one of his sweaty, unattractive hands into one of her even sweatier, even more unattractive hands. “And I’ll call you whatever I damn well feel like calling you. Dad told me you’re a filthy-minded, porn-addicted, double-entendre-mouthed, leering corpuscle of a masturbating loser, and those are the nice things. What can I tell you–I’m a girl who loves to be loved in whatever crude, unpalatable ways she can find. And you might just be the man I end up marrying, whether either of us likes it or not.” One of the kids from Honey’s unlicensed Daycare for Troubled Tots, Tusk, was gnawing at one of the loose table legs–which was perfectly okay with Honey, so long as he wasn’t gnawing on one of hers.

Dr. Harvey Weinstein, Diamond Dog Bowie Brazil, jail

Dr Harvey Weinstein (no relation) will do just about anything he can to get out of the cell he’s sharing with Honey’s estranged father, the brutal and tincture-devoted California legend in plein air landscape painting, Diamond Dog Bowie Brazil. It’s not just that the smell of acrylics have incited some disfiguring skin allergies he never knew he was prone to; or that Diamond Dog had learned to release his creative frustrations with a bed-board on the always-slow-to-anticipate Harvey. It was mainly because the only female guards at the facility were so unattractive that Harvey couldn’t even bring himself to leer at them when they went by his cell, or speculate openly on the color and dimensions of their underwear. “Life is hard,” Harvey often had occasion to reflect. “But no matter how hard it might seem, Diamond Dog’s bed-board is always at least several degrees harder.” Confronted with the only possibility of parole available to him in the state of California, Harvey was beginning to think that this Honey Brazil character might not look as bad as, well, as she looked.

Later, Honey visited the warden in his gothically-decorated office (rack, guillotine, wall-sized posters of Margaret Thatcher, the works). His name was Baron Marquis de Sade 2nd Class and Counting Steinbrunner-Cantankerous-Jones (Max for short), a middle-aged man who had spent his life–and his substantial inheritance–seeking a castle-away-from-castle where he could indulge his appetites for crude sexual wordplay and meaningless fetishisms without fear of exposure or ridicule. The California Men’s Colony, he had decided in just the last few days or so, was definitely not that place. “Honey,” the warden toasted her with one of his cut-crystal goblets filled to the brim with low-budget white wine from Trader Joe’s, “I’m going to do something I always promised myself I wouldn’t do. Out of a romantic streak in my nature, I’m giving your boyfriend Harvey a full pardon; and since it’s not possible for me to give him a full pardon, we’ll do the following. You drive your van up outside his cell tonight around nine or nine thirty. Then I’ll pack him up in a burlap sack of dirty laundry and toss him off the third floor. Catch him or don’t catch him–it’s up to you!”

GUNSMOKE’EM IF YOU GOT ‘EM

These days, poor Bob Johnson is feeling increasingly disenfranchised from the story of his own life. “Who the hell is Dr. Mabuse?” Bob moans to his grandpa, sharing day-old donuts with him on his sun-struck wooden bus bench on South Higuera. “And what has he got to do with me? And why does Honey Brazil merit more paragraphs per week than I do? I was the one she ran over in her stupid truck and almost died, or did die, I’m still not entirely clear about that part. And since when did anybody (i.e., me) care about the faculty at The Whole Earth University of Arts and Sciences in Rancho el Chorro? I don’t even know what composition theory is let alone zombies. I’m telling you, Grandpa, I’m starting to feel like one of those late episodes of Gunsmoke, remember, like after it had been running fifty years or so? Matt Dillon looked more than a hundred years old and about three thousand pounds; it made me feel so sorry for his horse. He’d walk into Kitty’s saloon and have a drink and wander off again and the whole episode would be about someone else. Some guy and his son coming to town from their ranch, or some mail order bride ordered by Festus through Wells Fargo. What was the deal with Festus, anyway? Chester, he was a different story, but Festus! I never understood him at all. By the way, do you have any more donuts with the sprinkles on them, Grandpa? I really love the ones with sprinkles.”

Bob and Grandpa on a bus bench with donuts

Grandpa was, at that very moment, guiltily wiping several rainbow colored sprinkles from his lips and cheeks and gazing into his expired box of day old donuts as if it contained the memory of some lost love. “Sometimes our lives get away from us,” he told Bob, hoping to do what grandpas were supposed to do in this town–provide wisdom, patience and understanding. (If Bob’s Grandpa could manage one of those qualities in a 12 month period, he figured that was about as good as he could expect from himself.) “That doesn’t mean we can’t keep trying, Bob. Or, better yet, just order more donuts with sprinkles next time.”

Bob thought about this for a few moments. His grandpa was trying to be forthcoming with wisdom again. Bob was wondering if he even wanted to encounter wisdom coming from the general direction of his grandpa when he looked up and saw one of the town’s oldest, most sway-backed and loudly farting horses trotting slowly past, wearing a long black Zorro mask as if it were acting out an equestrian version of Halloween. Turning to Bob, Tornado said, “Horse? What horse? And where can I rent or stream this excellent sounding television show you mention called Gunsmoke? Sounds muy excellente, mi amigo!”

Bob, bartender, girls

FRIDAY NIGHT LITERARY LIGHTS

Being electroshocked into and out of a coma that left most of the central coast without power for twenty four hours was the best thing that ever happened to Sgt. Stud Thunderbolt, former UFO investigator for the Truckee Police Department. One moment, he was a less-than-moderately successful sci-fi novelist whose dementia prevented him from having to read the horrible dreck he produced; the next moment he was a much more mobile, virile, and artsy Stud, who wouldn’t have been caught dead reading a Bug Suckler novel even in a public laundromat or place of worship–let alone writing one. “I’m more of a Henry James sort of guy,” the renewed, revivified Stud told his many adoring visitors who had come to line up outside the garage he shared with his son’s Oldsmobile to receive personally-inscribed autographs for his latest novel, Bug Sucklers Take Their Meds. “And when it comes to cinema, I prefer Truffaut, Fellini, Ingmar Bergman, and Pedro Almodovar. Sgt. Stud Thunderbolt autographs books

Visitors included some of the central coast’s best and brightest literary figures and cultural yay-sayers. There was, of course, the always-comely Madame Bovary, wearing something fetching and low cut, hefting a stack of battered, unwholesomely stained paperback copies of various Bug Suckler novels she had liberated from a recent library sale. And behind her stood the warden out at the California Men’s Colony, Baron Marquis de Sade 2nd Class and Counting Steinbrunner-Cantankerous-Jones (make it easy for yourself and just call him “Max”) who was wearing something almost as fetching and even more low-cut–not to mention the spiked high heels. “I’m hoping he’ll sign this old copy of 120 Days of Sodom,” he told Madame Bovary, which was the closest he came to a conversational gambit when attempting to introduce himself to a pretty girl. “Mainly so it doesn’t look like I wrote it.” And finally, bringing up the rear (and please don’t use that expression around Max), stood Bob’s former girlfriend and perhaps even ex-wife, Cassandra Knye (neither of them agreed to talk about it), wearing something that wasn’t at all fetching or low-cut but which definitely looked better on her than it would have on Max. Like any local novelist worth his or her salt, Cassandra never leaves the house carrying any books but her own–such as the recent reissue of The House that Fear Built, her latest ‘dark romance” bestseller to be optioned by the brilliant, commando-style international literary rights agent, Darlene “the Rock” Verhoeven-Johnson. “The idea came to me in a dream,” Cassandra told whoever it was standing behind her in line. “And if you want me to go into more detail about where I get my ideas, check out my Subtsack page. But of course no identifiably human entity could be found standing behind her–only a shortish, roundish, poorly groomed Cthulhu named Rex Morales. “I never miss a book signing,” Rex said, to nobody in particular. (Mainly since nobody was listening.) “Don’t ask me why; I just don’t.”

Stud Thunderbolt has his first-ever library card, he has been checking out many lesser-known films from the postwar San Luis Obispo Film Renaissance, a period loosely defined by historians as occurring between April 13th and June 7th, 1975, and all the finest examples of which are being currently released in overpriced 4k and Blu Ray restorations from Criterion. These include Ingmar Bergman’s influential masterpieces, Fanny and Alexander Johnson and Wild Strawberries a la Johnson, as well 8 1/2 Bobs, Jules et Jim (Sans Bob), Breathlessly Bob, and most notoriously, Fellini’s Satyricon-Bob, which is entirely made up of scenes featuring attractive young men and women wearing togas who sit around criticizing some Bob-like guy who looks incredibly awful wearing a toga. “Blecchh, just look at that guy, willya!” exclaims Marcello Mastroianni on more than one occasion. And: “I wouldn’t get caught dead talking to a guy who looked as bad in a toga as that guy!” chimes in Anita Ekberg. Everyone agrees it’s a masterpiece of some sort of brilliant type of film-making that nobody ever saw before, and this is especially notable since all these films were made well before Bob Johnson was even born in time to grow up to look half as bad in a toga as the guy playing Bob did.

Currently screening at the SLO Film Festival, Fellini’s Satyricon-Bob has garnered accolades such as: “Somebody please put some clothes on that guy!” and “I never want to see anybody wearing a toga ever again, not even Gina Lollobrigida!”

“I never meant to cause so much trouble!” the Bob-like character cries out in several notable scenes, especially when he’s being pursued by a bare-chested Anthony Quinn across the sands of Pismo Beach during a thunderstorm. “I just wanted to live my life without merit, and look what it brought me!” “I see what it brought you, Little Man!” thunders back Anthony Quinn. “It brought you me, Anthony Quinn! Hunter calls it BJ-2025®, and one would wish that it was an acronym for “Bob Johnson 2025,” but that would be a wish that failed to materialize in whatever it is these days we call ‘reality.’ What the app actually does is allow subscribers to manufacture a GIF of any celebrity giving the actual Hunter Biden a blow job and allowing them to send it out to whatever friends they have left (probably not many) on their i-Phones. “Just imagine the possibilities!” Hunter Biden Johnson told Sam and Sam. “Anybody you can imagine giving Hunter Biden the business–Mark Wahlberg, Nancy Pelosi, Hunter Thompson, Marco Rubio, Joe Camel, Frankie Laine Gotcha, the Doublemint Twins, any previous or current judge on either X-Factor or America’s Got Talent, or even the actual Hunter Biden–the possibilities are limitless! Unfortunately these endless possibilities are restricted to being used on an app which only allows these famous (often unjustly) individuals to do one thing, but then that’s tech-capitalism. Now, what can I put you boys down for? Would you like a ten percent share in this exciting new enterprise, or a fifty percent share in this exciting new enterprise, or do you want to just sell the spaceship and go whole hog? And by the way, I apologize for using the term ‘whole hog’ when it comes to my new app, but there you have it. I may not look like Bob Johnson, but I still got a lotta the guy in me! Oops, there I go again! So please accept my apologies in advance when it comes to making really horrible double entendres. Considering my new app, double entendres are sort of impossible to avoid–even if I wanted to. Which, of course, I don’t.”

Starting a start up turned out to be a lot easier said than saying, “Starting a start up starts up startlingly sudden.” But not quite as easy as saying: “Starting a starting up of a start up starts up startlingly easy for a start up!” Sorry, Sam and Sam. I guess I just don’t know when to stop! Pardon me!

ZOMBIEDEN

When Zombie Juliet was just a little zombie growing up in the house of her zombie parents, she had happily saved up her college money doing afternoon shifts at the family business–the Zombie-Smoothie Shack on South Higuera, which specialized in healthy death-style all flesh-and-fruit energy-drinks such as Huckleberry Hacksaw and Mango Oblongata. “Some day,” she often thought (though perhaps not this articulately), “I’m going to go to school, get my degree, and show the other zombies that there’s a much happier post-death experience than chewing on freshly slaughtered entrails and brain matter.” And sure enough, within only a few decades of starting her classes at El Chorro, she wasn’t simply attending classes in Composition Theory and Practice–she was running the whole department–if, that is, you could call what Zombie Juliet did “running” anything. All it really meant was stamping D+ grades on the hundreds of composition papers submitted by students she never met who never attended class, and keeping her faculty co-chair, Professor Emeritus Dodge Roundabout, locked safely in a utility closet with his pencils and crayons where he belonged.

Zombie Juliet and Trixie Belden

“Teaching Composition Theory was about the most you could expect from a zombie in my day,” Zombie Juliet often recalled for her girliest girl friend, Trixie Belden, when they met up for boilermakers at McCarthy’s Irish Pub. “Little did I know that I could’ve gone on to become President, or House Majority leader, like my newest heroes, Joe Biden and Nancy Pelosi! (Not to mention Chuck Grassley–whatever the hell it is that he does.) I could’ve become zombie-president, or zombie-ex-president. Or I could’ve helped push that really dead zombie, Diane Feinstein, in a wheelchair around the halls of congress during violent insurrections. I think that’s the problem with living or dying in this world–by the time you’re done doing it, all you can think about is all the wrong choices you made. And my wrong choice was definitely not choosing to be a major figure in the Democratic Party, where there’s no limit to what zombies can achieve–or how long they can keep achieving it.”

Of course, all Trixie ever heard during monologues like this were the sounds of Zombie Juliet’s broken lips and teeth emitting the words: “Errrrrr. Errrrr.” But that was the deal with being someone’s girliest girl friend–you knew what they were trying to say even when they had trouble saying it. And even after several boiler-makers.

JONATHAN LIVINGSTON (AKA “BUCKY”) ALEXANDER

Bucky Alexander, the California coast’s most cordial and unassuming seagull, has a philosophical bent to his nature that can’t be confused really with any other sort of bent. “The way I look at life,” he often told his neighbors on the San Clement pier, the (as) oviparous (as himself) space aliens, Sam and Sam, “you can either help contribute to the daily accumulations that cover the surface of our woeful world, or stay out of everybody else’s way while they do. Personally, I’ve never been a ‘leave it to the other guy’ sort of personality. So if the world needs more bird crap, then I might as well contribute my fair share.” Bucky had been born and raised in Antigua, but moved to California when he was just old enough to make the flight on his own. “You see your parents slaughtered by the propellors of an old two-seater Cessna and it changes you,” he said. “Antigua’s a beautiful place, but not when it comes to memories.”

Bucky had opinions about everything: such as that America’s two-party duopoly was not an accident so much as a deliberate plot by the world’s elite to own all of the bird crap it could get its greedy hands on, and that the only good approach to life was the carpe diem approach. “It’s the one reason I can come up with for getting out of bed in the morning,” Bucky often said. “To seize every scrap of bread I can shove in my beak and chomp it down before some other seagull comes along. Oh, and yeah. To crap on as many things as possible: people, plants, beaches, piers, dolphins, whales, other seagulls, and that two-party duopoly I was talking about. The world may not be a better place with me in it, but it’s definitely a lot crappier.”

Bucky, book, seagull

Of all the things Bucky has crapped on over the years, he has yet to crap on a copy of the once-bestselling paperback, Jonathan Livingston Seagull, which he often spotted lying tattered and abandoned on picnic benches and in large rusty garbage pails. But something told him that it was only a matter of time…

NURSE RATCHED DOES DESK DUTY

It was Nurse Ratched’s favorite day of the month–the day she could send out monthly bills to the relatives of elderly, disabled, mentally dysfunctional, and often already-long-deceased residents at the Los Osos branch of Never Die Young, Ltd., the only senior care facility on the central coast with its own lime pit in the back yard. “What a great day to be alive!” Nurse Ratched thought when she arrived, turned on all the lights in her office, and opened her Louis Vuiton leather-bound briefcase on her massy mahogany desk. “And best of all–it comes around every month!”

Nurse Ratched, desk

So she set about dispensing monthly “accounts” to each of the resident’s families–which amounted to a large rarely-itemized figure scrawled on the back of a bar napkin, or an old grocery receipt, and shoved hastily into a re-used white envelope with just enough stamps to arrive at its intended destination with a big red POSTAGE DUE imprinted on the back. She made up a bill for $13,476 for the ninety year old former soccer coach and Professor of Geophysics out at The Whole Earth University, who had made a side living selling illegally prescribed antihistamines to grade school children–Coach/Prof. Elmo Backside–charges which included a daily foot massage by two filipino nurses who Nurse Ratched had never heard of before she came up with the names for these monthly bills. (She had never yet even visited the Phillipines–but she was definitely looking forward to it!) . She made out another bill for $17,879 to the grandchildren of Emmelina Bushwrangler, a former dental hygienist at the offices of Li’l Terror–Credit Dentist, which included a daily “irrigation” fee for pushing her wheelchair through the local Dip&Dry Car Wash and Custom Detailing Service, even though Emmelina had never been requisitioned a wheelchair and, in fact, had been frozen in cryogenic hibernation since the first Trump Administration. (By choice–she just couldn’t bear to read another newspaper.) She made out a bill for $0 to the US Government for the care and maintenance of dear old Henry in Room 101, with the same personal note written in fine-tip pink flowery letters: “He’s our pleasure! What a lovely old war criminal!” And finally, she made out a whopping bill for $44,322 to the great grand children of the long deceased (and loving it!) Scintilla Jones, who had been last seen puttering off north on PCH in a smoothly-humming solar-powered wheelchair–and where she landed, nobody knew. (Except, of course, for her current live-in lover and devoted partner in exile, Bigfoot.) “What a glorious day to be alive!” Nurse Ratched repeated to herself as she stamped shut the last billing envelope with one of her tiny, well-manicured fists. “And it comes around once a month! Hurrah!”

But what’s this? The telephone? Ringing on her desk? But nobody knew this phone number except for Nurse Ratched’s best friends, family members and current top-ten list of once-per-month-lovers. And the voice on the other end of the line was both terribly familiar and terribly unfamiliar. “Nurse Ratched! Help! It’s me, your former co-director, Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation)! I don’t know where I am but I need help very badly! And I’m almost certain it has something to do with Honey Brazil!”

OVER-BORED

Of course, it might well be argued that Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation) was over-reacting to the predicament in which he found himself–bound up with zip ties in a brand new, heavily price-tagged green flannel bathrobe from Kohls, and laid out upon a warped mattress on the floor of Honey’s bedroom/slash van out in Reservoir Canyon. After freeing his limbs with a pair of conveniently-placed nail clippers he found on a wobbly wooden side table, he had since rubbed the circulation back into his wrists and ankles, placed a distraught phone call to his former team-health-care provider, Nurse Ratched, and only then noticed that the “bedroom” didn’t look half bad, decorated with pink lacy draperies over the dirty window, a pink lacy bedcover, and several heart-shaped pink lacy cushions. There was even a heart-shaped box of chocolates on the other side table, which also wobbled.

Dr. Harvey Weinstein, trailer

“In the privacy of my own heart and bedroom, I refuse to live up to my unearned reputation for brutality,” Honey told him later when she came home from her unlicensed School for Troubled Tots, dragging along her smallest care-receiver, the appropriately named Tooth Manchipper, who was fastened onto Honey’s right hiking boot with his tiny pink hands and a set of ominous baby teeth. “Sure, I’ve driven over a couple of Bob Johnsons in my day. I’ve even stalked so many ex-boyfriends that I have my own circular file at the FBI. And sure, sometimes my overdosing on fentanyl gets in the way of properly enjoying my overdoses on oxycodone. But inside, I’m just a girly girl who loves lacy pink fabrics and combing the hair of my stuffed unicorn, Freddy. Have you seen Freddy anywhere, Dr. Weinstein? Would you like to help me comb her hair? And as for you, Tooth Manchipper, let’s move those busy teeth of yours from my new hiking boot and onto the leg of that end table, where it might be of better use. As in, say, correcting the wobble?”

It was like waking from one dream of terror into another dream of terror, Dr. Weinstein thought, trying to decide which dream was better–the one occupied by his former cellmate, Diamond Dog Bowie-Brazil, or the one occupied by his former cellmate’s daughter, Honey. Until he met Freddy, of course, and the answer was obvious.

BIGFOOT MON AMOUR

The corpse of Scintilla Jones was easily the kindest, most open-minded and affectionate homo sapiens that Bigfoot had ever met during his long, fraught history with the species. She never made threatening gestures, or pointed at him while uttering words such as “freak,” “monster” and “Oh no! Help!” She never frightened him with flashlight-flaring cameras and video-recording devices. She never complained about his damp, poorly furnished cave like his previous mate, a multi-gender, pronoun-defying silver fox named Hannah Barbara had often done. (“Basically,” Hannah confessed on more than one occasion, “I’ll sleep with anybody, anywhere, and anytime. Amen.”) And she never bored Bigfoot to death with tales of all her previous, unsatisfactory relationships, but remained content to sit in her battered solar-powered wheelchair and allow Bigfoot to stroke her long and still posthumously flourishing gray hair until he fell asleep.

Scintilla, Bigfoot, cave

“Oooga urk urk hunga hunga,” he told her every night as he turned out the light. “Googa googa wood chock!” And Scintilla replied with the same hushed all-accepting silence with which she greeted every gentle moment they spent together.

“They live like gypsies,” Captain Spaulding informed his old NSA buddy, John Bolton, over a pitcher of Light Fulsome Ale between sets at the Drive Shaft Bar and Grill (but Mostly Bar) that operated out of a two car garage in Los Osos. “Bigfoot gets an SSI check every month, which he spends on bright shiny trinkets purchased from the Dollar Store, and Scintilla just does what she’s been doing. Reposes. Happy? Who can define “happy”? They’ve stayed together for several years, through good weather and bad, through fire storms and now two Trump Administrations, and I guess that’s the important part. All I can tell you, buddy, is you should forget all about her; she’s certainly forgotten you–not to mention everything else. And carry on entertaining customers with your… interesting punk band, though maybe you could turn the volume down a notch? In your rendition of “I Wanna Be Your Dog”–especially in your band’s innovative use of galvanized steel garbage can lids–you punctured both my ear drums.”

Ernst Sr. began the formalities–and pretty much ended them: “I am the only world-class super-villain who has yet to be hired by either of the Trump Administrations, and this is my new buddy, Elon, who spends all day firing people, being forced to rehire them by something very annoying called ‘federal law,’ and driving around town in a big iron-gray Tesla truck spray-painted over with crude representations of penises and dickheads. And this is my son, a county judge and former school supervisor who only accepts bribes from his father, even though he’s spent his life resenting my failure to appreciate (and support) his love for musical theater. Okay, son, I get it. I missed your first high-school stage appearance as the title character in ANNIE, but I was robbing Fort Knox at the time, so maybe I had other things on my mind. And as for you girls, I’m guessing you’re…Trixie? And you’re…Tiny? And you’re… well, you’re the red head, so that sort of clinches it. But who’s the zombie, and who’s she supposed to be hooking up with? I don’t recall any zombie profiles when we all met during that single’s party chat on Match.com. And who’s she supposed to be dating–if, that is, we can call this travesty of social awkwardness, by any stretch of the imagination, ‘dating.’”

To which Dr. Tiny Aguilera winsomely replied: “That’s Juliet. And to be blunt, after checking out you three losers, she’s our date tonight–by whom I mean myself, the red-haired former librarian, and Trixie.” To which Juliet added: “Errrrrr.”

59

ANTI-CAPITALISMO

Rejected by love, and by just about every other conceivable human attraction, the unholy triumvirate of Elon Musk, Ernst Blofeld and Ernst Blofeld, Jr., departed shamelessly out the front door of McCarthy’s to encounter the entire assembled order of the Divine Church of Brutal Mercy–Sisters Immaculata, Boniface and Claude Rains. They were climbing down from a brand new four-door large gunmetal gray Ford 150 Lightning truck, wielding bicycle chains, a monkey wrench, and last but not least, a well-used Oswin Hyde umbrella. (“Each piece showcases meticulous attention to detail, from the selection of high-quality fabrics to the elegant handle designs, making them a perfect choice for those who appreciate sophistication in their rainy-day gear.”)

“We’re not your next blind date, boys!” announced Sister Immaculata. “We’re what you’d call mundane, in-your-face, this-worldly justice!” added Sister Boniface. To which Sister Claude Rains concluded: “Geronimo!”

Elon, Blofeld, Blofeld, sisters

Back in the bar, the four now well-unescorted, charmingly-attired young women were definitely girling it up: challenging one another to down shots, debating the merits of capitalism (“It sucks.” “I don’t agree. It’s even suckier than that.”), and flirting with the rough tough guy behind the bar, former local P.I. Clam Hardass. (“I ain’t laid my peepers on a quad of molls this chic since I Betelgeused at a lawn mower’s convention, which was all the green grass I could chomp.”) (No, he didn’t make much sense, but as the girls agreed, the hard-boiled dialogue was fun to misunderstand.) And of course all the young college-age studs (and occasional stud-ettes) drifted by to pay their respects, their homage, and, before the night was over, most of their bar bill. “Who’s the blow-dried blonde?” they asked. (“Trixie Belden.”) “Who’s the older, wiser type with the medical prescription pad?” (“Dr. Tiny Aguilera.) “Who’s the hot red-head?” (“The even hotter-than-she-looks red haired former librarian.”) And finally: “Who’s the zombie?” (To which there was only one, relatively lengthy reply: “Do you mean Juliet, or the former House Minority leader who just came roaring through the front door in that Heavy Duty 4-Wheel Mobility Scooter, Nancy Pelosi?”) To which the young studs and occasional stud-ettes answered: “Both of them! Or either! Take your pick!”

60

COMACETIC

Ever since emerging from a life-threatening coma, former Detective Stud Thunderbolt (who, under the pseudonym of Robbert E. Hinnelleinn, has spent an errant lifetime producing the not-very-famous “Bug Suckler” novels currently being published by Dazed and Confused, Inc.), has developed an increasingly rarefied, piquant taste in literature and the arts–so much so that he often uses words like “rarefied” and “piquant” in polite conversational banter!

“The problem with my crappy “Bug Suckler” novels, which envision Earth’s enslavement by mammary-obsessed insect-aliens from another galaxy, is that they aren’t rarefied or piquant at all, mainly because they’re garbage. Sure, I’ll continue writing those crappy novels since the total proceeds come to a half-way decent lunch at Sal’s Day-Old Shellfish Restaurant every once in a blue moon–and boy do I love day-old shell fish under a blue moon! The other problem is that the world of literature is filled with a lot of blowhards with unearned reputations for greatness. James Joyce? Blowhard. Thomas Mann? Blowhard. Jackie Collins… well, I actually like Jackie Collins, but she’s also a blowhard. The only writers in the history of literature worth reading are Marcel Proust and, well, that’s it. Proust. Not a blowhard. Kind of boring, but he didn’t blow hard at all.”

Stud Thunderbolt and Cthulhu

Stud has recently become a recurring guest on SLO BLOWS, the only locally-produced, public access, arts and literature podcast featuring a Cthulhu as a host. And in order to be a proper host, it’s time for Yasgath Patootie, one of the lesser demonic entities appearing regularly on NewsMax, to hold up Stud’s recently published-to-hardly-any-acclaim paperback, Bug Sucklers Take Their Meds. “It’s got bugs!” Yasgath intones mercilessly, striking chill fear into anybody foolish enough to tune into this endless arts show. “It’s got suckling! Most of all, it’s got suckling bugs! Available from any local hardware or home improvement store since it got accidentally shipped out with some cheap Japanese box-cutters as ballast! Go get your copy and enjoy many piquant, rarefied hours of pleasures now!”

61

THE NEVER-ENDING DIMINISHING SPIRAL

“The universe,” Druid-in-Chief Rutger Hauer explained to Bob at a recent Illuminati wine-mixer, “is a never ending diminishing spiral towards total conformity and death–but only if we’re lucky. I mean, if the universe wound down to its lowest common denominator and we didn’t die, we’d never enjoy the opportunity of being reborn as someone splendid, such as Adam Weishaupt, hunkin’ Jeff Bezos, or Katy Perry. And if the universe spiraled outward in the other direction, there’d be complete chaos, increasing non-conformity, and did I mention the chaos part? Everybody’d be wearing a completely different hat–and we couldn’t distinguish between the MAGA ones, the SF Giants ones, and our much nobler white pointy hoods! Can you imagine how impossible it would be to establish peaceful table placement charts at dinner parties? I don’t think you could. You wouldn’t know who to trust and who not to trust. And the ones to trust, of course, are the ones wearing pointy white hoods. And the ones not to trust are the ones wearing everything else.”

Druid Zombie and Bob

The night’s keynote speaker is Zombie Joe Biden, who began by soliciting campaign funds for his eventual primary campaign to be re-elected as America’s second deadest president. (The title of first deadest president, of course, Biden “nailed down” in his first term.) At last word, Biden and Kamala Harris have established the country’s largest campaign bankrolls and the fewest potential votes among all prospective candidates–dead or alive. Which, of course, makes them a pair of shoe-ins at the DNC (Dead National Convention) in 2027!

Zombie Biden has just finished a large glass of embalming fluid before he moves into the intermediate part of his speech (the one sandwiched between long rambling solicitations for money.) He says: “I stand here. Dead. In sunglasses. I’m dead. I’m the president. No, cancel that. I’m the dead ex president. Who can tell? The difference? That’s me. I’m a survivor. In a dead way of speaking. We have to save this country. From the fascists. Dead or alive. They are much worse. Than we are. Because they aren’t dead. Sometimes they are dead. Sometimes they’re not. How you doing there, honey? You–blondie in the front row. You’re adorable. My name’s Joe. They call me Corn Pop! That’s me. Dead. Joe. Where’s my son? I want. To see. My son. Is this thing on? I’m hungry. Is there anything left. Of Diane Feinstein? Great girl. Gotta love that Feinstein. She’s dead but that doesn’t stop. Her. No sireebob. That’s another thing. Being dead doesn’t stop me from saying, ‘Nosireebob.’ No-siree. Bob!” (Which was the last thing Bob Johnson remembered hearing before he fell asleep in his folding chair.)

62

GIGILO BOB

Trixie Belden knows who she wants to vote for at the next presidential election (if the country lasts long enough to have one), and that would have to be Zombie Joe Biden–mainly because he singled her out in the crowd at the last Illuminati Wine Mixer. “He called me ‘adorable,’ which is, of course, true, but that doesn’t mean it still isn’t nice to hear it sometimes. He also told those cute little stories about waking up long enough to take a nap, and how good he’ll feel after the next election even if he loses, since he’ll have tried his best and that’s all that counts. Don’t you think he’s right, Bob? Isn’t doing the best we can all we can ask from ourselves? Then it’s certainly all we can ask for from Zombie Joe Biden, don’t you think?”

Trixie was easily the best looking woman who had ever sat down at a public table with Bob who didn’t pass out within minutes of their first drink. Sometimes they passed out from the drinks they had drunk before they sat down with Bob, and at other times they fell asleep from the mind altering chemicals they had dosed themselves with before agreeing to sit down with Bob. But most of the time they only sat down with Bob long enough to realize that he was sitting down next to them and then, like any smart girl, they either passed out or got the hell out of there.

Trixie and Bob

“You’re probably just misunderstood,” Trixie said, when the subject of their conversation came around, very briefly, to Bob. “I certainly know it’s easy for me to misunderstand you. Still, I find something faintly alluring about your white pointy hood, especially when it covers half your face and… there, let me just adjust that a little… that’s better. You’re even more alluring when your hood covers that rather gigantic nostril of yours. In fact, with just enough work and perhaps a lot of expensive cosmetic surgery, you wouldn’t be half-bad looking at all. Or maybe you’re already just half bad enough looking as it is, like a half full glass is better than a half empty glass–does that make any sense, Bob? I think I just confused myself. What have I been drinking? I’m surprised I didn’t pass out. Would you like to meet my Comp Professor, Zombie Juliet? I’m not proposing a threesome or anything (you wish), but I like her and I like you (I think) and that means you might like each other. In the meantime, let’s order another drink, and I promise not to pass out until I tell you my whole life story. Doesn’t that sound fun?”

63

TRIXIE’S LIFE STORY (OR, “JUST THE FACTS, MA’AM”)

The “whole life story” Trixie related to Bob on their first accidental date (when they sat down at the same table by mistake) went like this: Born in Bel Air to a Nasa engineer and a Uruguayan trapeze artist named Kitty “No Net” Cinderella, Trixie had triumphed through pre-school, triumphed through grammar school, and triumphed through high-school–when she had fallen for the school’s football hero (Blackjack “Nightstick” Hawthorne) the same day her mother fell from a fifty foot high-wire in Montevideo where she had been performing in South America’s version of “Circus of the Stars” with Antonio Banderas. Suddenly–“No-Net” Cinderella was “No-Net” Cinderella no more. “I cried,” Trixie recalled. “My dad cried. Our dog cried. The city cried. Even our President at the time, Generalissimo Motors, cried, though he was probably thinking about his retirement funds, since the government currency tanked at exactly the same time. Everything was falling, it seemed. But me, Trixie Belden. I just kept rising from one success to another.”

Trixie won hearts

Trixie won scholarships. Trixie won hearts. Sometimes she won hearts and scholarships simultaneously, and many of the elderly donors who presented her with large checks followed her home immediately afterwards, issuing frantic proposals of marriage, and often succumbing to their fatal heartbreaks on her rose-petal-bedecked front porch. “I love you, Trixie!” the elderly, grayly-mustachioed men shouted, clutching desperately at their overloaded chests (both literally and figuratively). “I want to send you to graduate school! I want to leave you my estates! I’m too young to die, Trixie! Please call 911! I’m too young to die!”

But of course, even when Trixie called 911, they tended to die anyway. Except for the most recent one–Reginald Smythe Girl-Masher III–who, these days, woke periodically from his long-standing coma at French Hospital to shout: ”You saved me, Trixie! Now you must marry me!” Before promptly lapsing back into his coma.

64

BOB’S NIGHT OF TRIUMPH!

It was the shortest, most thrilling date of Bob’s life, and it happened in full view of everyone who had been disparaging him all his life for his manifest failure to enjoy any thrilling dates of any description with anybody. (In other words, anybody who had ever met, been told about, or even surmised the existence of someone like Bob.)

His ex-wife, the renowned Goth-Gothic novelist, Cassandra Knye, had come waltzing through the front door (literally, she was waltzing!) in the strong robust arms of Jorge Vallente Jr., the son of her deceased flamenco instructor, just in time to see Bob ordering a fresh round of drinks–which definitely wiped the waltz off her feet. (“Who’s that attractive young woman sitting with Bob, and why hasn’t she passed out already?”) Several well-indicted and well-rehired by the Trump Administration partners at Charlie, Berkowitz, Charlie, Charlie & Charlie (don’t ask me which, I can’t tell them apart), looked up from their morose cocktails at the bar long enough to wonder–“Why would any woman that attractive choose a loser like Bob over any or all of us?” And even Bob’s grandma, Monumental Li, showed up looking for a bar without her husband in it to find that an unconscionable event had graduated to the level of the improbably actual to see in her grandson sitting at the same table with an attractive woman who hadn’t yet passed out. “What’s loser like him doing with pretty girl like her? And don’t let your grandpa see her, Bob! It get him all excited until he start pawing my apples and cumquats, and I ain’t talking ‘bout the backyard garden, neither!”

Trixie, Bob, man on gurney

In fact, the only person who didn’t show up during their historic date finally showed up just as they were leaving–and that was, of course, the obscenely wealthy local obsessor about young attractive women, Reginald Smythe Girl-Masher III, hooked up to a couple of glass bottles and riding a stainless steel gurney all the way from French Hospital, where no coma could keep him from professing his passionate adoration of Trixie. “I love you, Trixie!” He shouted huskily through his various respirators. “I want to marry you, Trixie! I’ve got loads of cash, Trixie! Please, whatever you do, don’t let me die on this crummy gurney alone!”

65

THE DATING GAME REPRISED

It’s spring in San Luis Obispo, which means a) love is in the air! b) everybody’s hearts have turned to romance! and c) the tax penalty bills and rebate checks have started arriving! And so Stevie Nicks, the central coast’s loneliest vulture, has invented a delightful new way to spend her mornings–by playing her own version of The Dating Game on a bus bench outside Sunshine Donuts with three (as they smelled to her) eligible bachelors.

Stevie, Tex Mex, Grandpa, Frankie

Pulling a black velvet hood over her head (liberated from the trash bin of none other than the now amorously-occupied Honey Brazil), she perched on the back of the splintering bus bench and sniffed down curiously at three invisible (to her) potential dates: Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee, Bob Johnson’’s Grandpa, and Frankie Laine Gotcha (a.k.a. the new improved Zorro.) “Bachelor number one,” Stevie whispered huskily, to inspire her potential dates with romantic anticipation, “if the title of any popular movie described your love making, what would it be?” “Child’s Play Two,” Tex Mex drawled seductively. “And Bachelor number two, same question.” “Child’s Play Four: The Bride of Chucky!” Bob’s Grandpa shouted, hoping that somebody out there beyond his deafness and enormous wide-ranging blind spot might be listening. “And Bachelor number three, if you were to take me to the scene of your favorite romance, where would that be, and what would we be doing there!” To which Frankie Laine Gotcha joyfully replied: “The peak of Mt. Etna during a violent eruption! And what do you think we’d be doing? We’d be bolo-dancing!”

But Stevie has always been more of a non-verbal sort of person, and she makes her selection not on the quality of their answers, but on the texture of their aromas. Bachelor number one smells like extra hot chili stirred with the rancid corpse of a frog. Bachelor number two smells like day old canned chili poured over the rancid corpse of a raccoon. And Bachelor number three doesn’t smell rancid at all… why is that? “How can I feel drawn to someone who smells so undesirable…” she thinks out loud. “And why can’t I choose anybody but you, number three! Come on down! Or better yet, come up here onto the back of this bus bench! We’re going on an all-expenses paid holiday to where, Jim Lange? Tell us what we’ve won!”

66

THE SECRET HISTORY OF SAN LUIS OBISPO 2.1: THE SPIRIT OF SAN LUIS

One of the many things people don’t know about Bob’s part of the world (or perhaps once knew but then forgot) is that the world famous aviator, Charles Lindbergh, didn’t bequeath his famous plane to the Smithsonian, where a cheap plastic replica has been dishonestly displayed as the “real thing” for more than a century. Rather he flew it to San Luis Obispo on a foggy night, while drunk to the gills on cheap champagne (Charles) and wearing nothing but a smile (the airplane.)

It’s what’s known as a “meat and potatoes” type restaurant, or so it’s described by Reginald Noseworthy, chief culinary critic on SLO BLOWS, the central coast’s only public access, nightly cultural arts program hosted by a Cthulhu. “That means they serve meat and potatoes for breakfast, meat and potatoes for lunch, and meat and potatoes for dinner–when they’re open for dinner, that is.” Reginald visited the central coast in the mid-fifties when he was fleeing persecution by people with “traditional opinions about food” (such as those “fresh greens and vegetables” zealots who populated his home town of San Francisco), and once he smelled the weekend patio barbecues, decided to stay for good. “My favorite is their meat and potatoes green bean salad, their meat and potatoes cherry pie, and their meat and potatoes leek and potato soup. Also, if you get a seat by the window, you can watch the airplanes come and go, and occasionally, you’ll even see Amelia Earhart sitting at the bar nursing one of their meat and potatoes dry martinis. It just goes to show you that meat and potatoes aren’t so bad for you as some posers–and by that I mean Bay Area posers–falsely claim.” Reginald delivers his bi-monthly “Report from the Food Front” on alternate Tuesdays, just after the host, Yasgath Patootie, gives his opening monolog (“So you seen these new baby basters they’re selling out at Cthulhu’s ‘R’” Us? Boy, they’re really something…”) and just before the Druid-Tabernacle Choir sings that week’s Bach cantata.

Lindbergh and Earhart

“The rumors of many deaths are greatly exaggerated, but maybe fabricated is more like it!” the host and chef, Charles Lindbergh, often shouts at his customers while showing them to a table. “Mine, Amelia’s, Mark Twain’s!” He usually wears a striped flannel shirt, gray dungarees, and an over-large MAGA hat that hangs down low enough to cover his alarming eyebrows. “That’s because they don’t want to protect our country from everybody who opposes its staunch moral values–and by that I mean every other country! Now sit here, keep your mouths shut, and I’ll send over your waitress. You’ll know me as your waitress by my ocean-blue raw-silk blouse, my dancing shoes, and my mittens! And enjoy these meat and potato breadsticks while you’re waiting! They’re on the house!”

67

CHILDLY PRODIGIOUS

Tooth Manchipper is the most-wanted toddler in San Luis Obispo County. A few weeks shy of his second birthday, he’s wanted in suspicion of grand larceny, assault, armed assault, wearing cloth diapers without a license, more assault, attempted murder, attempted grand larceny, grand theft auto, armed aggravated assault, attempted armed aggravated assault, destruction of federal property, and several DUIs that have gone to warrant, been forgotten about by the increasingly elderly and nap-prone SLOPD, and then gone to warrant again. “He’s a rambunctious little sod,” his parents, Hendrix and Beverly Manchipper informed Honey Brazil, on the day they dropped him off at her unlicensed Day-Care for Troublesome Toddlers out in Reservoir Canyon. “Now look, here’s our credit card, just wear the damn thing out. We’re off to Skagway and won’t be back unless Tooth here finds us, and we’re not about to let that happen. Just give him plenty of table-legs to gnaw, a meal every few days or so, and a bowl of water in his cage. Oh, you don’t use cages around here? Well, it’s your funeral. Ciao!” Very occasionally, Tooth receives a postcard that, through various circumlocutions, his parents manage to send postmarked from places they aren’t–Manhattan Beach, Panama City, Munich, Bengal. The postcards carry indelible images of cities very, very far away from Tooth’s teeth, and say the same thing: “Glad you’re not here, our little Manchipper! Please don’t harm your day-care supervisor, Honey Brazil! She’s the only day-care supervisor we’ve got!”

Not that little Tooth hasn’t tried. He’s tried gnawing chair legs out from under her. He’s tried gnawing bedposts out from under her. He’s even tried gnawing through the floor of her rickety aluminum-sided van/mobile (not very) apartment and pulling her off into the woods like a badger with a house cat. But everywhere he tries to gnaw, Honey already seems to be somewhere else entirely–lately, of course, in the company of her only inamorata that really mattahs, Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation.)

Honey, Dr. Harvey, Tooth Manchipper

Sometimes she drove him to the beach where they roasted skewers of unidentifiable (sale-priced) meat over a public barbecue. Sometimes they watched super hero movies outside at the Sunset Drive-In, cuddled up in the bed of Honey’s old truck with a keg of warm ale and an ice-box full of slightly melted Dippin Dots and pound sacks of beef jerky. “It doesn’t matter where we are,” Honey said every night before they did whatever it was they did that Honey called “making love.” “It just matters that we don’t have to worry about that little bully, Tooth Manchipper!” To which Harvey always replied: “It’s hard to crack these pistachio shells with these zip ties on my wrists. Not that I’m complaining, mind you. It’s just something I wanted to share.”

68

DR MABUSE–LITTLE LEAGUE COACH

The international spy, psychic parasite and arch criminal would do anything for his child-like gang of thugs, hoods and accomplices–even agree to coach their local little league team, the Los Osos Ringworms, for the spring P.A.L. (Police Athletic League.) And this notwithstanding the fact that Dr. Mabuse hates baseball, green parks, fresh air, hot dogs, popcorn, candy cane, and just about anything associated with America’s favorite pastime (next to weapons manufacturing, weapons dispersal and weapons deployment). Oh, and kids! Dr. Mabuse hates anything associated with kids!

“Run him down!” Dr. Mabuse shouts from the third base sideline, as his thuggish first string catcher, Rocko, goes barreling into second base. “Slide, slide, slide! And don’t forget your cleats!” he screams at his lean, mean shortstop, Fantomas, who goes into third base like a gigantic manta ray attacking a clam. “And you, Cy Sperling! Just run down that pathetic little catcher like a southbound train! He’s guarding the plate! He’s hardly a foot tall! His uniform doesn’t even fit! Run him down, Cy Sperling! And don’t lose your marvelous toupee while you’re at it!” And, as always, Dr. Mabuse’s henchmen and henchwomen (such as Vampirella Delgado, warming up in the bullpen) run amok on the little league field like rhinoceri at an orgy! OUT goes little six year old Betty Fiddlesticks, spinning into the blue sky like some spinning-thing. OUT goes little seven year old Joey Davenport at third, spattered with his own cleat-stricken blood like a victim of Poe’s “Red Death.” And now it’s the turn of Cy Sperling who comes thundering down the third base line towards a lone tiny tot–the only thing standing between him and home base! Run, you little bastard! he thinks. Run, run! For your life, you little twerp! For your bloody life!

Tooth Manchipper stands his ground

But of course the tiny tot doesn’t run. He doesn’t even blink. He just stands there in his onesie, wielding a glove bigger than his head, and baring a set of razor-sharp teeth out of an orthodontist’s nightmare. And stands his ground like only little Tooth Manchipper can!

69

THE POST-GAME WRAP-UP

“He was a ringer!” Dr. Mabuse consoles his weeping and broken kids during their post-game “wrap up” at French Hospital, where they were all, in turn, being wrapped up for their various contusions and lacerations by the centenarian head of the Emergency Room, Nurse Gladiola Glockenspiel. “That means they brought him in from off-campus, which is a clear violation of the rules. That kid doesn’t even go to school let alone belong to a school team. He’s wanted on dozens of federal counts of extortion, assault, aggravated assault, assault with intent to humiliate, mandibular destruction of public property, mandibular destruction of federal property, bank fraud, and various types of heretofore unspecified assault. Just don’t get me started on the assault charges against that little booger! Now, man up, Cy Sperling! Man up, Fantomas! And you, too, Rocko; you man-up as well. We’re going up against next week’s team with the same cold calculating criminal intent as we approach any of our nefarious enterprises, and we’re not letting one psychopathic little tyke named Tooth Manchipper make us lose our oomph! Right, team? Have we got our oomph? Let me hear you say yeah! We’ve got our oomph!”

Nurse, team, Tooth Manchipper

“We’ve got our oomph! We’ve got our oomph!”

“That’s the spirit, boys and girls! Now let me check our schedule and see who we’ve got on the agenda next week… next week is a Saturday… we’re meeting in Sinsheimer Park... the school… the school… maybe it’s a misprint? Anyway, it says right here that the opposing team comes from the grammar school of Our Sisters of Brutal Mercy in Los Osos? And oh… oh crap. Oh crap crap crap! Their starting pitcher is that goddamn Tooth Manchipper! Waaaaaahhh!”

70

SINS OF OMISSION

Gladiola often calls her estranged husband, Bob’s grandpa, but he never calls back. She knows he’s been “living in sin” with his ex-wife, Monumental Li, but he’s been doing it without the sin part, for which she can only be relieved. Committing “sin” with someone as old and unhealthy as Bob’s grandpa (especially when you were as old as either Gladiola or Monumental Li) was too unpleasant to talk about, let alone imagine.

Monumental and Grandpa

“It your wife!” Monumental Li shouted at Bob’s grandpa who, to prove that the tree never falls far from the acorn, has recently taken up the habit of sleeping on a fold-out cot in Monumental Li’s basement. “She claim she need to see you sort out tax situation on condo, and I think getting you out of basement even for few hours have to be big improvement.”

“I’m not saying I want you back,” Gladiola, from her end of the phone, tells the dead air that, according to Monumental Li, is Bob Johnson’s grandpa listening on the other end. “But if you’re not ready to help with the property taxes, then I need to start thinking about renting out the guest room, and the only individual who replied to my ad says she knows you? She put you down as a reference anyway. She’s a single-vulture whose name is Stevie Nix and I’m thinking of taking her with only a minimal deposit, mainly since she strikes me as very clean. She’s always preening her feathers, and never leaves the streets messy after she eats. There’s not a lot I ask from people or animals in these crazy times, but for now, those two things may have to do.”

71

YO YO MA’S MA MA

One of the biggest problems Monumental Li has faced living in San Luis Obispo (and this is one-quarter true for her grandson, Bob Johnson) is that, in the absence of any other Asian faces in the entire city, she misses all the things that once made her enjoy being Asian. She misses decent Chinese food, of course. She misses Mahjong and getting angry at the men in her life for playing too much ping pong. She misses spending hours in a hair salon getting massaged, clipped, tingled and fretted by attractive young men and women who only charged a few yen an hour. But most of all, she misses the company of other tiger grandmoms to make her feel like less of a bitch. Which was why she was so relieved when a familiarly Asian-looking face moved in next door to her condo, one belonging to none other than Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma.

Monumental, Ma Ma, Bob

“Practice, you lazy bastard!” I kept telling him. “Clean your room and mow the lawn! Varnish your cello, practice your lessons, go to lessons, and mow the lawn! There was no end to the things I had to tell that goodfornothing kid! And when he grew up to become famous, do you think he ever send me a mother’s day card? No. No cards. No phone calls. No nothing! You’d think he resented his mama for taking so much time out of her life to tell him what to do! Every so often he sends me tickets to one of his boring concerts and I have to sit there for like ninety minutes while he sits on stage holding his cello with the sort of affection he never showed his mom, no matter how hard I tried to nag him! And then he tells these stories, these boring stories!About his crummy childhood and how his tiger mom kept bossing him around, and then he starts giving audience advice! ‘Be good to one another!’ ‘Love children!’ ‘Support arts education!’ ‘Watch PBS!’ Where’d he learn to give people unwanted advice if not from his tiger mom? Boy, are his concerts boring! It make me so mad sometimes I go home and order food from only halfway decent Chinese restaurant in San Luis Obispo, and we’re talking of course about Panda Express. And that of course when I start crying alone in my new condo–the moment I realize only halfway decent Chinese restaurant in all of SLO is Panda Express! What has my life come to, Monumental Li? And why can’t I find a way out of it?”

Often, Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma comes over and sits with Monumental Li on the back deck, where they take turns spraying forever chemicals at the various bugs and critters that come wandering up from the creek. The back deck, with its dying plants and collapsed dead insects and critters, resembles the realm of Sauron in those endless “Lord of the Rings” movies Bob Johnson had made his grandmother watch with him as a child. “Oh the heavens please save us from Panda Express and ‘Lord of the Rings’!” Monumental Li moans loudly to her new friend outside on the back deck. “And from either ungrateful sons who never come to visit, or ungrateful grandsons who never stop!”

Faculty lounge

THE SECRET HISTORY OF SAN LUIS OBISPO 2.2: THE IRISH HILLS

Many visitors ask: “What makes the Irish Hills so Irish, and here’s a hint–it’s not their drinking! Some genuine similarities include: a) They like to wear green, b) they’re unusually chatty at bus stops, c) their girls have green eyes and they’re always smiling, d) they have learned to hate leprechauns (Let’s face it, they’re little bastards!) e) they leave stupid public displays of alcoholism on St. Patrick’s Day to everyone who isn’t Irish, f) they are always searching in vain for 1000 level sun block at their local CVSes, and g) they never, never get involved with parades.

The Irish Hills emigrated to the east coast of the United States shortly after the clover epidemic of 1832, and later hitched a ride west with the Naughty Forty Niners (led by their nasty pater familias, Rapscallion T. Underpants-Niner.) When they hit the central coast, the central coast hit them–with its splendiferous beaches, coral-pink sunsets, and lazily laid-back communities of brown and golden bears. (“How’s it hangin, Irish Hills? Feel like a pizza?”) In fact, the Irish Hills thought they could live here forever, and sent occasional checks home to their family in Connemara with a briefly scrawled note attached: “Come west, brothers and sisters! The central coast is where we were meant to be–not to mention the pizza!”

Irish Hills

But the best-laid plans don’t remain best-laid for very long, and only a few weeks into the second Trump Administration, they received notice that their green cards weren’t being renewed. “In fact, to be blunt,” shouted Captain Spaulding, the new assistant-in-training to succeed anybody who was summarily fired-amidst-scandal from any federal department involved with immigration, finances, law, governmental standards and justice, “your status is being revoked! That’ll teach you to say smart-ass things about our commander-in-chief on Facebook!” Which struck the Irish Hills as very hard to digest. Facebook? They asked themselves. Who the hell still uses Facebook?

Caitlin and children

Trixie, Bob, picnic

Trixie, Bob, picnic over

OLD KOOT

Koot Hoomi was the million year old-trans celestial personality who had been driving California divinity-hood since there was a California, and he had no plans of leaving just yet. Residing in the stone pyramid of Oddfellows Cemetery with his sister, his ex-wife, and several thousand ungrateful progeny who didn’t seem ready to move out and start lives of their own, Koot was known to the local theosophical communities as wise, benevolent, hard of hearing, a really bad flash-dancer, a random provider of free discount movie coupons, and the arranger of well-attended Medicare Advantage lecture-dinners at the Madonna Inn, where he successfully sold thousands of healthy Social Security recipients on how great it would be to spend their life savings on private medical plans run by the good people at UnitedHealth. Which is not to say that Koot was the greatest neighbor anyone in San Luis Obispo could hope for.

For one thing, while Koot didn’t mind living near the mess and spiritual uncleanliness of Bob Johnson’s life–he could really do without the smell. First there was just the eye-watering stink of Bob Johnson’s oil-burning ‘93 Plymouth Sundance ragtop driving back and forth on South Higuera making THC deliveries; and then, to make matters worse, there was the car’s interior odoriffic chaos of old sandwiches, mouse droppings, moldering sushi–and how old was that half-finished milk shake on the dashboard, anyway? If it really was a milkshake? Koot wanted to see the best in these messier human avatars such as Bob, since they were all preparing to embark on the same endless journey towards universal perfection that Koot had himself completed sometime during the first Trump Administration.

Bob, car, Koot

“I thought maybe going on a couple of accidental dates with a winsome, unusually attractive young woman such as Trixie Belden might put Bob on the road to a halfway decent reincarnation decision at our next C.O.A. (Cosmos-Owners Association) Board meeting, but no such luck. If Bob even makes it back to human status again after centuries of being stalled at the “deeply embarrassing” rung of the ladder, I’d be surprised. Personally, I think he should be demoted to one of the mice currently living underneath the floorboards of his Sundance, but I keep getting outvoted by my arch nemesis on the Board, the eternally-recurring spiritual essence of Rapscallion T. Underpants, the naughtiest of the Niner Fortyniners (and how!)” But then, possessing eternal wisdom, as Koot had often decided, wasn’t as much fun as it sounded. On some days, in fact, it wasn’t any fun at all.

MRS. HOOMI

Even though Koot Hoomi (one of San Luis Obispo’s–and the world’s–most eternally transcendent secret masters) is many millions of years old, his mother never forgets his birthday, and always manages to find him something special. “Instead of the normal fifty dollar book token for Bookshop.org, I thought you needed something to brighten up your three bedroom condo in the high Himalayan Mountains, so I got you this baby rose bush. Isn’t it beautiful? It’s called ‘Midnight Fire,’ which is pretty appropriate for the all-knowing master of time, space and dimension. Now give your old mama a big hug and I’ll go make your favorite dessert–chocolate cream pie!”

Koot knows his adorably devoted old mother is lying. Not about the name of the rose bush, but about the false sense she communicates of unwavering pride in the only career choice he ever made. “A lawyer, a doctor, or a really talented gardener,” she advised him many millions of times more than many millions of years ago. “Somebody whose knowledge most people can’t do without. For example, your uncle Mohammed was a really great lawyer, who specialized in getting criminals switched from one really awful capital punishment, such as having your limbs chopped off one by one, to a much less awful one, such as being drowned in a camel trough. Your other uncle Mohammed was a successful heart specialist who advised the emperor on the easiest way to sacrifice victims on the Altar of Pain, and your final uncle Mohammed owned a green grocer. Now, if you really want to sit around cross-legged on a cold linoleum floor chanting a lot of mumbo jumbo, or fly around the mountains in your Chariot of Divine Power looking for your freeloading friends such as Annie Besant and Krishnamurti, well, there’s nothing I can do to stop you. And whatever decision you make, I’m your mother and I’ll always love you. (Though I gotta admit, son, I would love you a whole lot more if you were a doctor!)”

Diamond Dog and Mrs. Hoomi

Mrs. Hoomi lost her first husband to a lightening storm, her second husband to a multi-raft collision on the Yangtze, her third husband to another lightening storm, her fourth husband to a ritual sacrifice, her fifth… another lightening storm… well, she lost a lot of husbands, that’s all we’re saying. Until, of course, she met the love of her current millennium, the plein-air master of sunset hues and memorable tinctures, Diamond Dog Bowie-Brazil. “Get off my goddamn lap you undying, prune-faced old witch!” Diamond Dog often shouted into her good ear. “I’m reading this really cool article in Outdoor Painter on ‘How to Master Acrylics. I swear, you old bats can’t seem to get enough of a felonious ex-con scoundrel and two-time California Plein Air Jury Award Winner such as myself, and while I don’t mind paying my rent around here, lady, I’d much rather be making art than making love! Especially when it means making love to a prune-faced old witch like yourself!”

I was the peeperest of peepers on the central clamshell, with action both coming and rowing, or my name ain’t Clam Hardass, private dick. I could also munch the lingo with the best of them, making me prime rib for the prime rib lovers, including myself. Her name was Violet Fondue, and she was a long time maker of the dog chow with her least favorite (and sole) owner, Ernst Blofeld, international crime syndicate honcho and current bestest-buddy of Elon Musk, but this was way back in time when the latter was a space satellite and the former was a recovering dad with delusions of grandpadom. Clam and Violet

“I think he’s planning to murder his wife,” Violet told me, settling her doggy haunch down on the doggy bed I used to keep on the office floor in case of sudden companionship. “He also plans to murder his son, me, his cat, Sonny Bono, the entire population of California, the nation, the world, stop me if you’ve heard this one…” A soft glaze was wandering across the babe’s peepers as if she had just mulched what she wanted to munch. “That’s because that’s what evil geniuses do, or my name ain’t Violet Fondue.” Which was when I replied: “I getcha, honey. Or my name ain’t Hardass. Clam Hardass.” And she replied to my reply: “Fondue. Violet Fondue.” And so forth. It just got too hard keeping up with the private eye lingo, is how I see it. However much I could munch. It was just too much!

WHAT DOESN’T STAY IN VEGAS

What happens in Vegas stays in Vegas, with the obvious exception of Bob Johnson, who went to Vegas, lost his wallet in Vegas (don’t worry–he didn’t have any money in it), got thrown out of two bars and a high end hot pot restaurant in Vegas, slept at the airport in Vegas, found his wallet again in Vegas (not a big deal–there wasn’t any money in it), and didn’t go on his third date with the too-adorable-for-Bob Trixie Belden in Vegas. “I didn’t even plan to be here but my city bus took a wrong turn on Tank Farm Road,” Trixie told him over a pair of matching cobalt blue and cherry-red Mai Tais. “By the way, did you know we have all-electric rapid transit in SLO, Bob? It’s one of the reasons I love our little city. That and the weather.”

Trixie and Bob in Vegas

Bob and Trixie had found themselves accidentally sitting at the same table in one of the Palazzo’s most expensive restaurants, the Mauna Loa Boa-boa, an all-Tahitian bar and grill which featured live boa constrictors running around on the floors and through the branches of overhead plastic trees, not to mention the 24-7 surround-screen, surround-sound footage of volcanos erupting. “This huli-huli chicken is really special,” Bob replied, wiping his lips with one of the hand-painted-with-orchids linen napkins. “And that’s coming from a guy who doesn’t even know what huli-huli- chicken is.” Every woman who passed their table complimented Trixie on her earrings; every man who passed their table couldn’t take his eyes off Trixie’s bared-by-a floral-patterned-sarong’s thighs. Meanwhile she was informing Bob: “It’s not that I don’t like you, or find you attractive, Bob; which, in both cases, I can honestly say I don’t. It’s just that you’re too old for me, too-many-times-divorced for me, too lost without me for me, and if it weren’t for the fact that I hit a weird jackpot that required we dine together in order to cash in twenty thousand dollars worth of chips, you’re too broke to afford a decent dinner with me. Oh, by the way, that boa constrictor just ran off with one of your mangoes. Do you want me to wrestle him to the ground and get it back? Or would you be happy just to ask the waitress for another mango? Please choose the second one, Bob. I’d really like to just sit here and enjoy my Mai Tai.”

It was probably the best holiday Bob could remember being on. And when his bus to the airport took a wrong turn at Harrah’s and dropped him off in front of his condo in Laguna Lake, he decided it was also the only holiday he had ever been tricked by fate into enjoying. “They didn’t even ask me for any I.D.,” he told his grandpa, who had fallen asleep on Bob’s fold-out cot in the garage. “Mainly since I didn’t have any when I arrived, so they didn’t need to see any when I left. So much for that Real ID the DMV ripped me off for. Since if there’s one person who doesn’t need a real ID in this increasingly crazy world, it would have to be me.”

“I know I should probably leave him,” Ernst’s devoted pet, Violet Fondue, confessed to her canine boyfriend, Butch Leavenworth, over a shared plate of pasta primavera at Stan’s Day Old Shellfish Restaurant on Monterey Street. “But that’s easier said than done. Sorry, Butch, I can’t seem to stop talking about my problems, and here you’ve taken me to share this romantic meal at our town’s most popular (with dogs) new restaurant. So now it’s your turn, Butch. Tell me something about yourself. Especially about this lovely meal. Should we order more chianti? How’s your side of the pasta primavera? You certainly look like you’e enjoying it, anyway.”

Butch paused long enough to lick a chunk of shrimp from his grizzly lips with a satisfied smack. “Really smelly!” he tells her. “How about yours?”
