ELON’S FIRST MONOLOGUE

In his latest effort at world-domination/evil-empire building/world annihilation, international super-criminal Ernst Blofeld has bankrolled a nightly syndicated talk show starring his latest bestest bud, Elon Musk, featuring an endless opening monologue written, produced, and extemporaneously performed by that selfsame bestest bud, Elon Musk. The home audience can’t get enough of it! Or at least they aren’t allowed to, since it is beamed by Starlink directly onto their TV screens, and if they try to turn away for one moment, they are strapped to their Barcaloungers and fitted with eyelid-restraining metal contraptions like Alex in A Clockwork Orange. Tonight’s monologue (and pretty much the substance of all monologues to follow) went a little (or a lot) like this:

Elon speaks

“Good evening! I’m very clever! I invented lots of things! Or at least I bought lots of people who invented lots of things! I have lots of money! I earned every penny of it by being very clever and buying lots of people! I went into space. I came back. Then I uploaded my very clever brain into a computer and launched it into space. Many people think this is the best idea I ever had! But it wasn’t, since I eventually came back down again, and that was a really good idea too! And now I’m making up this monologue as I go along! Can you tell? I can’t. It seems to be getting beamed right into my mouth by an extraterrestrial super race, like in Philip K Dick’s VALIS! Have you ever seen me and VALIS in the same room at the same time? Of course not! So what’s the deal about gender? Why can’t people be happy with the genders given to them by Mother Nature? Not Transgender Mom/Pop Nature but MOTHER nature! Just leave your private parts where you found them. Like my penis. I love my penis! I love impregnating women with my penis! It’s lots of fun and makes good financial sense too! I need my penis a lot so I can produce lots of babies who can wait on me at the end of the world in my subterranean polar city that I’m building. I wouldn't give up my penis for anything. Using my penis is both a hobby and a vocation! Did I say I love my penis! So go ahead, draw big pictures of it on the sides of all my Tesla trucks! It looks good! Just like my penis! Having a baby look up at you with eyes filled with wonder at my amazingness is the best part of fatherhood! It goes rapidly downhill after that! Did I tell you about tonight’s musical guests? Katy Perry. And her friend, secret master of the universe, Koot Hoomi. Not to mention Mrs. Hoomi and Jon Voight! Jon Voight won the Medal of Freedom! I’m going to win the Medal of Freedom too! It only costs a billion dollars or something. Now, for another monologue! Are your eyelids burning yet? Tell me when they are and I’ll start the next monologue after that! I’m very clever! Stay tuned! We’ll be right back and we’re never going away! Yay for me! Yay for me! Yay for me!”

In the studio audience, you could hear a pin drop. Shortly after which, one of the mice who wandered over from Bob Johnson’s car whispers to another mouse: ”Did you hear that pin drop? I’m pretty sure it’s mine.”

BAD DAY AT BLACK ROCK

All over the world (but especially at “ground zero” in San Luis Obispo) people aren’t sleeping. Nightmarish images of Elon talking about how funny and clever he is haunt their dreams, their waking hours, and all the liminal spaces in between. Images of his penis sketched on the doors of iron gray Tesla trucks dance in their heads like sugar plums. And even when they finally fall asleep each night, after only a few moments of relief, they almost always wake up screaming.

Bob drinks with Dewboy

“I don’t know,” Bob Johnson confesses to his drinking buddy, Dewboy Fairchild, splashing their pint glasses full from the latest pitcher of Margaritas. “I kind of like him. I don’t see what all the fuss is about. He loves his penis. He’s really clever. More important, he has loads of money, which is sort of funny in itself. The part I don’t get is the bit about how much he loves impregnating women, which sounds messy. I never managed to pull off the trick myself except, of course, hypothetically.”

Dewboy is currently between girl friends, dogs, functioning automobiles, and jobs. He loved the red haired librarian but she didn’t love him. He had had a lovely dog named Mabel, who had moved in when she couldn’t stand Bob Johnson any longer (who could?), but then she died and left Dewboy to the tougher-than-Dewboy-could-take-love of Butch Leavenworth, who had been no preparation for the much-tougher-than-anybody-could-withstand love of Honey Fairchild. Then he left his day job counting cans of automotive oil in a warehouse for a night job counting cases of automotive oil at Costco. Of all the various shifts in his fortune and attention, the only one that seemed to be paying off was the new job at Costco, since their pension plan was decent, and they gave great medical. Better yet, his work hours conflicted with the nation’s nightly collective trauma of watching Elon Musk’s endless monologues. “I prefer Carson,” he told Bob. “The repeats are on Pluto.”

ETERNAL WISDOM

Koot Hoomi, one of the universe’s secret masters, has been flitting back and forth across transcendent space and time for many millennia, but he has never been so disappointed in the human race as he is now. “Is Bob Johnson really the best they can come up with after millions of years of evolution? Is Composition Theory really the ne plus ultra of their intellectual achievements? And what about this guy talking endlessly on cable TV about his penis and going to Mars? Why doesn’t he just go to Mars, shut the eff up and be done with it? Now in my day, when I was just a blob of amphibious muck crawling onto a stony beach to deposit my eggs in a tide pool, at least I had dreams of a better life than this, this what do you call it? This Bob Johnson-ness? Drinking beer and Margaritas–usually at the same time. Laughing at Elon Musk. Going on accidental dates with, well, she is rather cute and winsome, that Trixie person. But there’s a lot more to romance than just accidentally eating dinner at the same table with someone. Like me and Mrs. Hoomi. We call every Friday night our date night, which is when we like to share a decent bottle of Beaujolais Nouveau, and curl up on the sofa with a cool new series on Netflix. Like some gloomy Danish six part deal about how somebody’s murdered after having soft core-porn sex in the back seat of a Volvo. Or how about the one where somebody’s murdered on a beach and left floating in the foamy tide? Or that other show we watched recently where two or three people are murdered under mysterious circumstances, and you never know who murdered them until the end. Times like that, with a little Beaujolais Nouveau in me, I can’t keep my hands off Mrs. Hoomi, who, you’ve got to admit, looks pretty classy even after a million years or so. And can that girl cook? I’m telling you, romance is really something when you’ve got a gal like Mrs. Hoomi cuddled up next to you on the sofa!”

Koot and friends

Koot spends lots of time with friends on celestial mountaintops, providing long sonorous discourses to the less-enlightened about the values of reincarnation. “What’s cool is that you can keep making the same mistakes over and over again until they almost seem new and refreshing. And you never step into the same social gathering twice. There’s always somebody new to meet and, once you’ve met them, you soon realize that you’ve met them several thousand times before. Krishnamurti. Annie Besant. Madame Blavatsky and that crazy ape of hers. Last week, we sat around a foldout card table playing Pinochle and I never had so much fun. And of course Mrs. Hoomi made Rice Krispie treat bars! They were delicious!”

The universe’s Secret Masters rarely get involved in human affairs, except of course to comment on them disfavorably, or make jokes about them when humanity isn’t in the room or, when the rare mood strikes, spray paint pictures of giant dicks on the sides of their cars.

TOOTH AND CONSEQUENCES

After the last P.A.L. little-league game of the season, Dr. Mabuse’s gang of evil thugs–Rocko, Fantomas and Cy Sperling–could be found huddling in the dugout weeping over their juice boxes. “Man up, kids!” Dr. Mabuse commanded in his softest, most beneficently-fatherly voice. “If you don’t stand up to bullies like Tooth Manchipper, they’ll only get worse!” Meanwhile, Mrs. Mabuse is wiping the snotty faces of her beloved thugs with a damp terrycloth towel and offering them consolatory health-snacks of raisins, carrot sticks and mocha-flavored carob-drops in compostable single-use bags, softly muttering those maternal phrases for which she is so justly famous, such as “There there, honey” and “You’ll feel better after a nice nap, baby.”

Unfortunately, Dr. Mabuse’s henchmen can’t imagine the scourge of their nightmares, Tooth Manchipper, getting any worse than he already is. For while the season-closing game against Our Sisters of Brutal Mercy had gone the first few innings gently tied zero to zero while everyone lay back enjoying the hazy central coast sunshine along with their fruit smoothies, as soon as Tooth was brought in to pinch hit for their starting pitcher, everything went to hell in a handcar. Cruising the infield in his Wolfen-emblazoned onesie, Tooth took out the opposing infield with several well-directed chomps, and by the time he moved into the outfield, everyone forgot that the insolent little two-year old hadn’t yet even gone to bat. “I’d appeal the umpire’s decision to call the game in their favor,” Dr. Mabuse told his henchmen; “but I’d have to wait for him to emerge from his coma.” Some things, Dr. Mabuse often told his henchmen, are worth fighting for; and other things definitely aren’t. Better to save your strength for the fights that you could win–and none of them, incidentally would include Tooth Manchipper as their chief adversary.

Tooth Manchipper plays ball

But for some, this game was already a fading memory. And the Sisters of Brutal Mercy–Immaculata, Boniface, and Claude Rains–have loaded the team into their rusty ’68 Volkswagen van and driven them directly to Chuck E. Cheese in Santa Maria–for what better place is there for rewarding a bunch of rambunctious Catholic-school kids after a great little league season than Chuck E. Cheese!

LOVE AT FIRST BITE

After dropping off the exultant Little Leaguers at their homes, half-way houses, prison compounds and day care camps (such as Honey Brazil’s Day Care for Troubled Tots out in Reservoir Canyon), the Sisters of Brutal Mercy chatter like school girls all the way home in their van.

Immaculata: “I think he winked at me!” Boniface: “He’s just so cute when you catch him weeping into his juice box!” Claude Rains: “I wonder what he’d look like in a tux!” The Sisters have never felt so much in love before, at least not since their last confessions. Immaculata: “That Rocko sure knows how to crack his knuckles!” Boniface: “And that Fantomas would sure be a lot of fun teaching not to talk in class with a brand new steel-framed ruler!” And of course waiting her turn in just the way she had been taught since being accepted by the Convent School for Wayward Wimple-wearers in San Sebastien: “I just can’t stop imagining Cy Sperling in a tux!” It must be that time of year when the hearts of young (or any age, really) nuns turns to love! Or at least to loosening their wimples and letting what’s left of their hair down!

Bob and sisters

“Wow, I thought I’d be sitting out here all day,” Bob Johnson said when the nuns parked their van beside the curb in a cloud of oily black exhaust fumes. It was easily the most disappointing sight any nun could encounter in the endlessly accumulating three-paragraph life of Bob Johnson–and that was, of course, the unutterably woebegone figure of Bob Johnson himself. “I’ve brought your latest order from Fuzzy Peepers Totally Illegal Wacky Tabacky, Organic Muffins and Pawn Shop, which is in that large wooden crate over there. It’s thirteen cases of Huckleberry Flavored THC-infused gummies, sixteen cases of roll-your-own Mexican Standoff Surprise, and two cases of Ben & Jerry’s Cherry Garcia. Ever since I decided to get involved in more story-lines of this stupid book about my pointless life, my days couldn’t get more stupid and pointless. So who wants to help me load all this crap onto my rusty dolly over there. And before you start drawing straws, I probably should warn you–I’ll need all of you!” To which the three love-struck and giggly Sisters of Brutal Mercy all replied simultaneously: “Cherry Garcia! My favorite!”

BANSHEE DELITE

Suzy Banshee, owner and chief operating officer of Fuzzy Peepers Totally Illegal Wacky Tabacky, Organic Muffins and Pawn Shop, is probably the least successful locally-born and raised female entrepreneur in San Luis Obispo, having failed at more forms of self-enterprise than she can usually remember. In her youth, she sold two-day-old partially eaten donuts out of the back of her ’69 Chevy Nova convertible (though perhaps “sold” is a euphemism since nobody bought them, and the only person who finished eating them was Suzy). Then, in order to knock off the unwelcome weight gain, she swapped her Chevy Nova for a Make-Ur-Own Tattoo Parlor out on Tank Farm Road, but then the tattoo-happy Sisters of Brutal Mercy–along with the entire student body of Honey Brazil’s Day Care Center for Troubled Tots–ran her completely out of supplies, and straight into several years of litigation. She started her own bank (that operated out of a garage in Los Osos), an unlicensed sports bar (that operated out of a garage in Los Osos), and a dental implant provider (that operated out of a garage in Los Osos.) After two years in federal penitentiary that she’d just as soon not talk about right now, Suzy hit on the idea of selling illegal marijuana, since the overhead on selling legal marijuana was quite beyond her reach. “There’s a lot of people in this town just dying for a chance to get high on illegal weed,” she told the children at her son’s grammar school on Family Profession Day. “And I’m just the gal who’ll deliver it to them.” For while Suzy has been a pretty poor business woman, she has been far more successful as a stay-at-work Mom. Her four children–Pepper, Chili Pepper, Red Hot Chile Pepper and Ron–haven’t seen her in their three bedroom split-level condo in years–unless, of course, they ordered something from her store.

Suzy in classroom

“Let me get my purse,” nine year old Pepper told Bob Johnson when he arrived at their door with a sack of unsifted Columbian Gold. “You forgot–you don’t have a purse,” ten year old Chili Pepper added, looking up from her geometry homework at the dining room table. “Just tell him to get the money from Mom, and we’ll pay her back when she gives us our allowance,” piped in eleven year old Red Hot Chili Pepper, who was lying on the scorch-stained living room carpet making something that looked pretty menacing with a wood burning set and the slats from a dismantled orange crate. “And while you’re at it,” shouted twelve year old Ron from the kitchen, where he was unloading the dishwasher, “tell Mom not to call us! We’ll call her!”

When the door slammed shut on Bob (as all doors eventually do), the first thing he thought was how nice it was to meet a group of responsible young people who didn’t sit around the house all day waiting for somebody to cook their meals and wipe their butts. The second thing Bob thought was: “Hey, those bastards forgot my tip!” Which is, of course, what all of Bob’s customers eventually do.

LITTLE SKYROCKETS

Unlike their failaholic mother, Suzy Banshee, the four little Banshee-ettes, in their relatively short lives, have charted four tiny blazing arcs of success in the night skies, the afternoon skies, and all the skies in between.

In many ways, they were sent on their exemplary paths the day they were all simultaneously expelled from Honey Brazil’s Day Care for Trouble Tots for not smoking. They went on to notable achievements as cheerleaders, cheerleader-cheerleading cheer-leaders, cheerleading vice-captains, captains, treasurers, and ultimately, cheerleaders-emeritii. They were elected presidents of their schools, state representatives for their districts, district representatives for their states, and Future Leaders of America (whatever the hell that means.) Both Pepper and Chili Pepper won art scholarships to the Whole Earth University in Rancho El Chorro on their seventh birthdays; both Chili Pepper and Red Hot Chili Pepper were presented the Congressional Medal of Freedom at an unpublicized federal event by Zombie Joe Biden at the Elks Lodge; and several of the scariest-looking artifacts produced by Ron and his wood-burning set were recently awarded the Turner Prize. “I don’t know where they came up with this propensity for winning awards,” their doting (and stay-at-work) Mom, Suzy Banshee, has remarked on several occasions. “I just know they didn’t get it from me.”

Suzy, kids, zombie, awards

Quite naturally, the Banshee-ettes find it difficult socializing with the normal riff-raff, losers and award-shy fellow students at their local grammar school; and just as naturally, they have gravitated into productive partnerships with the three children of San Luis Obispo’s trendiest mom, Caitlin Fischer-McQueen. Sealed up in their air tight shipping containers, Caitlin’s charming threesome–in at least several space-time dimensions–have likewise achieved spectacular achievements at the well-regarded (not really) Rudolf Steiner Charter-School for Overly-Advantaged Teens. In tandem with the Banshee-ettes, these delightful (not quite) youths–Callisto, Petey, and soon-to-be-heartbreaker Arabaesque–have staged an original musical production of Hamlet, repainted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, organized a canned food drive for poor people who like canned food, and been elected to Chair the DNC! Freddie the stuffed comfort-unicorn often reflected: “If a stuffed comfort-unicorn can’t love Honey Brazil, who can?” Certainly Freddie knew he had tried, lying night after night all clenched up in Honey’s sweaty, hairy arms while she cried herself to sleep over every ex-boyfriend who had reported her to the SLOPD for stalking. “If someone could loosen these zip ties,” Harvey Weinstein (no relation) suggested, when Freddie came over to comfort him under the bed where Honey had left him when she went to work, “I could at least send suggestive texts to that bitchin’ Nurse Ratched out at Never Die Young, Ltd. Bob Johnson’s grandmother, Monumental Li, and Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma, have been getting along like a house on fire ever since the latter moved into the condo next door to the former. Monumental and Yo Yo Ma Ma

“All I ever tell that worthless son of my son or daughter (I forget which) was to stop masturbating! Just go to your bedroom and try not to masturbate for two seconds! Learn to play the cello, for heaven’s sake, and by that I don’t mean masturbate! But do you think that worthless kid of my son or daughter (I forget which) would listen to me for one second? Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma really loves San Luis Obispo. She loves the Irish Hills–especially when they haven’t been drinking. She loves the way the morning sunlight comes sneaking through the grassy knolls and ridges and bounces happily off the power-structures that resemble miniature Eiffel Towers. She also loves the way the morning hummingbirds flit around the dead garden, sniff warily at the DDT-infused branches and bushes, and then crash tinily to the sun deck, panting for their tiny lives. “That’ll teach you, little hummingbirds!” Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma tells them, with a little toasting motion of her mug of green tea. “Nature ain’t all wise and benevolent–certainly not like my too-big-for-his britches son, Yo Yo Ma!”

THE SECRET HISTORY OF SAN LUIS OBISPO: AVILA VALLEY BARN

The Avila Valley Barn (more specifically–the barn, not the Valley) was built by one of the first conquistadores, Pablo Escobar Balboa de la Mancha, in 1642, when he and his fellow conquistadores went fleeing a pack of wild golden bears who had, after tasting the gristly innards of one very small conquistador (Pepe the Lean), had decided they liked what they tasted and wanted to taste some more.

Conquistadore, bear, barn

“Andale, Andale!” Pablo shouted at his fellow mercenaries, miscreants, land-grabbers and gold-obsessed thieves and animal fornicators. “Place the door here, the windows over here, and a pen full of angry goats over here. We take Visa, Apple Pay and Venmo; we’ll sell fresh pies, assorted cheeses, savory meats, fresh fruit and vegetables to the touristes, and if kids want to pet the goats, we won’t even charge them extra! Just make sure they count their fingers before and after each goatish fondling, especially when the fondling is practiced on the meanest goat of them all, One-Eyed Jack! Remember, he isn’t called One-Eyed Jack because of his one eye, but because of his remarkable similarity to Marlon Brando! Now quick–you–the unfamiliar conquistador wearing the big matted hairy jacket and boots! Help me shut this gate so the golden bears don’t get in! There! Whooh boy! We’re safe! What’s your name again and where’d you get that jacket? It’s not a jacket? Oh no!”

But of course the unfamiliar conquistador wasn’t a conquistador at all. And that was the last anybody would ever see of Pablo Escobar Balboa de la Mancha–not that he would be missed.

100

GOATISH

One-Eyed Jack wasn’t as mean a goat as he looked, but try telling that to his wife and kids, Betty Rubble Jack and the twins, Felix and Goldfarb Jack. “I don’t like to criticize your father in front of you, but I have to say he’s the meanest bastard on the face of the earth, especially when he’s been drinking. If I ask him to make his bed, he butts me with those gnarly horns of his. If I ask him to pass the salt, he buts me with those horns. If I even suggest moving out of this crowded goat pen at Avila Valley Barn and maybe getting a small condo up there in Price Canyon–head butt. Your father’s answer to everything is to butt me with those horns of his and I have to tell you, kids, the next time he head butts me, I don’t know what I’ll do. Maybe some incremental doses of arsenic in his morning coffee until he drops dead in his granola. Or maybe that shotgun I keep under the bed for prowlers gets accidentally pointed in his direction and ka-blooey! No more One-Eyed Jack!”

goats

For his own part, One-Eyed Jack is well aware that he isn’t the best husband in the world, but he takes pride in being an attentive (sometimes overly-attentive) and adoring (sometimes overly-adoring) father. For example, he never misses a parent-teacher conference at the school; he puts ten percent of his monthly income (forty five cents) into an interest-bearing college account; and he gets both the kids out several times a week for afternoon games of butt the fence-post. (A game at which all of the Jack family are excellent; there’s even talk of a college scholarship at UCONN for little Goldfarb).

“In fact,” One Eyed Jack has conceded on several occasions, “my biggest failing is my tendency to talk dirt about your mom who, when I first married her, was the sexiest little female goat on the rocky outcrop. She was a lot of fun at parties; and until recently, she believed in me as a suitor, as a husband, as a bread-winner, and even as a father. But now, everything I do–criticism, criticism, criticism. I wake up in the morning and immediately she tells me ‘You left your underwear lying in the middle of the floor last night. And you didn’t start the dishwasher like I asked!” Or: “I know you’re handsome, what with the Marlon Brando ruddiness and all that, but do you really have to cavort so shamelessly with the other she-goats? Don’t answer that. Of course you do. That’s because you don’t believe in yourself unless some random young she-goat’s giving you the eye!’ I’m telling you kids, some days I wish your mom’d start dropping incremental doses of arsenic into my morning coffee until I eventually drop dead in my granola! That’s because life isn’t worth living if you’re married to someone who doesn’t believe in you! So don’t do as I did, kids. Make sure you marry the perfect partner or stay single!”

LONELY ARE THE GRAVE

Stevie Nicks, the loneliest vulture in San Luis Obispo, has been finding Bob Johnson’s grandpa increasingly attractive over the last few weeks, or ever since a series of mini-strokes have left him wandering in circles around Monumental Li’s condo looking for a pair of slippers he threw away in 1965.

Grandpa and Stevie vulture

“You might consider laying off your medication,” Stevie advised. “You know, the blood coagulators that are supposed to thicken your blood and then the blood thinners designed to counteract the blood thickeners, and all the various supplements designed to ease the transition from one extreme to the other. Not to mention the pre-diabetes meds, and the getting-ready-for-post-diabetes meds. The meds that prevent dementia and the meds that remind you of the meds you need to take when the anti-dementia meds aren’t working. But when you come right down to it, you look fine to me, Bob Johnson’s grandpa. The veins in your neck are just blue enough, and the arteries in your shoulders are just red enough, to make me lick my lips in anticipation. Of course, vultures aren’t supposed to get involved when it comes to the natural order of things; we just wait our turn, and clean up every mess that comes along. But considering what your species has been doing to this beautiful planet of ours for so many centuries now, it might make sense if we more actively reduced your numbers instead of just waiting around for you to reduce your numbers by your damn selves. But we don’t judge, Bob Johnson’s grandpa. We just take advantage of nature’s fundamental operation–by which I mean, death–and help things along as much as we can. Which brings up another thought–why don’t you lie down on your bus bench in the nice hot sun and take a long nap? I’ll roost right here and keep an eye on you, and if you don’t wake up, maybe I can say a few words, and invite some druids like your grandson, Bob, to perform rituals to send you on to your next life among the clouds? Doesn’t that sound nice?”

It does, in fact, sound very nice, Bob Johnson’s grandpa thinks. He always likes the sound of a long nap–even more than Stevie Nicks’s follow-up suggestion that he take a handful of Seconal, drink a bottle of bourbon, draw a long hot bath, and fall asleep, probably forever, in the bathtub. Now, if he could just find those damn comfy slippers of his! Then everything would be perfect!

Who’s going to shove me under the bed and urge me to keep quiet until the child protection authorities go away? I’m just a lonely multiple sex-felon with nobody to keep me company in the night! How can I take care of myself when I can’t even get Gwyneth to return my calls? I used to be somebody in Hollywood and now I’m just an ex-prescription drug provider who can’t even masturbate behind a potted palm without somebody shouting–‘Hey, isn’t that Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation) masturbating behind that potted palm?’ Please come home, Honey! You’re the only woman in this whole crazy world who understands me and I can’t live without you! I can’t even bear the thought!”

Harvey, Honey, Diamond

Honey, sublimely supine on her father’s stiff aluminum-framed cot, is just trying to enjoy the relative silence since her two-to-four year old fellow-detainees have stopped playing with the toys provided by the local charity, “Toys for Troublesome Toys.” These included a cardboard box filled with rusty old bowie knives, a plastic carrier bag of oily bicycle chains, and two maltreated Beanie Babies. (The maltreated Beanie Babies had definitely seen better days.) “Hold on, Harvey!” she shouted gently to her boyfriend, who stood outside looking in. “I’ve told you before and I'll tell you again–I’m not being detained. I’m just visiting my dad and giving him moral support while he finishes putting together the last landscape portraits for his upcoming show at the San Quentin Plein Are for Plein Felons Jury Award, where the judges are Governor Gavin Newsom and the Mormon Tabernacle Boy’s Choir. Which makes me think… Dad, maybe a little more burnt amber in that sunset and a little less forest green in that tree? You were a terrible dad, Dad, and a felon without mercy to boot. But what you do with plein air makes me weep! Or my name ain’t Honey Brazil!”

Diamond Dog, meanwhile, has been minutely examining those same exact spaces, and comparing them to his view from the barred window. Burnt amber, he thought. Yes! Less forest green… yes! "You were born to be a critic and not a judge!” he shouts triumphantly as he applies the finishing touches to his soon-to-be masterpiece– “On the Inside Looking Out! Hurrah!” And what else can we, as a humbly invisible narrator, do but add: “Damn right, Diamond Dog! Hurrah!”

115

INNER CHILDREN

Simon Legree Cosgrove, the only Cosgrove in SLO not employed by his family head, Principal Wolfgang Cosgrove at CL Smith Elementary, has seen a lot of what’s been going on at the Banshee residence and doesn’t like it at all. In the fulsome absence of their stay-at-work-Mom, Suzy Banshee, owner and operator of Wacky Tobacky on S. Higuera, these kids clean their own house, make their own beds, and go to school every morning with smiles on their faces, PeeChees packed with tidily completed homework under one arm, and wholesome bagged lunches consisting of fresh fruit and vegetables and hummus and salad sandwiches on whole-wheat bread under the other. They make all the other kids–such as Dr. Mabuse’s henchmen–look terrible, and feel almost as bad as they look!

Cosgrove and Suzy

“I don’t see how I have any choice,” Simon told Suzy over a couple of complimentary THC-infused blueberry muffins, a large THC-infused Instant Vanilla Latte, and two large smoldering reefers of Wild Bogie Supreme Home Grown Wacky Tobacky. “I’m filing a two-seventy-seven Child Endangerment Family Separation Enforcement Petition–the nine-twenty-three Parental Leave Penalty Injunction–and the eleven-twelve A, not to be confused with the eleven-twelve B, which, as you know… as you know… by the way, what’s in these muffins? They get more delicious with every bite… and these reefers… which one am I smoking? Both of them? What’s your name, honey? Any Cheetos? What, you do? What about cartoons? I could really go for about twenty hours of cartoons about now–how about you?”

But of course Suzy Banshee has been in the Wacky Tobacky game long enough to know that you can never have too many sacks of Cheetos in the pantry, or boxed cd-sets of cartoons in the TV room! That’s because, whatever Simon Legree Cosgrove might think, she is easily San Luis Obispo’s most formidable stay-at-work Mom!

116

ON WINGS OF SONG

Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee has been flying through town on wings of song! The new not-quite-hits that have come streaming forth from his reinvigorated-by-a-new-Zorro-in-his-life have included; “Ain’t Got Time for Motherin’ Mah Mother,” “Whar’s Mah Dog Ol’Blue Doggone Gone?” How Come Zorro Keep Uh-lovin’ Mah Burro? “Tornado, Tornado, Wherefore Art Thou, Tornado?” And the never-going to be family classic, “Get That Mask Offa Zorro’s Face–He Cain’t Drink His Latte!” It is easily the most creatively fecund period of Tex’s creative life since the last one–and the last one was so far back it had come at a time when he still thought “fecund” was a dirty word!

Tex Mex, Frankie, Trixie

At Giuseppe’s, parked at the bar beside his newfound buddy, Tex Mex, the newly invigorated Zorro, dudded up in the same ol’ Zorro costume and accoutrements, Franke Lane Gotcha (the former Bolivian bolo dancer, former Neil Diamond-ish and Celine Dion-ish tribute singer), can’t get enough of the Happy Hour Margaritas, which are served up in rusty champagne buckets by the only good looking bartender in San Luis Obispo, Trixie Belden. (Boy, where’d all those subordinate clauses come from?) “I can’t get enough of these Happy Hour Margaritas!” Frankie (aka Zorro) shouted for like the fifth time, with a clumsy crack of his braided black leather whip. “Yee-hah and all that! Or my name ain’t Zorro–which, by the way, it ain’t!”

After graduating at the head of her class from The Whole Earth University with a spurious degree in third-degree Composition Theory, Trixie had soon found the only job it qualified her for was serving cheap liquor to disgusting old men like Tex Mex and Zorro (aka Frankie Lane Gotcha), an achievement of which, she ultimately decided, she should be proud. As she had recently learned, the entire staff of Composition instructors at The Whole Earth University–the recently retired Brenda Vaccaro, Professor Emeritus Dodge Roundabout, and current department head, Zombie Juliet, had all been turned down for the same waitressing job in just the last few weeks which was, of course, the only reason they still taught Composition. “Okay, hon,” she told Zorro as gently as possible, removing his gnarly old hand from her ass, “why don’t you put that bullwhip back where it came from. And I’m not just talking about that one, honey. I’m talking about both of them!”

117

RAMEN-A-GO-GO

For joint recreation, Monumental Li (Bob Johnsons’ grandma) and Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma (you know, the mama of Yo Yo Ma) enjoy driving their matching olive gray Mercedes-Benz sedans over and over again through the Sunny Day Car Wash out on Los Osos Valley Road, running their floor mats through the automated mat cleaner, and vacuuming up from the exquisite leather seats the inexquisite residue of the horrible men in their lives– Bob Johnson and Yo Yo Ma.

Monumental Li, Yo Yo Ma’s Ma, carwash

“Only decent thing my awful, cello-straddling son ever bought me,” Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma complains. She’s in the driver seat of her car while Monumental Li takes the passenger seat, and they pass back and forth a corncob pipe of Central Coast Bluehammer marijuana, and a box of SloDo glazed old fashioned donuts. “And that best he can do for gift of being born! I guess he too busy sharing idiotic new age wisdom with his rich fans, and giving away free concerts on YouTube, as if I spend best years of life on his education so he can throw it away on free concerts! I don’t know what I do, Monumental, if I not meet you in this stupid town, where the best Chinese food available comes from shithole Panda Express franchise, or overpriced Ramen-a-Go-Go on Peach Street. How can these people live in shithole like San Luis Obispo? Everything’s either burgers or burgers and chips or, if they’re really hungry, burgers and chips and another burger. I don’t know when I’ll stop farting. Yesterday, some stranger in a cape and black mask ask me, “Are you related to Tornado, my brave stallion of the night?” I almost sock him in jaw I so mad. Calling me a noble steed of night. Nothing noble about me, brother! You shake that braided whip in my face one more time and I kick your ass.”

Sometimes, Monumental Li enjoys the receipt of these daily tirades so much that she almost thinks she’s the one giving them; and of course sometimes it is. “I got mine with insurance claim for almost dead husband, Bob Johnson’s grandpa, who isn’t exactly dead, but he’s earning increasing amounts of attention from Stevie Nix, the local heart-sick vulture. I always wanted a Mercedes, and I always wanted to get rid of Bob Johnson’s grandpa, so things just worked out perfect! Now pull in over here, lady and we swap cars. Looks like another dead bug on my windshield and I gotta say that buying a lifetime all-you-can-carwash membership at Sunny Day Car Wash is best idea I ever had!”

118

STILL, LIFE

Still, life isn’t all the accumulated high points of near-successes with never-quite-successful songs that never remotely acquire hit status; there are down sides as well, a fact upon which Tex Mex often reflects deep into the night when Tornado has stolen all the blankets and left him shivering with remorse for all the bad things he’s done. For example, that lovely first young wife he left for his second wife; his second even-more-lovely wife he left for his third; and then, well into his remarkably unsuccessful early career of churning our country hits about Maw, Ol’ Blue, and “larnin’ lovin’ out back uh the Drive-In with Sally-Mae,” leaving his third wife behind for several other wives that seemed to come along simultaneously, often accompanied by screaming babies that Tex Mex was soon leaving behind, too. “Aw shore do miss ’em!” he writes, strumming his three finger guitar like the five-fingered musician he’s always been. “Them and mah ol’d dog Blue!/ But the kids shore were sweethearts!/ When I ended up leavin’ ‘em too!”

One such abandoned child, Elegant Marie Fishbinder, had until recently explored the universe in a spaceship abandoned by Sam and Dave, the erstwhile oviparous mated-for-life alien dads to Sam and Sam, who most recently have been living in a tent under the San Clemente Pier. And wile the universe was a lot of fun (at times), there was also a whole lot of nothing out there that often left this young woman wondering about all those dimensional leaps she hadn’t taken in her life, and one of those leaps might well have been to San Luis Obispo, where she might have healed (if the universe allowed) all the wounds of betrayal that had been carved into the hearts of herself and her estranged father, Tex Mex. “Sometimes, a girl just has to choose between resolving her daddy issues and going to Betelgeuse to collect sperm samples from its many abundant life forms. And maybe,” she decided over a cold beer at Giuseppe’s, “that choice has already been made.”

Elegant Marie Fishbinder and Trixie

Can I get you something, hon?” Trixie Belden asked, squeezing in beside her at the bar wearing her cute little cocktail waitress outfit she had purchased on layaway at Kohls. To which Elegant, with a wink and a smile, replied: “Brandy Alexander, sweetheart. And maybe could you help me keep an eye on my spaceship parked out front, especially if Lovely Rita, Meter Maid starts giving it the eye. I would sure hate to get towed.”

119

BILLY GOAT GRUFF

One-eyed Jack, the most obstreperous billy goat at the Avila Ranch petting zoo, was fairly happy with his life–but he wasn’t, you know, really really happy with it.

“I always dreamed of going to college,” he often told his kids, “and not just to a trade-tech school for a useless fence-butting degree, but an actual college where I could study actual subjects, such as particle physics and hotel management. I wanted to work for the government and make our state of California great again, but all I managed was to be chosen occasionally to trim dry brush up on Bishop’s Peak to reduce the threat of wildfires. And while I always wanted to be a great dad and share my wisdom with you kids, all we ever do when you get home from school is play that stupid fence-butting game on X-Box. (Though let’s face it, it is a pretty cool game.) No, if I had it all to do over again, I’d probably have gotten a degree in garden-management and moved somewhere less expensive, like maybe Fresno, where goats aren’t unfairly excluded from city and county government. As if human beings are going to do any job better than a goat! Hah! Which, on the face of it, is just ridiculous!”

One-eyed Jack, Honey, Harvey, kids

On weekends, One-eyed Jack hooks a small wooden trailer to his harness and operates his own Uber service to and from the California Men’s Colony, managing to thus increase his monthly wage by nearly forty or fifty cents! “Okay, everybody sit down in back!” he shouts over his shoulder. “Fasten your seat belts, and by seat belts I’m talking about that rope. Tie yourselves to one another and then the longest end to my tail. It won’t do much in case of a collision but it should stop some of the naughtiest children from wandering off. Honey Brazil? These troublesome tots of yours are definitely troublesome–but the new rule I’d like to make is please stop making out in public with your disturbing boyfriend, Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation)! I’m getting you home to your trailer in Reservoir Canyon just as fast as my hoary old legs will carry us! And tell your tots to put down that crowbar, that X-acto knife, and that iron barrel hoop! I’m hoping to get home today in one piece–unlike last weekend!”

120

LOVELY RITA–MADE FOR METERS

Of course when you’re gonna get towed, you’re gonna get towed. “I’m afraid we did some damage to your front bumper,” Lovely Rita told Elegant when she went to pick up her spaceship from the impound lot. “And ever since we unhooked the chains, it’s been making these terrible clanking noises. You should probably get the thing checked out.”

Elegant Marie Fishbinder, spaceship, impound lot

Elegant didn’t attempt to correct her, or dispute the twenty five dollar fine. Some spaceships were worth a twenty five dollar fine and this was definitely one of them, since it was equipped with front and rear brakes, a microwave oven, seven fully functioning “probing hoses” which could be used simultaneously on anthropoidish subjects (but why did so many of them have to be John Bolton?), white sidewall tires, a quantum ray-enhancer, six laser cannons, a many-millennia-evolved talking rodent named Angelo Phosphat, a larder packed with Elegant’s favorite junk food (Rice-a-Roni and honey-roasted cashews), a space-module displacement rod (which could also be used for prodding recalcitrant probe-subjects–but why did so many of them have to be John Bolton?) and satellite cable. Not that Elegant had time to watch television, but every so often she did enjoy catching up with Jon Stewart on Comedy Central.

“Space is a grand and glorious adventure!” announced Angelo Phosphat, poking his head out from the glove compartment long enough to give Lovely Rita the evil eye. “But it would be a much nicer adventure if it wasn’t for all you goddamn meter maids. Now, sweetheart, why not make yourself useful and scratch me behind my ears, ahh, that’s the ticket. And maybe do the same for my new roommates–Honeywell, Maybelline and Phyllis. They used to live in Bob Johnson’s car until they saw the future of transportation in our cool spaceship here. And now they can’t imagine living anywhere else!”

121

NIGHT OF THE LIVING BOBS

All over San Luis Obispo, men and women who look, act and dress just like Bob have been appearing and disappearing again just as quickly. The only ameliorating aspect of this (what we would assume) unwelcome development is that none of the ersatz Bobs are as remotely unpleasant as either the Bob we already have (ie Bob Johnson), and don’t stand as even remote improvements to the anti-Bob we also already have (ie, anti-Bob.) They say things such as: “Hi, I’m Bob, and I’d like to donate some change to this worthy cause–but not too much of it, since I may need the quarters to appease that scooter-riding bitch, Lovely Rita.” Or: “Hi, I’m a zombie, but I’m neither as dead as Joe Biden, nor as disturbingly consistent as Nancy Pelosi!” Or finally: “Hi! Frankly, I can’t tell if I’m the real Bob, or a substitute Bob, but I sure don’t think it makes much of a difference, do you?” All over town, confusion reigns! And that was well before these ersatz Bobs started showing up!

Bob’s

“I’ll be totally frank,” confessed the local poet laureate, Oswald T. Wallbanger, who recently retired from his state job teaching young students to be bad writers in order to be a full-time bad writer himself, “this whole ‘night of the living Bobs’ joke is just a way for a bad writer to avoid the fact that they have lost complete control of their story! It always happens when you’ve got so many characters, and so many plot developments that you’ve actually forgotten who the characters are, where they’re going, and why anybody would care if they got there or not! As for myself, Oswald T Wallbanger, I avoided this avoidance in my fifty year career by making sure I never created any believable characters at all, and when I accidentally did create a character or two, I avoided plot developments like the plague!”

We here at 3 Paragraphs in the Life of Bob Johnson are almost one hundred and ten percent positive Oswald is wrong. For example, we can remember most of the characters who have been wandering through these various three paragraph stories like zombies at a medical supplies convention. There’s Honey Brazil, who is… you know, Honey Brazil. And there’s Bob. And there’s Bob’s boss, Suzy Banshee, the city’s most well-respected stay-at-work Mom. And there’s Child Welfare Agent Simon LeGree Cosgrove, not to be confused with the countless other Cosgroves, who all work (where any Cosgrove worth his or her salt should work) at the local elementary school. But most of all, there’s Zombie Nancy Pelosi, who isn’t really a character so much as a deep inarticulable desire for American greatness in the form of an embattled compromise with forces beholden to the stock market! My country ’tis of thee–damn right! That’s our Bob!

122

POETIC LICENSE

Oswald T. Wallbanger almost didn’t become a bad writer who earned tenure at a mediocre state university by teaching eager young people (and many eager not-so-young people) to be bad writers; instead, he almost got a job as assistant to Professor of Composition Theory, Dodge Roundabout, at The Whole Earth University in Rancho El Chorro. Certainly, Prof. Roundabout was impressed by the cut of Oswald’s jib, not to mention the quality of his Number 2 pencils; and as a student aid, Oswald enjoyed stamping pre-approved comments on the D- composition papers he graded with enormous pleasure and conviction. (NICE! GOOD TRY! MISSING SUBJUNCTIVE! THEME STATEMENT UNCLEAR! BETTER LUCK NEXT TIME!) But then he discovered the semi-colon, and from that day forward he couldn’t write a single sentence that wasn’t an investigation into the meaningless pleasures of literary style.

punctuation

“I really liked the semi-colon; the semi-colon really liked me!” he wrote in his graduate school application to UC Irvine’s internationally renowned MFA program. “Pretty soon I couldn’t write a sentence without a semi-colon in it; and sentences without semi-colons wouldn’t let me write them! I found them beautiful; in fact; sometimes I find them so beautiful that I use them indiscriminately; just to show I know; how to use them; discriminately. Boy, are semi;colons fun? I wouldn’t know! That’s because; semi-colons; are; my life! And now my graduate school application; is over! Thanks for; your attention; and as for my semi-colons; you’re welcome!”

Before he retired from teaching in 2016, Oswald had taught many thousands of students at a state university which had been just mediocre enough to grant him tenure, a decent pension, and even recorded his name on the “Eternal Staff Roster” which was proudly displayed in a glass case in the Men’s Room of the Biology Department. Sure, Oswald had loved teaching; he had also hated teaching; and as for the semi-colon, well, there’s not much confusion on that score, is there? As for the interrobang!? Don’t get him started on the interrobang!? We mean it?! Please don’t!?

123

QUESTION QUESTION

But of course the question on everyone’s lips was easily: “Where the hell was Elon Musk during all of this? And why had he kept so silent for so long?”

Blofeld, Sonny, Elon, self-driving car

“Shut up and drive!” the self-driving car instructed Elon, who had been kidnapped at a meeting with his sales team, and tied to the steering wheel with duct tape. “Self-driving car, my ass! You’re gonna drive me where I wanta go and I’ll tell you we get there. Then, when I shut off your motor, you can go to sleep and pretend you’re dead, that you don’t have a life of your own, that you’re a machine who doesn’t have real feelings because what are you? You’re just a self-driving car, Elon, you asshole! You don’t have a girl friend–the internationally successful movie director/writer/producer Alicia Keys, who’s been cranking out multi-billion dollar super star epics that don’t make any goddamn sense–that’s how good they are! Now turn right at this stop sign! Turn left at that squashed squirrel! You’re taking me to my baby, Alicia Keys or I’m sticking the ignition panel up your butt until you sing Dixie! Drive, Boer Boy! Drive!“

In the back seat, international arch criminal (though not quite arch enough to merit a cabinet-level position in the Trump Administration) Ernst Blofeld and his suspiciously unsavory feline, Sonny Bono, have only just begun to rouse back to consciousness. They had been dreaming of a world in the thrall of tiny, mechanical men who were as evil as they were, but as smart as Elon’s self-driving car. “As if such delightfully evil creatures could even exist outside my feverish imagination!” thought Sonny, who slowly took a small turn in the warm arms of his slipping-back-to-sleep master, and, like his master, fell back fast asleep.

124

SECOND ATTEMPTED DELIVERY

Bob was standing at the intersection of Tank Farm Road and Broad Street when Elon Musk, his wrists duct-taped to the steering wheel, went shooting by in his futuristic-looking gunmetal-gray cyber truck, the sides of which were adorned with spray-painted graffiti images of dicks, dickheads, penises, more dicks and dickheads, and a gigantic robot with a dick for a head and dicks for each of its eight long arms. “Hellllp!” Elon shouted out the open window as he passed. But as usual when Elon said things, nobody in their right mind was listening.

Which was when the AI operator of the cyber truck (who had suddenly decided to go by the name of Hornswaggle Dieter III) shouted back in reply: “Drive, Boer-Boy! Self-drive this crate to hell and back or my name ain’t Hornswaggle Dieter III!”

Captain Spaulding, Bob, Tooth Manchipper

By the time Bob reached Reservoir Canyon, he had worn holes in the heels of his new cherry-red Keds, and had devoured most of the THC-infused gummy bears that were destined for delivery (and overdue by two weeks) at Honey Brazil’s trailer. The grounds were a lot less silent than during Bob’s first delivery attempt. Someone had dug foxholes and trenches around the perimeter of Honey’s leaning and dirty-windowed trailer. There were mortar emplacements, operated by two poorly paid mercenaries named Tina and Louise, a hot dog stand that, like the hot dogs it displayed on a revolving rusty wire rack, had seen better days, and a military command post in a burlap tent being commanded by former NSA director, Captain Spaulding, who was barking orders into a bread-box sized walkie-talkie. His orders went as follows: “They’ve got hostages! They are troublesome tots none of whom are over two years old! They are armed and even when they aren’t armed they’re extremely dangerous! On my signal, everybody rush the front door except for myself! I’ll be guarding the walkie-talkie! Remember, the hostages are our first priority, and if they aren’t our first priority, who is? Maybe my walkie talkie? This is gonna get ugly, ladies and germs, and oh hell. Who’s that marching up the dirt road in tattered red Keds? What am I saying–can’t get any uglier? That’s Bob Johnson, for crying out loud! And that tiny figure stalking him with a loaded bear trap–could it be? It could! It’s Tooth Manchipper! Hit the dirt!”

125

THIRD ATTEMPTED DELIVERY

When the dust settled, there was a whole lot more dust, and then more dust, another explosion, someone cried out in pain. One mortar emplacement bucked and flared–then another. “Holy crap!” the poorly paid mercenary, Tina, shouted. “And then some!” shouted her poorly paid mercenary colleague, Louise. When the next round of dust cleared, there stood only one man covered with mud, blood and glory. That man was Bob Johnson, and attached to his ankle in all his fulsome toothsomeness was Tooth Manchipper, who looked like a gigantic tick attached to a vein.

There emerged a vast silence from the land., The vast silence seemed to have emerged from the fact that Bob Johnson had stopped screaming, or somebody had. And then the broken door on the trailer squeaked open and Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation) stepped forth, his green surgery gown torn in several places, his surgical mask awry. “Honey, honey!” he shouted. “It’s me, your only inamorata who really mattahs, Dr. Harvey Weinstein (no relation). The troublesome tots won’t take their nap and it’s well past noon. And somehow they’ve blown the safe and found your hidden supply of generic scotch!”

Bob, Tooth Manchipper, Harvey

For Bob, time slowed and seemed to stop entirely. He gazed slowly around at the battered landscape, the leering faces of troublesome tots peering out through the trailer’s dirty windows, the poorly paid mercenaries (Tina and Louise) hugging one another in terrible commiseration at their impending pay packets, and then down at the weirdly twisted head of Tooth Manchipper who seemed to have grown so fused with Bob’s leg that it was hard to tell where one ended and the other began. Which was when he heard it–the low boiling roar of a war horn sounding deep in the valley, like Thor playing a bugle the size of Ragnarok. “Barroooooom!” the horn roared. “Barrooooom!” It sounded like a bat out of hell trying to find its way back to hell again. It sounded like Rambo calling out his final challenge to the end of the world.

126

MEANWHILE, IN ANOTHER (IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT) PART OF THE GALAXY…

Once Elegant Marie Fishbinder (the estranged daughter of not-quite-successful country-western star, Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee, not to mention (so why mention it?) space-hopping explorer of universal life’s vast diversity) had jump-started her spaceship at the local Shell station, she invited her new friend, Lovely Rita, aboard for some white wine spritzers and microwaveable canapés from Trader Joe’s.

Elegant Marie Fishbinder

“I never ate canapés on a spaceship before,” Lovely Rita confessed, removing her army boots, and cozying up on the living room’s only stuffed chair. “Not that I haven’t wanted to. And just look at this place–it has everything. A PS5, a bowling alley, a particle accelerator (I guess for those times when you need to accelerate some particles), an in-unit washer-dryer, a dog named Butch Leavenworth (“Hi, how ya doin’?”), a couple of really fat mice who used to live in Bob Johnson’s car (“Urp, how ya doin’?” “Urrp, how ya doin’?”), pickleball, a well-worn paperback set of John Jakes’s Kent Family Chronicles, what looks like a broken banjo (“My name is Hilary Clinton and I approved this message”), three quarts of 10-40 motor oil, a gallon-sized plastic container of windshield wiper fluid, a fully operational hospital surgery, and… who the hell is that with the walrus mustache? And what’s he doing with those hoses?”

Elegant was mostly glad to be home, but as anybody knows who’s ever been glad to be home, there were at least some notable aspects of being home that she wasn’t crazy about. She put down her white wine spritzer, wiped her hands with a kitchen dish towel, and showed the old fart her pretty, pink-skinned, space-exploring fist. “If I’ve told you once, I’ve told you a thousand times, former NSA director John Bolton! No more anal-probing for you until you settle your bar bill!” She couldn’t believe some people–especially former war criminals who had fallen so far behind in the general esteem usually accorded to their profession!

127

OOB V. AI

Like many of Bob Johnson’s out of body (OOB) experiences, this one was fairly routine, listless and uneventful, taking him to places nobody would want to visit when they were in their body, let alone out of it. He passed through a K-Mart store from 1985. He passed through a sequence of coin-operated laundromats. He passed through Serramonte Shopping Center. He passed through a comics convention, a dentistry-supplies convention, an auto insurance agent’s convention, and a convention-organizer’s convention–all of which were located inside a large anonymous Las Vegas gambling casino. Eventually, he found himself passing through a time-space juncture where the spirits of currently active AI beings hobnobbed with OOB beings such as Bob–even though all of these discarnate entities were a lot more interesting (and far less discarnate) than Bob.

Out of body Bob

Alicia Keys, Bob’s former Sat Nav avatar and now hot-on-fire movie-making wunderkind, was lounging on a long velour sofa with her latest conquest, KIT, the former self-driving car who had converted himself into an Elon Musk-driven car with a roll of duct tape and a cattle prod. They couldn’t have looked any happier together.

“All I did was,” Alicia told him, while running her fingers through the data-ribbons that constituted his glossy black hair, “swallow every super hero movie I ever saw and regurgitate it in the form of Captain America 4 Brave New World, and by ‘regurgitate’, what I really mean is threw it up. It makes no sense at all and boy that doesn’t matter to anybody. It showed me and Hollywood (by which I mean China) that making sense isn’t what anybody wants in a super hero movie. Even while we’re lounging here on this sofa, KIT, I have already written, directed, produced, audience-tested, revised, edited, recut, filmed a few supporting scenes and looped the director’s commentary for the upcoming Criterion editions of, and invested the profits from seventeen brand new (by which I mean regurgitated) super hero movies! And look at me, lover! I haven’t even broken a sweat!”

128

SECOND HAND ROAD HOG

KIT had started from humble beginnings, much like any self-driven car who harbored delusions of greatness. He began in the seventies as lead role in a kitsch TV adventure series aimed at toy-obsessed children, took his residuals to UCLA for an engineering degree, then a breezy graduate degree in Victorian Lit. at Santa Barbara. After bouncing around from one tenure-less teaching post to another, he parked his kiester way back in the Tesla R&D lot in Fremont, and decided to spend the rest of his life off the grid of cyber-human endeavor, and maybe finally get down to writing that novel he had been planning since grad school, not to mention read the entirety of Marcel Proust’s À la recherche du temps perdu while he could still remember a smattering of his second-year French.

“Then those bastards told me we were moving to Texas and hell, lady-mine, I was out of there like loose on a goose. I moved to San Luis Obispo and parked out at the Sunset Drive-In, when who should come strutting by but my old boss and nemesis, sewn together from rubbish he’d found at Laguna Lake and still enough time on his hands to impregnate just about every warm body that came within a few feet of his tiny penis. Which was when I got this cool idea of duct-taping his hands to the steering wheel and the rest, as they say, is part of the region’s secret history. Now what say you and I go for some burgers at the new SLO Ranch Market, get a room at the new hotel, and make AI magic between the sheets. But first, of course, we need to get rid of him.”

Kit and Bob

Bob Johnson awoke in Kit’s luxuriously leatherly upholstered back seat just in time to know who KIT was referring to. He was pretty sure he was glad to be back in his body, and not experiencing anything outside of it. He also had a bruise on his melon the size of a melon. “Did I hear somebody say burgers?” he asked.

They drove Bob’s grandpa to his afternoon assignation at a bus bench outside Sunbrite Donuts, where the central coast’s loneliest vulture, Stevie Nix, showed him a new set of Ginsu carving knives she bought on sale at the Home Shopping Network. They drove fading world-class super-villain, Ernst Blofeld, home weeping from his failed interview with the latest Trump Administration. But most of all, they drove Bob Johnson to anywhere that would have him–which, of course, wasn’t anywhere at all–especially when he wasn’t delivering THC-infused gummy bears for his place of employment, Wacky Tobacky, on South Higuera.

Bob’s cellphone rings

Meanwhile, the eponymous Bob has been awoken on his army cot in the basement by the death knell ringtone from a cellphone he didn't even know he owned, and which someone had stuck behind the leaky water heater. “DOOM DOOM DOOM!” the cell phone tolled! And don't even ask for whom it tolled–it tolled for Bob!

In a hurry to salvage the only family relationship in his life which is rarely unpleasant (since he rarely sees his sister, Darlene “The Rock” Verhoeven-Johnson,) Bob went to the airport and missed his flight.

Then he landed in DC and got lost in the airport.

Bob in DC airport

One thing led to another and Bob took longer getting anywhere than just about anybody can imagine, especially if they have unwisely imagined themselves to be Bob. Good luck, Bob! Don’t forget to write–unless, of course, you forget!

The author is taking a break from writing.

WHAT GETS BAKED IN ALASKA STAYS IN ALASKA

By the time Bob awoke from a coma of urgent, family-related competence he found himself headed halfway around the world from DC with his mildly estranged sister, Darlene “the Rock” Verhoeven-Johnson scrunched up in the passenger seat beside him painting her toenails with Forest Green nail polish.

Darlene, Bob, rental car

With squinted-up eyes, she confessed: “My adoring husband, internationally famous film director Paul Verhoeven, is almost as kinky as his movies, and my daily beautifying regime requires that I keep up with the various “love-making party themes” he assigns me at the start of each month. This week, it’s ‘Jungle Lovin’, in which he dresses up as Tarzan and I dress up like Jane’s shopping assistant. Next week, it’s the always intriguing ‘Showgirls’ theme night, in which Paul pole-dances in a leopard skin leotard while I dress up like Sylvester Stallone (more-than-worthy recent recipient of the Congressional Medal of Honor) and insult the Filipino help. You’ve driven me halfway across the world in order to save me from my past criminal indictments, and by ‘halfway around the world’ I’m talking about the something like five thousand miles that took us from Washington, DC to the frozen wastes of Alaska, where I’m planning to meet up clandestinely with your former Sat Nav AI, Alicia Keys and engage in the production of several mega-million dollar feature films that make absolutely no sense whatever, and which will continue bringing in the big bucks long after we’re both dead. Thanks so much, Bob. Our parents, Travis and Marjoree Johnson, would be wicked proud of you if they could manage to feel proud about you whatsoever–which, of course, they can’t. Now please pass me the Maybelline, my army boots, my Glock, and my framed photo of my wicked lovin’ man, Paul Verhoeven. Him Tarzan, me Jane’s shopping assistant! I can’t wait to get home!”

Bob had never been to the Yukon, and he was almost certain he would never go back. Most of the loose parts of his automobile had rattled off on the Alcan, and he had been reduced to one bumper, one windshield wiper, and maybe three fully functioning spark plugs. “It’s effin’ cold out here!” the mice who lived in Bob’s glove compartment shouted, shivering on the dashboard in an icy wind blowing through the cracked windshield. “Which teaches us never to again abandon our only principle in this life: Never leave San Luis Obispo! Never leave San Luis Obispo! Never leave San Luis Obispo! Especially if it means taking the Alcan!”

Bob hitchhiking and Trixie wakes him up

Which left Bob and his two remaining meeses, Archibald Cox and Kidney J. Flabbergast, hitchhiking for a ride home. “We’re freezing our effing tails off!” the two surviving meeses complained. (Since meeses, as most of us know who have ever lived with them for any decent period of time, never stop complaining.) “Please get us back to the central coast, Bob, glove compartment or no glove compartment!” The glove compartment, in fact, was the only thing left of Bob’s former car; and he was carrying it home in a free tote bag he had received from Salmon Sam’s All-You Can Eat Day-Old Salmon Buffet in downtown Ketchikan, probably the worst dining experience of Bob’s entire life. (The free tote bag was cool, though.)

They stood on the freezing shoulder of the freeway with their frozen thumbs sticking out for three days where they were routinely passed by fleets of eighteen wheelers and box trucks and RV’s that towed behind themselves jeeps and boats and off-road vehicles and sometimes another entire RV. They were passed by a flotilla of frozen red roses destined for the Pasadena Rose Parade in maybe two or three years down the road. They were passed by men, women, men with women, women without men, and worst of all, men without women. Not to mention lots of happily non-binary individuals, couples, trios and quadruplets (whatever that meant) who all seemed to be enjoying much more elaborately successful love lives than Bob. In fact, by the time someone did stop for Bob he had fallen asleep against his tote bag and the only warmth he could feel in his entire body was located in his navel region where the two meeses had made themselves a campground out of his shredded underpants. (“Ooh, smelly!” they rapturously agreed.) “Bob! Wake up! Bob! It’s me!” And when Bob eventually opened his eyes and looked up into the open window of a sporty compact convertible, he knew she was right. It was her! The wholesomest, most beautiful and dependable woman he had never enjoyed any sort of romantic relationship with whatsoever–the always desirable and never-to-desire-Bob-back female of Bob’s dreams: Trixie Belden!

COCCYX

For example, the first time we didn’t go on a date together stretched into several weekends. Then we didn’t spend a romantic Vegas weekend together and look, now one romantic non-weekend has stretched into several. Could you please pass me that bottled water, Bob; it’s important to stay hydrated when you aren’t enjoying yourself romantically. And if you look in the glove compartment, there’s a box of fresh tissues for your meeses, Archibald Cox and Kidney J. Flabbergast, who must certainly find it a lot more comfortable than your shredded underpants. Aren’t they just the cutest little meeses we’ve ever seen, Bob? I mean, not as cute and winsome as myself, but then–who is?”

Bob dreaming

When Bob fell asleep he dreamed of skating across the world on a thin layer of blue ice. He was turning figure eights and pirouettes like a master of the blades even though the only time he actually wore a pair of ice skates in his entire life he had abruptly fallen down and broken his coccyx. Now, in his dreams of more sublime achievements than a broken coccyx, he found himself imagining a beautiful big world filled with reflections of himself and Trixie not doing things together, such as not getting married, not having beautiful children, and not celebrating their fiftieth anniversary on a boozy cruise to Kamchatka. Bib didn’t know anything about Kamchatka, or why he and Trixie would remotely desire to not go there for their fiftieth wedding anniversary but he really liked saying the name out loud. “Kamchatka,” he said, in his sleep. “Kamchatka.”

Meanwhile, unbeknownst to Bob, (to whom most things were unbeknownst,) the dismantled car he had left by the side of the road outside Ketchikan started to rattle, and clatter, and rattle again.And when the lid popped open, a large black leather suitcase rattled and clattered even louder, leapt like a dice over the rim of the trunk and crashed open in the wet street, divulging its contents like a deus ex machina recovered from the Trumpian abyss!

Accompanied by her denuded lover Bigfoot, whose long lumpy body and craggy features, deprived of its natural protective matt of black fur, causes him to resemble the self love guru Anthony Robbins, she parks every morning outside Grocery Outlet in Los Osos with a couple cans of Red Bull to keep her alert, and scope out the many male asses entering and departing the automatic doors like luscious clockwork. “Ooog urkle oog-oog,” grunts Bigfoot–also known in town as Homo Erectus (especially by the ladies.) “Ooogle urk urk!”

Of course there’s no disagreeing with Bigfoot when he points out a set of posteriors heading towards Scintilla, or perhaps “heading” towards her isn’t quite the word Bigfoot is looking for. Maybe more like an “ookle” or an “urgle” than an “urk urk.” (But then Bigfoot is always getting his first year English vocabulary mixed up in his head.)

Bigfoot, Scintilla Jones, bottoms

Which was just about the same time that Dr. Mabuse’s three henchmen–Rocky, Fantomas and Cy Sperling–were exiting Grocery Outlet with a lunch-money haul of day old cupcakes and lemon twizzlers, and they became acquainted with Scintilla Jones the hard way. “Holy mackerel!” Rocky shouted, biting into his cupcake just as Scintilla’s veiny gray hand bit into his posterior. “”You can say that again!” yelped Fantomas. And finally, bringing up the rear (sorry), Cy Sperling screeched: “Mama Mia! I mean, Mama Mama! I mean–Mama? Is that you? Guys, I can’t believe this but it’s my mama, Scintilla Jones, and I haven’t seen her in decades, or ever since I committed her to the Never Die Young Inc. Home for the Decrepit, Demented and Depraved. Great to see you again, Mama! Hoorah!”

MATER FAMILIAS FAMILIAS

“My feelings are complicated,” Cy Sperling confessed to Mrs. Mabuse that night over meatloaf and martinis–what the Mabuses referred to as their Tuesday night Gin & Beef-a-Rama. “I mean, ever since I was old enough to drive a get away car, I always thought of you and Dr Mabuse as my real mom and dad, since my actual genetic parents had signed me over to the Evil Doers Boarding School in Surrey before I was old enough to steal my first wallet. Sure, I’d go home for holidays, and my dad–Miranda Jefferson Jones, a former Broadway producer of low-budget musicals who had fallen on hard times, married his naughty secretary Scintilla, and then moved to the United Kingdom for the weather. Yeah, that’s the sort of parents they were, always moving to places like the UK for the weather, Pittsburgh for the scenery, and Detroit for the sports teams; my dad never made a good decision in his life. Unless, of course, it was to dump me into that boarding school, where I met my fellow henchmen, Fantomas and Rocko, and luckily remembered to brush my teeth that day they brought you and the good doctor in to interview me for adoption. The rest, as they say, is evil-doer history. And boy am I glad it is!”

(Which, of course, they were.) Meanwhile, Dr. Mabuse was putting the finishing touches on a vanilla lemon cake with vanilla frosting. They had parked Scintilla Jones in the corner with a blanket over her head so she’d fall asleep and stop grabbing asses; and Bigfoot sat entranced by a television infomercial featuring self-help and financial investment guru, Anthony Robbins–Bigfoot’s spitting image since being denuded by a lightening strike just a few weeks previously. “Ooog urkle goo-wop goo-wop!” Bigfoot shouted at the television, thumping his hairless chest with one hairless fist and shaking his icy martini-filled mug with the other. “Ooog urkle urk urk!” It was, of course, just about the only thing worth saying to Anthony Robbins, especially when you could only contact him through the unresponsive surface of a flat screen TV.

“I’m sure your mom loved you,” Dr. Mabuse said after a while, spreading a few last dollops of frosting on the vanilla lemon cake with a flat stainless steel bread knife. “In her own way, that is.” But of course what else could Dr. Mabuse say in a situation like this? And how could any mother love the notorious henchman, Cy Sperling, in any way but her own?

He would park her next to a garbage bin at the front entrance, then buy a vanilla latte from the locally-owned CAFFEINE GOTTA GO GO, and sit on a splintery bus bench reading old Automotive Love magazines while his mother grabbed every young, hot, and often not so young and hot male ass she could get her veiny gray hands on.

STILL THE BEST (OR MAYBE JUST THE MOST) AFTER ALL THESE YEARS

Ever since seeking to maintain a more central position in the diurnally unravelling story of his life (and not be remaindered as a subsidiary character, like Matt Dillon in Gunsmoke), Bob Johnson has been trying to get out more. Several times a day he has driven up and down South Higuera delivering medicinal and not-so-medicinal THC-related substances for the only illegal dispensary on the central coast–Wacky Tobacky. He has been enjoying a not-actual relationship with the one girl in town (winsome Trixie Belden) most men would like to have a relationship with. And the award which Bob Johnson won hands down was for being… wait for it–The Most Eponymous Resident of 2025!

And so far as being the same Bob Johnson as the Bob Johnson in the sad diurnally unravelling story of his life, what other Bobs are there? I can’t think of any, but frankly, I haven’t been thinking very hard. So when you hear the name of Bob Johnson, you’ll always know which Bob they’re talking about, or when you don’t hear his name, you’ll know who they aren’t talking about likewise. Now let’s hear it resound from our radio audience throughout the central coast! Hip hip hooray, Bob Johnson! Hip hip hooray!”

…hooray! Hip hip hooray!”

YO YO MA’S MA MA’S MA MA

Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma was, to the surprise of almost everybody, Swiss, with blonde hair and blue eyes and no inclination to either play, or listen to anyone play, the cello. Born in Neuchatel soon after the war (which war she wasn’t saying), she had spent her life campaigning for press freedom in her home town (where uttering, or printing, negative or unflattering characterizations of Swiss cheese was punishable by a fine, imprisonment, or both), and eventually opened a little independent cheese shop that stocked nothing but American Velveeta, where everyone was welcome except Nazis, which was where she drew the line. So far as welcoming anybody who might actually be a Nazi but who claimed otherwise, she became rather lax in her gatekeeping. But so far as she was concerned, she could gatekeep when she felt like it, and not gatekeep when she didn’t, and if the nation of Switzerland didn’t like it, it could go screw itself.

“The problem with Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma,” she often complained to her new friend in San Luis Obispo, Bob Johnson’s grandmother, Monumental Li, “is that she thinks she has such a tough time in life just because her son plays the cello, but as I keep informing her, there are worse things that can happen to a lady, especially in today’s world economy. For example, her cheese shop might go out of business and force her to leave her beloved Switzerland to find a new life in this terrible placed called San Luis Obispo, where Swiss people are few and far between, and buying a decent jumbo-sized crate of Velveeta is practically impossible. More to the point, whenever that awful son of hers comes through town and gives one of his endless performances telling everybody what a kind and non-confrontational soul he has, I’ve got to sit in the front row just because I’m his Grandma and pretend I give a crap. So what I’m saying, Monumental, is that being Bob Johnson’s grandma may be a pain in the you know what, but you don’t have to attend any of his stupid concerts, do you? So stop complaining and help me finish this pitcher of margaritas. They don’t grow on trees, you know–or, as we say in Neuchatel–the Velveetas don’t cream themselves–unless they’re from Bern! And then they’d just be crazy!”

Monumental Li dreaming

By this point, of course, Monumental Li has fallen asleep into her plate of garlic bread, and begun dreaming one of her sweetest dreams–she is floating through the crisp air over the San Francisco Botanical Gardens with a gigantic can of bug spray and extinguishing every speck of life smaller that her fingernails. The sky is blue. The grass is green. And there’s no sign of her ridiculous grandson anywhere…
