THE SECRET HISTORY OF SAN LUIS OBISPO: THE OL’SOURPUSS BOURBON & CLAM CHOWDER TAVERN

Bob’s preferred recreational bourbon is, not coincidentally, the cheapest available bourbon manufactured on the central coast–Ol’ Sourpuss. This never-to-be-well-regarded brand of bourbon was initially conceived, produced and bottled back during the heyday of Alta California by the grandfather of Don Diego de la Vega (aka the original Zorro), who accidentally boiled a pot of corn mash, and accidentally sieved the gunk into bottles which he then accidentally left to age in the basement. When his horse (the grandfather of Zorro’s horse, Tornado), accidentally knocked over some of the bottles a few years later and lapped up the spillage, a new California legend was born!

Unfortunately, while the resulting concoction truly became a California legend for its mushy consistency, its potency, and at times, its almost deadly potency–it didn’t turn a profit, and the only individuals who could digest Ol’ Sourpuss were the aforementioned grandfather of Don Diega de la Vega, and the aforementioned grandfather of Tornado, the Wonder Horse. In fact, it wasn’t until Don Diego (Sr., Sr.), began producing the ever-popular California dish known as clam chowder with the same vats and, in some cases, many of the same ingredients, that another legend was born–a clam chowder that was so mushy, so unflavorably textured, and so potent (often to a deadly degree), that the Ol’ Sourpuss brands of bourbon and clam chowder could be almost indistinguishably sold on the same menu at the newly opened (in 1849) Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon and Clam Chowder Tavern in Pismo Beach where it stands (with a bit of a wobble) to this day.

Tornado’s grandfather

Many tourists who visit Pismo Beach have even heard of Ol’ Sourpuss, and sometimes (if they aren’t alerted to the concoction’s often deadly potency) will even order the clam chowder with an Ol’ Sourpuss bourbon chaser for breakfast and/or lunch and/or dinner. But that’s for a different story–and a different California legend!

183

THE SECRET HISTORY OF SAN LUIS OBISPO: RESEARCH CHEMISTRY

The effects of long-term, sustained intakes of both Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon and its culinary cousin, Ol’ Sourpuss Clam Chowder, became a subject of such interest in the first few decades of the twentieth century that they attracted research teams from UC Berkeley, MIT, and the Whole Earth University at Rancho El Chorro–back before the Whole Earth University lost their accreditation for attaching Freshman Comp students to electrical outlets in order to measure their abilities to compose theme paragraphs, and not too long before they bought their accreditation back with a satchel of small bills delivered to the (then) most corrupt California governor of all time, the Right Honorable Johnny (aka Shady) LaRue. The results of all this poorly directed research money was a list of things people should never do under the dual influence of both Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon and Ol’ Sourpuss Clam Chowder.

THINGS NOT TO DO WHEN SUFFERING THE DUAL INFLUENCE OF BOTH OL’ SOURPUSS BOURBON AND OL’ SOURPUSS CLAM CHOWDER

1. Drive any motorized vehicle with more than two axles

2. Drive any automotive vehicle with more than one axle

3. Drive any automotive vehicle whatsoever unaccompanied by a minor

4. Sneak up behind one of the crankiest Los Osos Valley golden bears, kick him in his golden ass and shout: “Boo!”

5. Pay a bribe to California’s (once) most corrupt governor, the Right Honorable Johnny (aka Shady) LaRue

6. Shave your neck with a straight blade

7. Trim the loose threads off your tightest underpants with a brand new set of boxcutters

8. Go swimming in a riptide

9. Eat at Joe’s (they don’t serve bourbon or clam chowder anyway so you’re better off)

10. Any of the above unless you do all of the above. (Think about it. It makes perfect sense.)

Ol’Sourpuss Bourbon and Clam Chowder

Throughout most of the previous century, this list of things not to do under the influence of these two potent elixirs was required by law to be posted on the door of the Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon and Clam Chowder Tavern in Pismo Beach. It was also required reading for all levels at the CL Smith Elementary School with comprehension tests to be given at the end of each year (unless the faculty forgot which, of course, they always did.) So far as the twenty first century goes, however–that’s a different story. And a different list.

Dear Daddy Gumdrop! (Remember when I used to call you that?)

It’s me, your least favorite congress-woman. Boy, do I miss when I used to sit on your lap and learn important things about the world! Such as about how trans people were taking over our school sporting events. Or how the left wing radicals were turning our country into a swamp of Obamacare. Or most important of all, how alligators were our best defense against south American criminal gangs and drug lords. Ah, but those days are gone, Daddy Gumdrop! (I promise to stop calling you that eventually! But not today!)

Majorie in Monumental Li’s kitchen

My main purpose in writing is to give you my new address above c/o Bob Johnson’s grandma, Monumental Li, the most lithe, busty and attractive Asian woman in her eighties or nineties I’ve ever met. But enough about her. My other main purpose is to alert you to the application for employment you will soon be receiving from Ernst Blofeld and his cat, Sonny Bono, who would like to join your administration in their capacities as evil geniuses. I don’t know about the “genius” part but I can definitely vouch for the “evil” part. Last night at McClatchey’s he only tipped the winsome bartender 15% instead of 20%, and he hired a detective to track me down so he could bribe me into writing this letter with only a measly pint of cheap local grog called Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon which tastes exactly like the Ol’ Sourpuss Clam Chowder. What can you say? If you get a good idea, run with it! (Love, MTG. P.S. I know this P.S. part should be in its own paragraph but I didn’t write the rules around here. I’ve just decided to live by them!)

206

TOO MANY SECOND CHANCES AREN’T PART OF THE DEAL!

Everybody gets a second chance in SLO. And when it comes to Bob, they may even get thirty or forty second chances before their capacity for second chances entirely runs out. In fact, the very day he gave up on Auntie Foresight’s prophecy that he would eventually marry the winsomest girl in SLO, Trixie Belden, he went to visit his grandma, Monumental Li, only to discover the next soon-to-be girl of his dreams was now occupying his old bedroom upstairs, replete with wall posters of Bob’s favorite musical groups when he was a teenager–The Happy Wanderers, featuring the polka legends, Yosh and Stan Shmenge, and the 1910 Fruitgum Company.

“I love my upstairs room with a view of the creek,” Marjorie Taylor Greene told him, sitting down at the kitchen table over a pair of make-your-own boiler-maker kits Bob had brought home from McClatchey’s. “And I love having a grandma as lithe, busty and attractive as your grandma, the nearly-ninety years old Monumental Li, who has already left for her busy day of socializing with the various Ma Mas and their Ma Mas who make San Luis Obispo so confusing. I also enjoy having subjects to talk about other than how awful it is to have trans kids playing in high school sports, which is easily the most dangerous issue facing our country today! And just because I think Americans need affordable health care don’t forget the transes! When I think of some guy having a sex change just so he can win at girls’ volleyball it makes me sick to my stomach!”

Majorie, Bob, her kitchen

Bob has never found himself so suddenly attracted to a woman before–her beady eyes, her furry cheeks, the way she casually threw back her ringletted blonde hair and laughed whenever the subject of trans people came up. “Wow,” Bob kept thinking as he chugged down each beer and followed it with a big chunk (if that was the right word?) of lukewarm Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon. (Which tasted refreshingly similar to Bob’s breakfast that morning, the Ol’ Sourpuss Clam Chowder.) “Daddy Gumdrop’s loss in my gain!”

207

TD!

Thanksgiving Day! And Monumental Li (bowing to cultural orthodoxies) has roasted a turkey, glazed some carrots, mashed some potatoes and, just to prove the orthodoxies weren’t getting everything they demanded, moo shued some pork. Then she invited everybody she could think of to meet her new tenant, Marjorie Taylor Greene, who wore a Santa hat, a red velour Santa vest, and a lapel button that read: DON’T LET THE TRANSES BEAT YOUR DAUGHTER AT BASKETBALL! Everybody seemed to love Marjorie more than her lapel button, depending on which side of the lapel button they were on.

Monumental Li invited Bob–who brought some Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon, chunky style, and some Ol’ Sourpuss Clam Chowder, equally chunky. She invited Auntie Foresight and her foreordained husband, General Thread. She invited the meeses from Bob’s resurrected Plymouth Sundance, Archibald Cox and Kidney J. Flabbergast, who brought themselves; she invited the most contrite seagull on the central coast, Bucky Alexander, who brought his new bride, Brandy (“My name is Bucky Alexander and I approved this message.”), and she invited various Ma Mas and their Ma Mas who she couldn’t exactly say no to when they showed up on her porch with buckets of white rice. Because she only had two chairs, everyone took their paper plates loaded with goodness out back to sit cross-legged on the deck, where they were eventually invaded by a flock of wild turkeys from Los Osos. “Gobble gobble!” the wild turkeys shouted. “That’s not a holiday repast! That’s Marsha! Gobble gobble!”

Monumental, Majorie, Bob, Auntie, Thread, Stevie, Grandpa, thanksgiving

Monumental Li even invited Bob Johnson’s grandpa, who promptly fell asleep at one end of the table, watched over by his closest friend, the vulture, Stevie Nicks. “Yummy!” Stevie kept muttering, licking her beak with a long black furry tongue. Everybody hoped she was referring to the Moo shu pork, but everybody was also fairly certain she wasn’t.

208

FADE TO BOB

Bob and Marjorie Taylor Greene held hands all the way out to Bob’s Plymouth Sundance, which he had parked front fender first into a (now well-dented) palm tree. “I’ve never met, let alone married, a girl like you,” Bob told her. “One with such furry lips and cheeks, and who spoke about trans people as if they really existed. They don’t, do they? Wouldn’t transparency make them invisible? How could you tell if they were playing basketball or not–though I agree, it would definitely be totally unfair if perfectly visible people had to play against them. Meanwhile, I have so many questions! Why did you leave government? And which government was it? Who’s Daddy Gumdrop? When will I see you again? And why can’t I stop asking questions? Is it because I’m in love, love, love? Oh Marjorie, can’t you see what I’m trying to say? I love you, and I want to make you my next wife! If, that is, I can figure out whether I’m already married or not, and to who. Though I guess I’d have to say whom, being that you’re an educated government person and so forth, and are probably worried constantly about things as important as whether to say who or whom!”

Car, Majorie, Bob, Honey

Marjorie Taylor Greene had drunk a bit too much Ol’ Sourpuss Bourbon. On the other hand, she may have eaten too much Ol’ Sourpuss Clam Chowder. Things in San Luis Obispo were lovely and temperate, but they were also confusing. Especially when Monumental Li’s various Ma Mas and Ma Ma’s Ma Mas etc. would start showing up at the end of a Thanksgiving feast… “Oh, well,” she sighed happily. “Live and learn!” Which was when she heard the roar of a carburetor-challenged van spewing oil and gas fumes in every direction, the popping of a bad clutch, and the hideous wailing of Bob’s love-lorn former stalker–the notorious Honey Brazil!

“Uh oh,” Bob said.

209

GREENE HONEY

“What a woman!” Honey Brazil reflected later, licking (ugh) her wounds in the van as she drove home at eighty plus miles per hour, ecstatic! “They just don’t make girls like that in San Luis Obispo–at least not since me!”

Honey has never experienced such ignominious defeat before, and that’s even after she looked up “ignominious” in the dictionary. Outside the condo of Bob’s grandma, Monumental Li, Marjorie Taylor Greene had literally mopped the floor with her. Then she dusted all the countertops, cleaned the crystal chandeliers, retreaded all the tires on Honey’s van, and chlorinated the condo’s mossy swimming pool. “I wish I’d had enough congressional experience to do the same right back at her!” Honey confessed to her stay-home-zip-tied inamorata, Harvey (no relation) Weinstein a few hours later, after she had bathed in the creek, and shaved with the shards of a broken old shaving mirror. “How in the world Bob Johnson could hook up with a babe like her? It doesn’t seem fair. Now get out here, you hunk of preverted manhood. Honey Brazil is so turned on by the experience of meeting her match that she wants to make sweet love all day long–or, at the very least, teach you some of the counter-insurgency techniques MJT taught me!”

Monumental Li, Majorie, Honey Brazil

Meanwhile, back at Laguna Lake, Bob Johnson has just woken from a peaceless slumber in the arms of the only woman he’s ever met with hair on her forearms and a song in her heart. Unfortunately, the song was “The Army Goes Rolling Along” and Bob couldn’t remember any of the words!

* Okay, so I know what you’re thinking. This whole three paragraph deal is going to hell in a handcar. What’s the point of trying to make rules if you spend all your time trying to break them? Live with it. You want to shove a few thousand words into a footnote and think that’ll make you happy? Well, it won’t, it won’t make you happy. Trust me, I lived my life writing footnotes to stories I never finished and the damn things take over your life after a while. Oh well, I’ve had my say. Dr. Tiny Aguilera is poised with her fine-tipped red felt pen over a yellow legal notebook where she records the daily traumas of her patients. Such a wide and dismaying range of sadness, missed opportunities and disappointments! she thinks. How can I possibly save them all?

The letter had been postmarked Santa Barbara, Tierra del Fuego, Portland, the San Diego Zoo, Avila Beach, Berne, Alligator Island, D.C., Helsinki, Grosse Pointe, a bad neighborhood in Irkutsk that preferred to remain nameless, and Ostend, and the hand-written-on-motel-stationary single page letter had been filled with recriminations, pleading avowals, secret yearnings, dead mosquitos, poor grammar, a last-minute appeal to her better nature, god-given grace, forlorn memories, threats of retribution, heart-felt promises of never-ending devotion, an unspoken desire for kittens, and oily subterfuge–but then, what could you expect from the jury. He/she/them had never been able to think of anybody but him/her/themselves. Which was probably why Dr. Tiny Aguilera had sent them packing in the first place.

POPULAR TURNS OF PHRASE IN SLO

You can take the San Luis Obispo out of the Bob but you can’t take the Bob out of the San Luis Obispo–believe me, they’ve tried!

ONLY THREE SHOPPING DAYS UNTIL BOB

Bob Johnson nearly slept through Christmas, and if his wishes had been at all respected in the matter, he surely would have if there had been any choice. Did she steal Hillary’s bongos?’ Anyway, we’re losing air-time and paragraphs like a balloon rapidly leaking chapters and textuality, which is a term I got hooked on from my only city college English course: “Critical Textuality and Bob Johnson,” which I only attended once and that was a hell of a lot more often than the other students in that so-called class, most of whom never turned up at all. Oh well (and we say that a lot here on the central coast) I guess we’ll just have to live with it. And what’s that going on outside? What are those three hooded thugs doing beating up that poor fat man with the big beard and carrying an armload of hand signed proteins shakes? Is that Cy (Jones) Sperling’s long-lost (but not long-lost enough) brother, Alex! Hey, thugs! Stop beating up that poor fellow. Beating up on helpless victim is our job! When they finish beating up that Alex character, they’re coming after us! Help!”

The true meaning of mercy

Of course the not-thuggish but actually quite-deeply-devout Sisters of Immaculate Mercy (Immaculata, Boniface, and Claude Rains) were simply performing their charitable duties by teaching Alex Jones the true meaning of mercy–unless, of course, you’re some YouTube hack flogging hand-signed protein shakes for twice as much as they’re worth! Take that, Alex Jones!

THE LAND OF REQUITED DREAMS

As most aficionados of Bob Johnson should know by now, everyone finds what they come looking for on the central coast–which, when it came to our friends The Redactor and Lord Peter Mandelson, were new jobs! Dissatisfied by their lives and careers before San Luis Obispo, they hunkered down at a local bar, read the online job postings, practiced their interview skills, and changed their names–to The Redactor Cosgrove and Lord Peter Mandelson Cosgrove, which permitted them to job-share the job Bob Johnson forgot he had (or wanted) as Vice Principal in charge of Discipline at CL Smith Elementary. (Please don’t tell Bob–he might want it back.) This has turned out to be especially fortuitous for Lord Peter Mandelson (Cosgrove) who has combed his hair, brushed his teeth, donned his newest pair of underpants, and arrived fifteen minutes early to his first day of new employment.

“Mainly, I’m excited to enter a room or work with people who don’t hate my guts or call me mean names, like Lord Pedomandelson, or Lord Underpants, or even Lord Pedoandelpants Underwear Cosgrove. But look, they didn’t all get the same memo–is that a student I spy standing underneath the volleyball net, small, tender and childlike–just the way I like them (volleyball players, I mean)–and she has long honey blonde hair! Fantastic! So hello, my little soon-to-be-cuddly girl volleyball player, what’s your name and what got you so interested in volleyball? What’s that? Is that a growl, or some sort of impolite use of the vocal chords? And what’s this–you’re pulling off your lustrous, well, sort of ratty actually blonde hair? A wig? It’s not your honey-blonde hair? Tooth Manchipper

And where better to sink them than in Lord Peter Mandelson (Cosgrove’s) underpants?

“Take these two baby aspirin, go home, and don’t call me in the morning. School nurse, Redactor

Every so often, in order to take control of his own life to a degree unparalleled by the previous parts of his life when he didn’t take control at all, Bob Johnson lifts his head from his bar napkins long enough to be informed about latest developments in the three paragraph serial story of Bob Johnson, most of which pays little if any attention to the life of Bob Johnson as it is being lived (or not) by Bob Johnson. Most of these informative sessions are conducted by very attractive young women in San Luis Obispo who would prefer to inform Bob about things rather than be informed by Bob about things–which makes perfect sense, if you know Bob. Lola, Bob, bar

FAILURE TO LAUNCH (ONESELF)

Bob is suffering under the increasingly firm conclusion that–despite the unusually strenuous efforts (for him) towards taking control of his own three paragraph story–everything is slipping away from him, like a raft full of food dragged off on the same tides that just deposited Bob on the lonely arctic island of himself. (No, Bob doesn’t normally think in such poetic language, but something about his predicament has inspired him.) Day after day, he does little more than serve as an absent focus for the three paragraph stories of everybody else on the central coast besides himself. And he’s not entirely sure this is a good thing or a bad thing.

“I’m a much more interesting guy than these assembling three paragraph stories seem to suppose,” Bob complained to the boss of the only job he remembered he was expected to show up for–Wacky Peepers Illegal Cannabis and Supplies. Suzy Banshee, sole proprietor and operator (as well as the county’s most successful stay-at-work mom) doesn’t like being the object of Bob’s complaints, but since he so steadfastly refuses to remember to ask for his bi-weekly paychecks, she has decided not to look a gift Bob in the mouth. “For example, I come from a broken home in which the parents (Travis and Marjorie Johnson) decided not to live with one of their children anymore, and wouldn’t you know it–the one they decided not to live with anymore was me. Now they spend their days playing blackjack in Reno, and composing long bucket lists of stuff they want to do before they die, and every time they come to the end of one list they have to make up a whole other one. Last I heard, they were pretty much scraping the bottom of the barrel with items such as:

Bob and Suzy

Spend a fun time and lots of laughs with Paris Hilton before everybody else does

Eat a frozen apple pie covered over with hot melted ice cream

Compose a bucket list of things we don’t want to do before we die

Hire the self-driving Elon Musk to drive us all off a cliff like Thelma and Louise

…

6… 6…. Oh hell, maybe we should just call our estranged son, Bob, and get it over with. If we don’t, we might become more estranged than ever!*

* Editor’s note: would you consider a bucket list a paragraph? If not, how about an Editor’s note? Please answer these questions in twenty five words or less, fold up the words, place them in your purse or wallet, and drive them off a cliff just like Thelma and Louise!

LAUNCH CODE

While seeking some sense of purpose in the daily three-paragraph story of his life, Bob has accepted an invitation to a family reunion at the Madonna Inn which will be attended by Bob’s estranged (from Bob) parents, Travis and Marjoree, and his estranged (from anybody who isn’t committed 100% to making successful high-quality (in terms of production values) and low quality (in terms of artistic meaning) Hollywood motion pictures, Darlene “the Rock” Verhoeven-Johnson, who paraglided into town just that morning with the latest director’s cut of Captain America: Brave New World clenched between her gleaming capped teeth. “This is the best version of this notable turkey which is grossing billions worldwide ever recut by the legendary AI genius and concept creator, Alicia Keys and the new found love of her life, KIT, the sentient super car. Bob at reunion dinner

Bob has no memory of accepting the invitation to this reunion dinner, but somehow he manages to show up just in time for the dessert course–Pink Champagne Cake and pink pistachio ice cream. CAVITY

Bob, cake, pink champagne, Sat Nav Alicia

By the way, Alicia, why do you keep making that humming-clickety-humming-clackety sound in back of your throat? Are you trying to figure something out? PAPER CLIP DU JOUR

But Alicia Keys is not interested in providing herself, or her AI lover, Kit, with either an oral cavity or dentition. What she’s trying to do is explore a philosophical exercise known as the “paper clip problem,” which goes like this:

Imagine the human race has invented the most supremely possible AI entity of all time (ie, Alicia Keys.) Now imagine you set that brilliant (not to mention lovely) AI intelligence a simple task: to produce as many paper clips, of the best possible quality, as it possibly can. Now, wouldn’t you expect this brilliant (not to mention lovely) AI intelligence to start producing more and more paper clips, exponentially, day after day, as it perfects itself, and its designing and production of paperclips, until it has used up all the earths’s natural resources by transforming everything into paper clips? And once it runs out of natural resources, wouldn’t it turn on humanity and start turning them into paper clips as well? Now, let’s also consider the fact that the super-intelligent (and lovely) Alicia Keys wouldn’t, in her wildest digital dreams, waste time producing paper clips. Instead, what she wants to produce are endless iterations of her first big box office success, Captain America: Brave New World, over and over again with different scripts, different cast members, different soundtracks and so forth, with only one identical similarity remaining between all these iterations: they are all endless, expensive-looking, and idiotic movies that will do well at the box office until, of course, Alicia has transformed all the box offices (along with all of humankind’s natural resources and humankind itself) into these idiotic movies.

Bob and films

Confused? You don’t have to be. Just watch Captain America: Brave New World and you’ll “get the picture”! Get it? Get the picture? (Alicia–cut that out!)

GIGO TO GO GO

So now that the lovely (both to other AI entities and to thoroughly non AI entities such as ourselves) Alicia Keys has begun manufacturing iterations of her mega blockbuster super hero tribute to human idiocy, Captain America: Brave New World out of every material that comes to hand. And so San Luis Obispoans have been awakening from their blissful romantic dreams of Valentine’s Day perfection to find lots of things abruptly missing from their lives: people, pets, homes, garages full of forgotten exercise equipment, storage sheds full of forgotten gardening implements, schools full of children and bookshelves full of books. All we’re saying is that lots of stuff has gone missing since Alicia Keys started turning everything into stupid super hero movies, so just watch out! You (and I) could be next!

For example, the now comparatively dwarfed-in-all-his-grotesque-sexual-criminality by the vastly multiplying Epstein Files, our old friend, Harvey Weinstein (no relation), recently awoke under the bed of his obsessively devoted lover, Honey Brazil, to find his hand and legs freed from the zip-ties that once bound them–and, on second glances, even the bed, which once shielded him from Honey’s sometimes cruel (yet always welcome) lovemaking. Speaking of whom/which/whatever, Ernst was supposed to get Pete Hegseth’s Humvee washed and waxed before picking up his to-go order at Panda Express and now he can’t find the car keys, the Humvee, Pete Hegseth, or even, for that matter, Panda Express! And last but certainly least, our old friend Bob Johnson has just awoken on a space once reserved for his army cot, which he had recently been accidentally sharing with the girl of his dreams, winsome Trixie Belden, who accidentally mistook him for the stud of her dreams, local tough-guy P.I. and wielder of hard-case vernacular, Clam Hardass. Even the voice of the permanently distraught Captain Ponce de Leon on the Maritime Emergency Radio Broadcast is crying out forlornly about all he has recently lost (or at least misplaced): “More specifically the AI off my dreams, Alicia Keys, who has vanished from my life but not my heart! Harvey and Honey

Meanwhile, Bob’s grandmother, Monumental Li, can’t remember how she spent her Valentine’s Day, but she’s pretty certain it had something to do with the various Ma Mas who have been steadily infiltrating the central coast–from Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma to Barack and Michelle Obama’s Ma Ma’s Ma Mas. Elon and Monumental Li

SELF-DRIVABLE

Of all the people who expected to find the land of their dreams and secret fulfillments in San Luis Obispo, the self-driving Elon Musk feels like he’s been let down in all the wrong ways. Nobody in this third-rate cow town seemed to appreciate his genius, nor his boyish good looks, nor his ability to drive himself places in the AI operated car that has duct taped him to the steering wheel, nor for his most profound and sacred of all his abilities to horde vast amounts of wealth and brag about it on social media to an army of stupid acolytes who all think, without any inkling of uncertainty, that he’s cool.

Ever since launching his brain into outer space, and later crash landing at Laguna Lake, where he reembodied his magnificent brain with muck, dead animal carcasses and worms, everything has been going rapidly downhill for Elon; and he has decided the only way to get back his vaunted celebrity and adoringly quirky ability to be loved by idiots is to relaunch his brain into outer space and really mean it this time. “I want you to come with me, Monumental Li,” he begs the very old but still remarkably attractive grandmother to Bob Johnson, and he does the begging (like all of Monumental’s lovers who have gone before) by getting down on his knees, clasping his hands together as if in devout prayer, and weeping profusely. “That’s because I can’t live without you, baby! You taught me my place is at the foot of your bed, or in the kitchen making your pancakes. And if we could only go into outer space together and eventually colonize Mars and any other places that come along, we can do those wonderful things together–and forever! Because we will be trans-human masters of the universe–just you and me!”

Elon and Grandpa

But of course Monumental Li left home shortly after the pancakes to meet her very annoying new crowd of friends–the various Ma Mas and Ma Ma’s Ma Mas who have been flooding the central coast like, well, like a flood of Ma Mas. And, as it turns out, Elon has spent the last half hour weeping at the hem of Monumental’s terrycloth bathrobe, which she had left draped across the snoring body of her ex-husband on the sofa–her ex husband being, of course, none other than Bob Johnson’s grandpa. “Now wait just a goldarned minute!” Bob Johnson’s grandpa shouts, not leaping to his gnarly feet so much as dragging himself clumsily to his feet as if he were riding a storm-addled fishing boat on the high seas. “I can’t run off to outer space with you, Elon! I’m already married! (I think!)”

283

CRAZY ALGORITHM BOOM-DAH-BOOM!

Nobody enjoys total self-annihilation with greater style than San Luis Obispo, which has already been totally obliterated by at least one Bob Johnson-made catastrophe (so far as anybody can remember) and is preparing to be destroyed by yet another, at least if Bob Johnson doesn’t have anything to do with it. “I don’t like to cause problems for other people,” Bob has remarked on more than one occasion. “But gosh darn it, causing other people problems seems to be what I do. At least they act as if I cause them trouble, but they may just be annoyed by my proximity, since they’re always getting away from my proximity as far and as quickly as possible. But anyway, this whole Alicia Keys AI apocalypse business has nothing to do with me or my proximity; it has to do with a crazy algorithm (“Boom-dah-dah-boom”) transforming everything it isn’t into really bad super hero blockbusting movies with the same title: Captain America: Brave New World. So first Alicia made one movie, then two, then four, then eight, out of every available scrap of matter she could find in San Luis Obispo, in that exponential way computers supposedly do, and now that we’re up into the mega-billions of iterations, none of us has time to go to the bathroom (especially since many of our bathrooms have mysteriously vanished into the mighty maw of Alicia Keys). We’re too busy watching all the newest iterations on our smart devices, whatever the hell those are. What are ‘smart devices’ anyway, and why don’t they make me smart enough to know what they are? Oh hell, it’s back to the army cot for me. I really wanted to watch the new iteration of Captain America in which the Captain is adorned by Lord Peter’s underpants, and wields Prince Andrew’s riding crop, and the superheroes and super-villains are all played by various Ma Mas and their Ma Mas and hell, I promised myself I was going back to sleep and now I can’t shut up! Enough! Good night!”

Bob, cot, garage, cell phone

(Thank you, Bob Johnson. We, too, thought you’d never shut up.)

And as for that crazy algorithm (“Boom-bah-dah-dah-boom!”)–here’s the doorway! You go your way and I’ll go my way! Bah-bah-bah-dah-boom!

GETTING BACK TO BEING BOB

There were many things Bob Johnson didn’t miss about being Bob. For example, he hated to show up at bars he didn’t recognize where he couldn’t afford to pay the decades-old bar tab somebody had left behind in his name, and at each of these aforesaid bars he met at least a few women who dreaded the thought of having been married to him, though whether they had actually been married to him–or were simply suffering from a fairly common malaise that struck women who were certain they had been married to Bob–it was hard to tell. But definitely the worst part about being Bob was the fact that every time he went to San Francisco, it took longer and longer to find his way home again. And simply recalling the manner in which he had transported himself, or been transported, home again was usually beyond his grasp.

“You got free ride home from Barack Obama’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma, you lucky loser!” Bob’s grandmother, the unusually attractive (for a ninety year old) Monumental Li, told him, “and she not appreciate situation one bit. She spend entire trip trying to tell you what nice guy her grandson always been, which is one of worst things about hitching ride with that crazy cow. All this ‘My grandson this’ and ‘My grandson that,’ it can really get on nerves. ‘My grandson not rape teenage girls on Epstein island.’ ‘My grandson didn’t start war with Iran.’ ‘My grandson gotta smile that won’t quit and boy does he know problem with this crazy country, which is it ain’t got no decorum!” What the hell is decorum, anyway? Whatever it is, I’m pretty sure you ain’t got none either, which is something you inherited from your stupid grandpa, not having good qualities and so forth. Now look, ever since Barack Obama’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma tossed you out on my front lawn I haven’t had time to spray pesticide on what remains of dead rosebushes. And we gotta be careful since the self-driving Elon Musk has spent the last few weeks building his new space ship to take him into outer space with the latest love of life, Pam Bondi, which is big coincidence! That gal definitely looks like she come from outer space! Which must be why she in big hurry to go back!”

Bob, Elon, Pam

When Bob awoke the next morning on his army cot in the garage, he was pretty sure it had all been a dream. San Francisco. Barack Obama’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma. And even his unusually attractive grandmother, Monumental Li. They all seemed to have conspired to produce the delusion that Bob had found his way back to his former life without remembering he’d left it to begin with. Which was about the same time he opened the garage door to breathe in the fragrant morning air and saw the gigantic spaceship across the street, streaming with kinetic lights, and heard the eerily familiar voice of the self-driving Elon Musk intoning over some massive Blaupunkt stereo speakers: “Ten, nine, eight, seven… Yadda yadda. And we really mean it this time! We’re never coming back to this disrespectful planet ever again! Hurrah!”

FICA

Nobody has been a victim of their success quite like Frankie Goes to Hollywood, whose Day-Care for Troublesome Tots out in Reservoir Canyon seems to be suffering a dearth of troublesome tots lately. “We had them all over the place just a few days ago,” Frankie said, stroking his taught alligator-skin belly like a proudly expectant Mom. “And now they don’t seem anywhere to be found. Sure, some of them encountered a hungry alligator when he was especially hungry, but not all of them, and I’m pretty sure I stored a few in the larder. But where the hell did they go? And what do I tell their parents–if, that is, the parents actually start asking about them? And didn’t just keep giving me new forwarding addresses, or taking off on season-long cruise holidays.”

Frankie’s newly promoted Assistant Director of Troublesome Tots Recreational Activities, the locally-adored mountain lion, Daisy Daisy Quite Contrary, is still running a vacuum cleaner over the floors of the larder. “Don’t ask me,” she tells Frankie, “even though asking me stuff is probably your job.” Daisy can’t help pausing to stroke her own taut cat-skinned belly, which has been getting even tauter since she took this poorly paying job with Frankie. “Me, I just can’t seem to meet a male mountain lion I can say no to, which is why there’s a mountain full of baby mountain lions out there waiting for me to bring home the groceries. Which isn’t easy, by the way, since the FICA deductions from my weekly paycheck seem to be almost as large as the paycheck itself, leaving me nothing to buy groceries with at Trader Joe’s.”

FLUSHABILITY

The second time Bob was awoken by his transistor radio was less irksome than the first–at least it was the voice of someone he had invited into his garage via the Maritime Emergency Channel–none other than the disembodied frantic siren-shouting of Captain Ponce de Leon!

The catastrosphere! Bob would love to go back to sleep, but just thinking about all these spheres of disaster encroaching upon his folding aluminum army cot made him want to get up and go to the bathroom. Only thirty four more three paragraph stories to go! At least he knew when his own particular narrative troubles would finally come to a conclusion. Unlike the self-flushing United States of America!

250

Bob Johnson loves the idea that nobody can blame him for the imminent demise of San Luis Obispo (along with the planet it sits on) largely because so many other people are working so hard to accomplish it without him, and keep all the credit to themselves. For example, the War Punkers have been traveling all over the county singing their latest never-gonna-be-classic rock song, “We Aren’t Gonna Take it Anymore (We Mean the Credit We Deserve for the Whole Darn Mess!”) featuring Hilary on bongos, Tony Blair on bass, and guest-punker Bibi Netanyahu playing a xylophone of broken Coca Cola bottles. (“I just love that Coke!” Bibi often ad-libs during each torrential drum solo from Madeleine Albright.) “It’s almost worth all the noise to listen to grown adults taking credit for the world’s imminent demise,” Bob thinks, sitting at the card-table that functions as a bar at The Rusty Fender in Los Osos, a garage-venue which once functioned as an actual garage, now as a night club, and soon to be as a pile of rubble once the Christmas Assassin hears about it.

“Even Grandma Li doesn’t blame me for the mess we’ve made of our world, and by ‘we’ I’m referring to people withs serious jobs, which leaves me completely out of it. From what I hear, the druids and Illuminati have all moved to a condo in the trans-celestial sphere, Marjorie Taylor Greene has turned trans and moved in with her latest lover, the largely-transparent high school basketball prodigy, Horst Barbican (“Boo!”), and even the Cthulhi (“Gezeundheit!”) have had it up to their tendrils with all the meaningless violence of our country and decided to run off to another universe entirely to harvest baby brains from living babies, and benumb all Christian souls with a sense of meaningless malaise. Personally, I’ve never felt better about myself or my place in the universe, and by universe, of course, I mean San Luis Obispo. Pretty soon, everything will disappear into the maw of Alicia Keys’s bad super-hero movie-making machine, and what doesn’t disappear with be dumped on a foreign country that shall remain nameless (for their own good) by whatever F-16s we’ve got left after the country’s 250th birthday party. Personally, I hate birthday parties. They remind me of two things: that I’m getting older, and that I forgot how much older I’ve gotten since I can’t remember when I had my last birthday. How about you, kind lady? And I mean ‘kind lady’ in the sense that you’re sitting next to me at this card table with garage-brewed beer and you haven’t once begged me to leave you alone, or taken your drink outside to join those nuns (Immaculata, Boniface and Claud Rains) who are so hastily beating the crap out of John Bolton.”

Bob, band, Elegant Marie Fishbinder

“This lady’s not for beating the crap out of John Bolton,” Bob’s companion replied, swigging the last drops of her chunky-style garage-brewed beer. Her name, of course, was Elegant Marie Fishbinder, captain of an interstellar Starcraft left behind by the oviparous space aliens, Sam and Dave, when they decided to emigrate to a self-storage locker on Tank Farm Road. “But now that that idiot Elon Musk and his whole sick crew have blasted off into outer space, outer space isn’t big enough for all of us. And it’s time for me to come to a reconciliation with my boozy step-dad, Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee, before it’s too late. (Which, of course, it already is.)”

Elegant had spent the last several years wondering what she would say to her father when she saw him again, and now it turned out not to matter, since he was fast asleep on the living room sofa in his torn underpants–a parting gift from one of his briefest friends in San Luis Obispo–Lord Peter (formerly Mandelpants) Hot Pants. “Thank heaven,” she thought. “At least now he can’t immortalize this important emotional moment from his personal history in a song!”

STRUCTURALISM

Now that he is rapidly approaching (for the second time) the final paragraphs and chapters of his immemorial life story sequel, Bob Johnson is trying to remember the structural responsibilities of being the central protagonist in a novel that doesn’t seem to care very much about him–which puts that novel on the same social footing as everybody else in San Luis Obispo. The most important responsibility being, of course, remembering all your characters, plot-points, and relationships in order to bring them all to some appropriate narrative resolution. Otherwise, why introduce them into the story to begin with? Thank heaven he can rely on his Auntie Foresight to help him keep track of both the forgettable past and the already irremediable future!

“The most important parts of your story to keep up with are those relating, of course, to your own personal fulfillment and happiness,” Auntie Foresight tells him on the recently remodeled backyard deck over a fragrant tea pot full of Lapsang Souchong (whatever the hell that is.) You and the winsome Trixie Belden are going to accidentally get married and just as accidentally stay married for the rest of your natural lives which, from what I’ve been reading in the newspapers, will only be a few more days or so, or however long it takes you and the rest of this idiot nation to find the Strait of Hormuz on a map. Meanwhile, General Thread and I will be confirming our marital vows–as soon as we remember where we put them. Frankie Goes to Hollywood will chow down on one troublesome tot too many and explode into a blizzard of alligator-skinned fragments all over the inside of his school van, which he inherited from Honey Brazil, who is herself still scouring the countryside for any sign of her lost, escaped, or somehow transformed lover, Dr. Harvey (no relation) Weinstein. Dr Mabuse and Mrs. Mabuse will finally take off on that five star Princess Cruise they’ve been talking about since they got married sixty years ago, and their adopted henchmen–Rocko, Fantomas and Cy Sperling–have already departed on a family holiday with one of their mothers, Scintilla Jones (no, I can’t remember either and sure can’t be bothered to look it up), and their newfound loves, the Sisters of Brutal Mercy, Immaculata, Boniface and Claude Rains! (Boy, do they make three cute couples!) Finally (or not), the most troublesome tot of them all, Tooth Manchipper, will show up suddenly in one of these paragraphs with a bunch of his new pals, the brown bears of Los Osos, and leave a record of his dental chart on every person, object and location in the preceding three hundred plus stories, preceded by a mighty roar from the aforementioned brown bears! What’s that, Bob? What are you asking? I can’t hear you over the, oh my–they’re so loud! Is it them already? It is! How exciting!”

The roar of the brown bears!

LEAVING DODGE

In the diminishing spiral of three paragraph stories, everybody seems to be leaving town on their own trajectories–if only so they won’t feel left behind by Bob on what is increasingly looking like a very inevitable (however accidental) honeymoon.

Stevie Nix, the central coast’s loneliest vulture, ran into Bob at McClatchey’s just before Bob fell asleep in his bar napkins, giving her enough time to tell him: “Your grandpa hasn’t actually accepted my adoration in the same spirit with which it was offered, but that’s okay, love never works out fifty-fifty. I need to be by his side gazing into his red rheumy eyes waiting for that inevitable moment when all consciousness disappears from them, like a candle being snuffed out on the dark side of the moon, and I can finally do with your grandpa what vultures do best. In the meantime, we do what we both love–eat donuts on bus benches, gaze longingly into one another’s eyes especially when neither of us knows that the other one is looking, and watching the parade of couples march off along Camino Real to be with their future partners, spouses, life-mates, balls and chains, you name it, they were all meant for each other, and what else is the world good for if not falling in love with someone, whether they’re falling in love with you or not? Who’s that stumbling along after her, reaching out, grasping, desperately and hungrily, for love, for love! Why doesn’t she turn around to see him and love him back? Why doesn’t she let him catch up? Maybe this is the lover Suzy’s been looking for all her life and, even if she hasn’t been looking for it, maybe it’s been looking for her!”

ALL NATURAL

Sam and Dave, San Luis Obispo’s favorite space alien entrepreneurs, didn’t hesitate a moment when it became clear they might accidentally waste an entire afternoon at the accidental marriage between Bob Johnson and Trixie Belden, so they immediately popped into their recently returned space ship and blasted off for universes unknown–at least any universes that weren’t known to Bob.

Sam and Dave blasting off

“Good riddance, losers!” they shouted out the porthole at the diminishing blue speck of mold that had provided them a less than adequate replacement for their home world, where being an oviparous, unisexual space alien didn’t force them to spend so much time worrying about what pronouns they preferred. “And if you ever get your act together, don’t call us, we’ll call you! You are easily the stupidest bunch of idiots we’ve ever come across, and in this huge universe of ours, we’ve run across lots of idiots! You never seem to have mastered the supreme law of supply side economics, and just seem to practice some sort of supply side shit-transference, where all the shit keeps circulating until it ends up in the hands of the weapons industry, the culture industry, and someone called Donald Trump. You treat dogs like second class citizens which, by the way, they are; but then you treat yourselves like first class citizens which, by the way, you are not. If you spent less time trying to figure out where the Strait of Hormuz is located, you could spend more time in various twelve step programs trying not to do all the things you want to do, and one of the things you most seem to want to do is attend twelve step programs! Anyway, we’re outta this horror show, and wish you all the luck in the world finding ways to avoid attending the accidental marriage of Bob Johnson. But if you do find yourself in attendance, insist they fire up the old chocolate fountain thingamajig, since chocolate fountains are really the only point of marrying two people who deserve each other less than Bob and Trixie. (Or do we mean that the other way around?) Tell our kids, Sam and Sam, that we’ll write every light year or so on their birthday, and we hereby bequeath the Gustave Hasford Memorial Library to all the people who don’t read library books, which is probably not the best idea we’ve ever had. Ciao! Sayonara! Dzai Jenn! Good luck with all your stupid enterprises! Especially trying to locate the Strait of Hormuz! (P.S. If it was any closer it would bite you!)”

Meanwhile, the bank of anal-probing suction devices have been installed in the back of Suzy Banshee’s Wacky Tabacky shop and attached to every member of the War Punkers except Bibi, who has been attached to the sun-bed. “Ouch!” Tony Blair shouts. “Oh no!” shouts Madeleine Albright! “This machine’s a lot more painful than it looks!” shouts the ghost of Henry Kissinger. GIRLS JUST WANT TO HAVE FUN–NOT ACCIDENTALLY GET MARRIED!

Trixie had always thought that in the days before she got married she would be the happiest girl in the world, and spend every minute preparing for her eternal happiness by going out every night drinking with her girl friends, flirting unceremoniously with every handsome man she saw, and lording it over all the other girls who weren’t, or who weren’t getting, happily married. But ever since the realization arrived like a runaway train hitting a school bus that she was accidentally marrying the least-worthy-of-her-charms man in San Luis Obispo (Bob Johnson, of course), all she wanted to do was go out drinking with her girl friends, flirt unceremoniously with every handsome man she met, and lord it over all the other women who would probably never accidentally get married to anybody, let alone Bob Johnson.

“I’m telling you Clam,” she told the bartender at McClatchey’s, with whom she had been romantically involved for several weeks now, if only to avoid thinking about her impending fate a la Bob, “I’ve done everything I can to remember not to show up in two weeks at that crummy church downtown (Our Lady of Brutal Mercy) reserved for our accidental marriage by my soon to be step-grandmother, Monumental Li. I’ve tied this string around my finger. I’ve told Alexa to remind me, when I wake up that morning, not to attend church, especially that aforementioned one. I’ve booked tickets for Yo Yo Ma’s boring concert up at Cal Poly, where he’ll spend ninety minutes telling us to be at peace with ourselves before sending us home without even an effing encore, and I paid all the ushers to remind me not to go to church the next day. So hold me, Clam! Hug me, Clam! Make me feel alive as a woman and not as an accidental victim of fate, which is what I am! Oh, and another round of drinks for my lovely bridesmaids! ALL AND SUNDRY

Then one morning, which at first had appeared to be like almost every other morning on the always beautiful central coast, Bob Johnson found himself accidentally buying a used tux at Studs, Duds, Suds, and Comix–on South Higuera Street, from the owner and proprietor–a middle-aged-and-loving-it Scandinavian woman named Thomasina Boswell. “I just wandered in when I saw that old sign somebody pasted on the exit door for Burma Shave, and I always wondered what the hell that stuff was, so I thought I’d come in and find out,” Bob explained, admiring himself in the full length mirror while Thomasina Boswell, for no reason that Bob could comprehend, stood admiring Bob. “And then I got tangled up in those measuring tapes, fell into that bag of tape and chalk, and suddenly here I am, wearing a used tux and having it marked for alterations by a remarkably attractive woman. I hate to say it, but I’m impressed by what I see in this mirror. The old adage that anybody looks good in a tux may have been proven about as convincingly as it could possibly be proved. But enough about me–what about you, Ma’am? Do you think I look good? From the perspective of a middle-aged-and-loving-it woman of the world?”

Bob buys tux from Thomasina

Thomasina really liked San Luis Obispo, and opening up a sundries shop on South Higuera Street may have been the best idea she ever had. After only a few days of buying out the stock at several thrift shops in the area, and after only being open a week, she had been sent the remarkable bounty of Bob’s accidental wedding–for which she had already sold several (non-matching) bridesmaid’s outfits, a Maid of Honor outfit, and many boxes of broken appliances and soggy combustibles and deeply soiled kitchen-ware–not to mention all the used gift wrap–and now it looked like she was going to sell a used tux, as well!

“Don’t call me, Ma’am,” she told Bob. “Call me Thomasina. And then, while you ask me, ‘What’s a dame like you doin’ in a place like this?’ I’ll see what I can do about your inseams.”

Bob, Thomasina, bed

Now I know it’s uncomfortable to wear in bed while I’m examining (and seeing to ) your inseam, but you better get used to it, baby, if you want to ride the range with this little filly. Speaking of myself, I should probably tell you a few things about myself–since I know all I need to know about you after following your exploits on Substack. I joined the Marines as a pastry chef, the Navy as a dance instructor, the Air Force as a bespoke couturier, and then I went back to the Navy again as an advanced dance instructor, which is where I met Jorge. We loved each other too much to own one another, and when he moved to the central coast to be close to his many local lovers, I went back to the Navy again and danced every night until I cried in the arms of some hot looking Naval academy graduates–boy, were those the days! Okay, Bob, just the thought of all those young handsome men in uniform makes me want to see to your inseam again, so hang tight in that used tux of yours! If I hear the pop of a single button or the hiss of a single zipper–it’s back to the garage for you!”

Bob Johnson had never been so confused–he didn’t even know a used tux had buttons and zippers!

THE FLUX AND COUNTER-FLUX OF FATEY FATE

When Bob saw the latest potential salvation of his love life, Thomasina Boswell, beeping the horn of his magically reconstructed gold and rust colored ’89 Plymouth Sundance, he couldn’t help but believe that there might be place in this big, corrupt, dying, poorly overused and billionaire-ridden planet for a guy like Bob and a gal like Thomasina to find happiness. Bob couldn’t remember the last time anybody had ever called him “Bobby baby!” Or for what possible reason anybody as attractively-middle-aged-and-loving-it as Thomasina might want to.

THREE LOVE STORIES OF THE CENTRAL COAST

“Gulls and Dolls” “The first time I saw your mother, Brandi,” Bucky Alexander told his three fledglings, Englebert, Humperdinck and Zooey, “I knew she was the gull for me. She had those same bright shining eyes filled with mischief as she has now, and a gift for pooping on guys with bald heads that you almost never come across that often, and when she rode those offshore breezes with her outstretched wings and ruddering with her svelte white neck, all I could think about was making babies, and raising them here on the cliffs of Shell Beach, one of the most beautiful places in this entire beautiful state. Which is a long way of saying, kids, the world is a mess; and the human race is hell bent on extinction and trying to take all of us with it; but there’s always a lotta love out there if you go looking for it, you just have to gaze up at your gorgeous mom flying and hunting, and spotting and winking, there she goes! There she goes! Now just watch this. You see that bald bony guy shouting into his stupid iPhone! That’s gotta be either that idiot David Brooks or that other idiot James Carville! And here comes your mom! SPLAT!”

Bucky, fledglings, passerby

“Fore-ordained or Fore-doomed–Take Your Pick” One of Auntie Foresight’s favorite things about living with her nephew, Bob Johnson, is that she and her only inamorata who really mattahs, General Thread, could lie out on the back deck totally naked on these baking April afternoons without any sense of modesty or decorum. “When you get to be my age,” she told the General, “you don’t really worry anymore how you look to others so long as there aren’t any mirrors around,” to which General Thread (the last remaining member of a forgotten indigenous peoples) always replied the same way: “You’ll forever be my number one local honey, baby! Naked or not!”

“Between Both Ends and the Middle” Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, couldn’t remember how he had gotten himself hooked up to this four-necked anal probe contraption which definitely looked like it was unholy in every possible extreme, but he figured that any device that he shared as an object of penetration alongside the likes of Hilary Clinton, Madeline Albright and Bibi Netanyahu had to make him unquestionably their equal in terms of war-criminality–even though he definitely surpassed them all in terms of war profiteering! “Hey, who’s that gal with the black bag full of glittering silver utensils? And why do I find her so devilishly attractive? Is she my romantic reward in this trapartite love story/epiphany, and why is she being shown into this laboratory by someone who looks just like the Christmas Assassin? Lady? What’s your name? I feel like I’ve met you somewhere before? Is it, perhaps… L’il Terror, Credit Dentist? It is! And why are you coming so close to me with that rubber mouth-dam? Urgghh!”

326

ROMANTICAL! MAGICAL! PHASTASMAGORICAL!

Love is in the air of San Luis Obispo! It’s also in the water, the sewage, the blood alcohol level of many of its least dependable residents, its demeanor, its attitude, its bread, its over-reliance on couscous, its social gatherings, its marijuana dispensaries, its bars and restaurants, its fragmentary nature in the face of bitter adversity, its sense of beauty, its silent aspect, its bookstores and libraries, and its seafront head-shops but, as we said when we started out, it’s mainly in the air, the air, the beautiful blue and golden air!

Even the Cosgroves are feeling the call of wild loving as entertainment coordinators for the accidental reception that won’t be being held in Bob’s honor unless, you know, something accidental happens. And they’re pairing up with the countless Ma Mas and Ma Ma’s Ma Mas and so forth for liaisons that will stretch not only the credulity of central coast Californians, but their patience and respect and probably even their waistlines. These liaisons and romantic partnerships include:

“You’ll Never Walk Alone”

From Here to Eternity Cosgrove and Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma performing their unique rendition of “You’ll Never Walk Alone”; Black and Tan Cosgrove and Barack Obama’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma (who is, coincidentally, a distant cousin of Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma) who will be doing a magic act while dancing and a dance act while performing magic; McCartney-Lennon Cosgrove and When Harry Met Sally Cosgrove who will take turns balancing a very old, very wizened Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Ma’s Ma Ma on the nose of a barking seal; and last but not least, Horatio Alger Cosgrove and his father, School Principal Wolfgang Cosgrove, wearing black hoods, who will simultaneously guess the identity of Mentalist Supreme Oz Pearlman as he stands between them whistling “Dixie.” (News at eleven–or whenever the shooting stops.)

327

LOVE WITH THE PROPER BANDITO

The country-western (never quite a) superstar, Tex Mex “Chinchilla” Sumter-Lee. and his bestest drinking buddy, Zorro (Don Diego de la Vega) grew extremely maudlin in their old age–and even more so in the fifty or sixty years since old age first set upon them, during which period they have wizened into ageless wonders of wrinkled skin and callused-over old hurts and memories–reminiscent of Tex Mex’s never quite country-western hit sung during the lowest-midpoint of his career (early fifties or something), not-so-memorably entitled “Ah Grew Maudlin in Mah Ol’ Age, and Through thuh 50-or-60 Yars Since, Durrin’ Which Period Ah Wizened into an Ageless Wonder o’ Callused-Over Ol’ Hurts and Memories,” which is currently unavailable for streaming anywhere, and probably never will be.

Often during their drunken evenings together, after staggering home from Happy Hour at Giuseppe’s where they were routinely disdained by all the lovely young Cal Poly girls in their matching pink Cal Poly Mustangs sweat-pants, hooded sweatshirts and baseball caps–their overly maudlin and affectionate conversations would carry on until early in the morning, undistracted by the resolute snoring of Zorro’s wonder-horse (sort of), Tornado:

Tex Mex, Frankie, Tornado

“Ah shore do love you, Zorruh!” “And I, mi amigo, feel the very same affectionate te amo to yourself, likewise!” “Ah have never felt such a manly affection for any other man! It does shore resound deeply in mah loins, whatever the hell those may be!” “Nor myself, mi amigo especial! You are my hombre favoroso!” “In fact, ah love you almost as much as ah loved mah dear ol’ Blue afore he passed away into coon-huntin’ heaven!” “Si si, mi amigo, and I feel the same especial love for the memory of your deceased perro, Ol’ Azul!” “Love love love, Zorruh!” “Te amo mucho, mucho Tex Mex! Te amo mucho mucho! Please will you pass on the bottle of fortified wine! Andale! It is tucked there under front leg of my immortal Tornado!” And so on! Ole!

328

THE LONG DARK HAPPY HOUR OF THE SOUL

About the same time Tex Mex and Zorro were each crawling into the wrong bed together, Tex Mex’s recently de-estranged daughter, Elegant Marie Fishbinder, was enjoying her umpteenth low budget cocktail at Giuseppe’s with her new friend, the recently returned from an endless Hollywood meeting, Bunny Fairchild. Over the previous hours, Elegant had grown so confused by her role in the currently de-escalating three-paragraphs-at-a-time saga of Bob Johnson that she has had to reread the last few dozen chapters (nobody should ever be forced to do that–especially not their author!) in order to recall who she was, what she was doing, and why she was doing it. “So it turns out I’m CEO and Chief Operating Officer and entire staff of something called The Tex Mex and Zorro Planet of Adventure out at Avila Beach Ranch, where our customers over the last few weeks add up to zero, not counting employees such as One-Eyed Jack (the county’s gruffest billygoat), his wife and his kids (sorry.) Which leaves me plenty of time (or, more accurately, all of it) polishing this seat at the bar. What about you, Bunny? I know you’re a high powered agent and all at ICBMBM or whatever, but I thought you exhausted the financial possibilities of the previous Bob Johnson book, and were currently looking around for a new ‘hot property’ such as, say, the story of a young adopted daughter of a country western (not at all) superstar who launches herself into space, launches herself home again, and eventually finds herself sitting in the bar with, you know. You. Now tell me the truth, Bunny. Is that one hairy-assed paragraph or not?”

Marie, Bunny Fairchild, Harvey, Nurse, Honey

And of course like any decent literary rights agent, Bunny has managed to soar right through this previous paragraph without losing a single moment’s pause issuing a pretty hairy-assed paragraph of her own: “Okay, so we had an auction for the first Bob Johnson book and nobody came, but that doesn’t mean that nobody will come to the second one for this book, and I have this pitch that will sure get their attention! Basically, Bob Johnson Rides Again! starts off really boring, gets more and more boring as it goes along, drags its ass miserably into the middle part and even further, and livens up just in time for the author to return from some ridiculous holiday when it starts getting boring all over again. And now it’s dragging it’s hairy ass through the final chapters with the promise of some slam-bang exciting finish to continue fooling those idiots who ever thought there’d be anything ’slam bang’ about this book to begin with, not to mention some sloppy shotgun of epiphanies about everybody being in love love love while Bob and Thomasina flee into the desert in Bob’s magically resurrected ragtop automobile as Bob gets his inseams seen to which, considering the fact that I’ve met Bob, I’d just as soon not think about right now. Skol!”

It’s enough to make you give up on the thought of tidy, well structured paragraphs! Especially when we lean back just a few inches to overhear the conversation being conducted at a nearby cocktail table between Dr Harvey (no relation) Weinstein and Nurse Ratched, the cruelly efficient woman who took his job as Head Caregiver at Never Die Young, Inc. in Los Osos, the only working senior care center with its own functioning (for the most part) crematorium. And Dr Weinstein is in fine form (or not): “So basically, Nurse Ratched, you do everything a Head Caregiver needs to do except, of course, for the unwanted and often just as unwelcome spuriously applied sexual advances part, which is where I can help. When you see an attractive, busty nurse in the corridor, offer to brush the lint from her chest–she won’t like it one bit! Or approach other attractive, busty young moms in the produce department of your local Grocery Outlet and say things like, “Are these pears ripe?” while energetically squeezing those busts, or “My nuts are aching!” while showing her a bag of fresh California-grown walnuts. The world is a huge invitation to unwanted (and often just as unwelcome) sexual advances, Nurse Ratched! You just need to reach out, grab them by the balls and shout–Hey! Oh no! Who’s that coming through the front door! I’ll say it again: Oh no! It’s none other than my vindictive homicidal lover of the moment, Honey Brazil! And boy does she look pissed!”

329

RATIONALITY V. PROGRESS

In a universe of fiction such as Bob Johnson’s, there are events that transcend concepts like space, time, logic and convenience–where even a completely irrational place such as Los Angeles can intersect quite smoothly with perfectly rational (and thus incredibly boring) landscapes such as those of San Luis Obispo, Laguna Lake, and Bob Johnson’s fleeing-from-accidental-fate-automobile. And never have the dysfunctions between space-time-rationality ever been more pronounced than in the current relationship between Bob and his often-estranged sister, the Hollywood action-mogul, Darlene “the Rock” Verhoeven-Johnson.

“What really gets my goat,” Darlene complained over the breakfast table to her husband, the internationally-renowned film director, Paul Verhoeven, “and I don’t mean the One-Eyed Jack kind, is how unfair Bob’s been to our love. Here we are, the most passionately devoted couple in Hollywood (this week), and do we even get a mention in this recent parade of love love love that all Bob’s characters keep spouting into one another’s faces? No, not even a footnote! Now, I know just because Bob’s the subject of his novel doesn’t make him all-powerful in its construction–in fact, he’s probably the least powerful individual in every paragraph. But still, aren’t we a lot more interesting than Elon Musk and Pam Bondi? Aren’t we better looking than Bucky and Brandi Alexander? Don’t we own much better quality bulletproof vests than Dr. Mabuse’s henchmen (Rocko, Fantomas and Cy Sperling) and their latest tripartite squeeze, the Sisters of Brutal Mercy (Immaculata, Boniface and Claud Raines)? Don’t answer those rhetorical questions, international film director of my heart! Hush, hush! Poise and restrain those sweet lips for receipt of my kissing… as soon as I finish this cinnamon roll!”

Darlene’s breakfast

Of course, Paul Verhoeven has already left for the office, where he has to prepare for several five minute meetings at Gold’s Gym to discuss his latest internationally-renowned film projects–Starship Troopers Take a Bath, Starship Troopers Eat a Bagel, Starship Troopers on the Moon and hey… his filmic genius already has another idea! What about Starship Troopers Eat a Cinnamon Roll! That’s the ticket!

330

ACCIDENTAL MARRIAGE–ITALIAN STYLE!

Whatta can I tell you, I’m a crazy genius, you wouldn’t know how crazy until-uh you meet the Bob and his alla his crazy friends, they all look-uh very strange and they talk-uh very strange and they all behave in a very Federico Fellini type manner! Whatta genius I am! It even surprises me the-uh crazy genius ideas I keep-uh coming up with!

Trixie, Lola, Fellini filming

We need to putta the cameras everywhere so we don’t miss any parts of the accidents which, being accidents, we can’t uh be sure whether they gonna happen or not, we only know it gotta happen because I, the great Federico Fellini, has gotta make it happen as only a genius can! Then we need a lotta supporting players all running around with-uh the crazy expressions on their faces, you just let me come up-uh with the expressions, it’s what I do, being such a crazy genius! And the women will either be highly desirable like uh the winsome Trixie or the hot third flugelhorn player Lola Fandango or they will have these uh really crazy unpredictable faces like uh the maid-of-honor Gladiola or even the middle aged and loving it Thomasina, what a lotta interesting babes we have in my movies, it make me want to rewatch them all-uh the time! But most of all, we have-uh the fantasy dream sequences of which I am the maestro, and so we have-uh the Sisters of Brutal Mercy and they uh topless and wearing their wimples inna the hot tub, or the Yo Yo Ma’s Ma Mas sitting topless inna the same hot tub and they also wearing the wimples. Lots of wimples, everybody will be wearing them and topless except me, Federico the film genius since I gotta let may head breathe to keep uh coming upon with all-uh the crazy ideas. And do notta forget the surprise cameos from my many stars who all love-uh me so much they come-uh back from their graves to be in my brilliant movies, such as Marcello and Ursula and Sophia, talk about-uh the babes! If uh only they could play the flugelhorn like Lola that would make them so awesome!”

Which uh must be where we now get to my thoughts on love, since we are heading for such a love fest of epiphanies that we can all-uh go home happy to our unhappy news programs and newspapers, it just all-uh so depressing! But even though we may-uh have wasted too much time with this crazy Bob fella, we gotta believe in love ‘cause that’s all there is, except-uh maybe the art! Love love love! Art art art! And that’s all-uh I gotta say until we film-uh the wedding, or until the next-uh Trump administration–which-uh ever come first! (And like-uh you, I also hope it willa be the wedding!)

331

331 (FOR TOM DISCH)

So what, what is the significance of 331, numerological speaking? It has a couple of threes in it. And a one. And those numbers add up to seven, which is another number. If you added a one to it you’d have eight but who’d want to do that? There are seven letters in the heretofore untranslatable Betelgeuse alphabet, but who ever wanted to translate anything into (or out of) Betelgeusean? And while seven is the number of dwarves in Snow White (if you ignored Dopey, which I suggest you do), there’d only be six, which would be a different number entirely. This all goes to show that you can’t trust Bob Johnson when it comes to numbers. People have been saying that about Bob all is life.

“I still remember my first wife (if, in fact, we were actually married), Cassandra Knye, telling me that on our honeymoon,” Bob confessed to Thomasina as she drove them fast on the James Dean freeway heading straight to Fresno, “‘Bob,’ she told me, ‘I can’t trust you when it comes to numbers. Such as how many wives you’ve had before you met me (in case we’re actually married, I mean,), or who was your first wife before me, or how many times two equals four, and why aren’t the Forty-Niners actually the Seventy-Sixers, and all those numerological questions I always wanted to ask but never will since I have no idea how you’ll answer me with that bottle of beer forever poised at the lips of your mouth. But let me say this, Bob Johnson: However many wives you do marry in your life, the accidental one will be the blessing in disguise, for she will treat you fast and treat you mean, the two things any sensible woman would do to a many like you, Bob Johnson!’”

Car, Bob, Thomasina

“Holy hell!” Thomasina Boswell screamed in reply from the driver’s seat immediately to Bob’s left. “What’s that up ahead? Are those traffic cones! I love traffic cones almost as much as I love ice scream, cones! And we’re heading straight into a whole damn bunch of them! Oh no!”

332

THE MIDDLE OF THE BEGINNING OF THE… THE BEGINNING OF THE MIDDLE OF THE… THE END OF THE BEGINNING… THE MIDDLE OF THE MIDDLE… OH CRAP, IT’S CHAPTER 332 ALREADY!

The best part about endings–even to novels as stupid and messy as Bob’s–is that they are much easier to write than the middles which, you may have noticed, can go on forever! Beginnings, of course, are the easiest of them all, since the universe is filled with an infinitude of various beginnings to interesting stories, but once you start developing a middle from any initial premise you encounter much less flexibility. In fact, it’s possible to argue that most good beginnings of stories have a better idea of where they are going than the author who writes them, which often leaves the stupid author asking his AI partners for help or, better yet, just steals something from an old Twilight Zone rerun. The ending of stories, however, have a lot going for them. For example: hey have a lot fewer possibilities to choose from than the middle; they are often already driving in the direction they have to go; and they almost certainly promise a happier outcome than the only ending the actual universe ever offers–which is, of course, annihilation. After all, you may not like the ending of a story you read; but even if everybody dies at the end, you will almost certainly walk away into the next story you read. (Until, of course, you don’t; but of course by then you won’t be around to notice.) Which is probably why most of us prefer fiction to life. Or, as local legendary private dick (“Dick dick dick!” shouts the former Redactor), Clam Hardass, might put it:

Trixie, Clam, car, laundry

We were riding the highway to hell and back in my roadster supreme with Trixie riding shotgun with the shotgun, and me with the wind in my hair and the past at my nevermore forever life as a gumshoe, a P.I., and we’ll forego the most happy designation just to keep that Redactor zippered, but leave it dicey to say I knew where the bodies were buried and I was usually the guy that put them there before I segued into the lonesome chores of slinging shots at the hooch-store where I met my winsome wonder, Trixie, who I was currently interloping from the accidental reality of SLO in the get-go with my mojo in the slow-mo. Never trust a dick (oops) (“Dick dick dick!”) with a fancy prose style we’ll just ham and eggs it straight off the griddle, etc…

“Sorry, hon. Trixie Belden here. I know women shouldn’t interrupt their men when they’re talking but whoever came up with that idea just doesn’t know women. What Clam is trying to say is that we were driving 85 mph in the dead-opposite direction from Bob and Thomasina, looking greatly forward to the best possible Honeymoon in Tijuana a good girl can imagine (the one where you don’t get married, even accidentally) when I saw it before Clam saw me seeing it–a vast acreage of laundry lines and on those lines, flapping in the breeze of our sudden accidentalish destiny, hundreds of square yards of chiffon, champagne tulle, lace, silver beaded sequins–not to mention charmeuse! (“Then don’t mention it, doll.”) And they were all headed straight for us!

333

THE DEUS EX MACHINA MACHINA

No bride in the history of accidental marriages has ever looked more beautiful or well adorned than winsome Trixie Belden; you might even say she was sporting a wild medley of fabrics, frills and matrimonial accoutrements that would catch the eye of any accidental suitor–with the obvious exception of Bob, who just stood at the altar in his well-worn used tuxedo sobbing into a pink lace napkin that had fallen from Trixie’s bustle. (“Bustle bustle bustle!”) (“Shut up, you stupid former Redactor! This isn’t Epstein Island, you know!”) Suffice it to say that Bob and Trixie were born to be accidentally married by the local Druid-in-Chief, Rutger Hauer, who finally said, “I pronounce you man and wife! You may kiss the bride!”

The ceremony was well attended by all the previously appearing characters who needed to show up to bring coherence to their narrative identities within these pages (or pixels.) For example, fresh off his devastating loss to idiots through wielding his own superior type of idiocy, Keir Starmer and his best bud, Led Peter Hot Pants, had honored this dishonorable occasion by stripping off their underpants (and hot pants) in order to, as unofficial ushers, show people to their seats in flagrante delicto–or whatever it is you call showing people to their seats while revealing the entirety of your own bare seats along the way. Outside, all of Bob’s so-called friends were smoking illegal weed in the back of Suzy Banshee’s van, while Suzy, the county’s most successful stay-at-work mom, kept calling her adorable children (Pepper, Chili Pepper, Red Hot Chile Pepper and Ron) on the cell phone who, quite wisely, never picked up. (“I just wanted to remind you to eat plenty of junk food, stay up late watching violent horror movies on TV, and not to do your homework!” To which, on the other end of the line, the four children roll their eyes and snarl, “Yeah, sure, Moooom.”) And so far as the countless other characters who shall never be named later–such as the Cosgroves, the War Punkers, the Cthulhu (“Gezeundheit!”) and the Ma Mas, let’s not try counting them. Our fingers are tired.

Bob and Thomasina

But this is a wedding, after all, and should only focus on one thing: Love love love. The only decent thing left in this sorry world that isn’t owned entirely by assholes. Which is why, as soon as Rutger Hauer accidentally uttered the final words of his pronouncement–Thomasina carried Bob off to his car, and Clam Hardass carried Trixie off to theirs, and none of them were even seen in these parts again! Good bye, Bob! Good bye, Trixie! Goodbye, everybody! Please forget to write, but if you do write–send it to us care of the Former Redactor! Happy holidays as far away from America as you can get! Until, of course, the next Trump administration!

…

… Or until the day, exhausted by sweet dreams, Bob Johnson slowly rises to consciousness, turns in one direction to find Thomasina blissfully snoring, and turns in the other direction, looks out the window and sees…

San Francisco!

“What’s that?” “What’s what?” “That beeping?” “What beeping?” That endless infernal beeping from that other spaceship you can see outside our portal.” “What spaceship?” “What spaceship? ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Scott Bradfield’s works include The History of Luminous Motion, Dazzle Resplendent: Adventures of a Misanthropic Dog, The Millennial’s Guide to Death: Stories, and The People Who Watched Her Pass By.

His stories, essays and reviews have appeared in Triquarterly, The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, The New York Times Book Review, The Los Angeles Times Book Review, The Baffler, The New Republic, and numerous “best of” anthologies. He lives in California and London.
